Welcome to Gewu Insight

Gewu Insight is a local workspace for collecting papers, preserving their files and versions, and following journals, subjects, authors, and your own publications.

Windows 1.1.0 · October 28, 2026

Source-available research software. The Gewu Insight Academic and Non-Commercial Research License permits downloading, installing, building, running and modifying the software for academic/non-commercial research. Original and modified versions, derivative works and patches may be shared free of charge for those purposes under the same research-use terms, with retained notices and clearly identified modifications. Public research forks and pull requests within those terms need no separate permission. Commercial use, commercial redistribution, sublicensing and integration into commercial products or services require separate prior written authorization. Copyright © 2026 Lingyuan Kong and Zhengran Wu. All rights reserved except for those express permissions. Read the complete LICENSE, also included with the local distribution and in the application folder, before use. This is not an open-source license.

Why this workspace exists

Research rarely arrives as one clean collection. A paper may first appear in a feed, later acquire an arXiv version and a DOI, be downloaded under several filenames, reappear through an author's profile, and eventually become part of a project or your own publication record. Publisher pages, alerts, PDFs, folders, notes, and citation services each preserve only part of that history.

Gewu Insight is designed to keep those fragments connected. It treats discovery, identity, files, versions, organization, reading state, and provenance as parts of one continuing research process. The aim is not to accumulate the largest possible list. The aim is to preserve enough context that a useful paper remains understandable and usable months or years after it was first found.

Why the name 格物洞见

The name draws on the Chinese idea of 格物致知 and expresses a way of doing research shaped by physics: begin with real-world phenomena and experimental observations, and seek to understand what lies behind them.

Gewu Insight keeps papers, versions, supporting files, and research notes connected so you can return to experimental results, compare physical pictures, and pursue emerging ideas. Read the full explanation in Visual Identity and Cultural Elements.

Investigate nature through experimental phenomena; seek insight through physical pictures and intuition.（从实验现象中格物，以物理图像和直觉求洞见。）

Five design commitments

Local ownershipYour live database and managed research files remain in your selected local Gewu Database folder, separate from the App. Online services contribute evidence; they do not own the workspace.
Visible evidencePDFs and attachments remain real files that File Explorer, Preview, and other applications can inspect.
Continuity over timeA preprint, later DOI, publication version, annotations, and personal contexts can accumulate around one persistent paper object.
Explicit state and provenanceCompleted, empty, partial, failed, downloaded, imported, and retried are different states. Sources and operational outcomes should remain visible.
Researcher controlAutomation assists discovery and maintenance, but classification, interpretation, organization, and scientific judgment remain yours.
Local-first does not mean offline-onlyThe durable workspace is local, while supported discovery, metadata, profile, and download features may require network access and remain subject to source, publisher, and institutional availability. Verify uncertain matches and versions; the app does not bypass access controls.

Windows desktop edition

This manual describes Gewu Insight 1.1.0 for Windows. Install the versioned Setup.exe, then open Gewu Insight from the Start menu. The installer includes Python, .NET and application dependencies. It reuses Microsoft WebView2 or installs it from Microsoft when needed.

Requires 64-bit Windows 10 version 1607 (build 14393) or later, including 1803, or Windows 11. The x64 package does not support 32-bit Windows or Windows 10 on ARM.

The six workspaces share the same paper identities, file classifications and SQLite records. Windows supplies File Explorer, file associations, Recycle Bin, a built-in PDF reader and a WebView2 Browser. Apple Passwords/AutoFill, Safari source sync and macOS system Quick Look are not Windows features.

Your research files and SQLite records live in the selected Gewu Database, independently of the installed program and any development checkout. The default for a new database is %USERPROFILE%\Gewu Database; an existing database may be elsewhere. Use File > Open Gewu Database to locate the actual folder.

The startup selection is recorded in %USERPROFILE%\.gewu-insight\database-location.ini. SQLite owns the database identity and research state; the locator only remembers which database to open.

The default program folder is %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Gewu Insight. Existing installation and Library selections take precedence. Updating the program does not move your Library; uninstalling retains research data.

What this guide covers

This guide follows the work you do in the app: put papers into the Library, organize them, manage publication versions and attachments, review new literature, and keep the database and files safe. It describes the current interface rather than the history of the project.

What Gewu Insight is—and is not

It isIt is not only
A local research workspace that connects discovery, identity, files, versions, organization, and durable state.An RSS reader that forgets a result after it leaves the feed.
A visible file and resource system built around persistent paper identities.A PDF folder whose filenames must carry every piece of meaning.
A personal research memory shared by Library, Spaces, publications, and monitors.Five unrelated tools that happen to occupy the same window.
A system that records evidence and assists repeatable work.A black-box ranking or summary engine that replaces scientific judgment.

Six main tabs

  • Library — your managed papers, folders, spaces, versions, and related files.
  • My Publications — your publication list, citation metrics, author roles, and export tools.
  • Journal Monitor — papers published on a selected date, organized by journal and field.
  • Subject Monitor — topic-based discovery from supported online sources and feeds.
  • Author Monitor — monitored researchers, profile-linked discovery, and newly found work.
  • Browser — Google search, websites, online PDFs, hierarchical bookmarks, and local browsing history.

One continuous research loop

Important SQLite is the source of truth for Gewu Insight. Do not replace, rebuild, or edit the database by hand. Use the app to move, classify, or delete managed items.

Choose a path through this guide

This is one comprehensive manual with three complementary reading paths. The operational path explains how to use the app; the concept and architecture path explains why the workspace is organized this way; and the technical reference path documents storage, database, network, migration, and troubleshooting details. They remain together so visible behavior, product principles, and implementation constraints do not drift apart.

Take a Guided Tour

The top chooses a work mode; the panes move from context on the left to the active object and its evidence; the bottom preserves navigation and progress without reshaping the workspace.

Read the interface as a sentence

Gewu Insight uses a consistent left-to-right grammar. The exact number of panes changes with the task, but their meaning remains stable: choose a research context, narrow it to an object, inspect its evidence, then act. This lets a dense workspace remain predictable without hiding the underlying files and relationships.

The Library window

1. Source tabsLibrary, shortcuts, and independent Spaces.
2. Folder columnsMove from broad folders to the selected item.
3. Item columnPapers, files, and child folders in the current location.
4. Paper FilesOne flat list of resources with independent type, annotation, source, and Default status.
5. DetailsMetadata, identifiers, actions, citations, and folder membership.

Follow selection from broad to specific

A selected item does not always mean “open this file.” In a folder column, selection establishes the next level of context. In the item column, it identifies the active paper or standalone file. In Paper Files, it identifies one resource inside the active paper bundle. Paper Details then describes the shared work rather than merely repeating the selected filename.

SelectionWhat becomes activeWhat remains shared
A Library folderIts child folders and items.The papers keep their identities, resources, and other placements.
A paper in the item columnIts Paper Files bundle and Paper Details.The same work can still belong to other folders, monitors, or My Publications.
A resource in Paper FilesThat version or attachment for preview, classification, or file action.The parent paper remains the active scholarly object.
A Monitor resultIts discovery evidence, report, and available actions.Adding it to Library reuses the cataloged paper record when identity has been resolved.

Tabs across the top

Click a top tab to change workspaces and focus that tab. Left/Right then switch tabs; Down enters the page. Monitors show calendars, filters and papers. Browser has a Bookmarks/History sidebar beside a native webpage. Progress messages stay in reserved status areas.

The top-right search control expands on hover or focus. Each research workspace retains its query; clear it with ×. Use the Windows title bar to move, maximize or restore the window.

Window movement, snapping and virtual desktops follow your Windows configuration. Start a drag from the native title bar; tabs and search controls have their own actions.

AreaPrimary questionTypical next action
LibraryWhat have I chosen to keep, and how is it organized?Read, classify files, move, copy, attach, or recover.
My PublicationsWhich works are mine, and what authorship or citation context do they carry?Verify roles and metrics, refresh, order, or export.
Journal MonitorWhat appeared in selected journals on a given date?Filter, inspect, download, or add to Library.
Subject MonitorWhat matches a defined scientific topic across supported sources?Review source evidence and preserve useful results.
Author MonitorWhat is new in the work of a researcher I follow?Inspect the author relationship, open the work, or add a Library placement.
BrowserWhat can I find on the web without leaving this workspace?Search Google, read a website or online PDF, save a bookmark, or revisit history.

Watch one paper move through the workspace

Resize a pane

  1. Point to a divider. Move the pointer to the vertical line between two panes.
  2. Drag the divider. Move it left or right until the useful content fits.
  3. Release. The app uses the new working width without changing the underlying files.
NoteThe right-side Paper Details area scrolls independently. A long author list or citation section does not move the Library columns.

Recognize stable and temporary state

Selection, keyboard focus, menus, and scroll position are temporary interface state. Paper identity, placements, resource properties, read state, provenance, and completed operations persist when saved. A breathing progress message means work is active, not that a paper or folder was created.

Keep the active context visibleBefore moving, deleting, or attaching, check the focused pane and selected Paper Details. Similar names can identify different targets: a paper placement, one Paper Files resource, or a standalone file.

Set Up Your First Session

Start with one paper, confirm its identity and context, then inspect or add a local file when the work is file-backed.

Open your Gewu Database first

  1. Install the versioned Setup.exe and open Gewu Insight from the Start menu. Setup selects the program directory and database directory independently. A configured installation remembers its database.
  2. During installation or first-start database setup, choose Use existing Gewu Database for an existing collection. Select the whole folder containing data/paper_monitor.sqlite, not the SQLite file or the inner data folder.
  3. Choose Create new Gewu Database only for a new collection, using a new or empty folder. This is separate from creating a Space in the current Library.
  4. Use File > Open Gewu Database to reveal the active folder. This reveals the current database in File Explorer; it does not switch databases.

If the remembered database is unavailable, reconnect its disk or locate the intended existing folder. Gewu does not silently replace it with an empty database. A populated database moved to a different path also needs its managed file references and Windows shortcuts verified; selecting a copied folder alone is not a migration.

Open your database first

  1. Open Gewu Insight from Applications. A configured installation remembers its database and opens it automatically. Updating the App does not require another Library import.
  2. If Choose Your Gewu Database appears, select the appropriate action. Use Open Existing Database for an existing collection and select its enclosing Gewu Database folder, which contains data/paper_monitor.sqlite. Select the whole folder, not the SQLite file or the inner data folder.
  3. Use Create New Database only to start a new collection. Choose a new folder name at a local location you control, such as ~/Desktop/Gewu Database. The chooser does not replace an existing folder. This is separate from creating a Space inside an existing Library.
  4. Check Gewu Insight > Database Location…. It displays the active research folder; Show in File Explorer reveals it. Keep that folder together when making a backup.

If the remembered database is unavailable, Locate Your Gewu Database offers to open the existing folder or quit. Reconnect its disk or locate the intended folder; the App does not silently create an empty replacement. For an older installation whose data is still inside the source project, follow the one-time migration first. Moving a populated database to a different path needs its file references migrated too.

Choose your starting route

You do not need to prepare a perfect record before beginning. Start from the strongest evidence you already have, then let the paper object become richer over time.

You already haveStart hereWhat Gewu Insight does first
A local PDF or another research fileDrag it into the target Library folder, or use the folder's add command.Preserves a visible file, creates a catalog record, and attempts to extract or resolve identity evidence.
A DOI, arXiv identifier, supported URL, or titleChoose Add Paper in the target folder and enter the evidence.Creates or reuses the metadata record. Download or attach a PDF separately when needed.
A useful result in Journal, Subject, or Author MonitorSelect the result and choose Add to Library.Adds a Library placement for the cataloged paper while retaining its discovery provenance.
External originals stay separateFolder Loader and ordinary file import are designed to preserve the external source rather than silently reorganize it. The managed copy and the source path can both remain part of the provenance.

Add and inspect a paper

  1. Open Library. Select an existing folder, or create one from the context menu.
  2. Add a paper. Drag a PDF into the folder, or open the target folder, Right-click blank space in its contents, choose Add Paper, and enter a DOI, arXiv identifier, supported URL, or title.
  3. Select the new item. Paper Details appears at the right. Gewu Insight attempts to identify the work. A local file is recorded only when you imported one or a supported download succeeded.
  4. Check DOI and arXiv. Edit either identifier and press Return. Wait for the green Identifier updated or Identifier saved message, then use Refresh Info to retrieve metadata.
  5. Inspect the available evidence. If a local PDF exists, choose Open in Default App, or enter Paper Files and press Space for Preview. If no file exists yet, use Open Website or download a supported version when one is available.

The paper now has a cataloged paper record, a stable Gewu Key, and a Library placement. A cataloged paper may have no local file; that state is valid. A file resource exists only after a file is imported, downloaded, or attached. An independent non-PDF file instead uses an internal storage key without a public Gewu Key in Paper Details.

Understand what may now exist

Verify the identity before enriching it

  1. Compare the title and authors with the PDF. A similar title is useful evidence but not sufficient proof.
  2. Check the DOI and arXiv fields. A work can have both. Correct an inaccurate identifier before refreshing more metadata or downloading another version.
  3. Read the source and journal information. Confirm that a publication record belongs to this work rather than a cited paper or a similarly named article.
  4. Keep uncertainty visible. It is safer to leave a field empty than to confirm a plausible but wrong identifier.

Complete the first Paper Files bundle

A cataloged-only paper may have no local file, and nothing is missing merely because Paper Files is empty. Continue with these steps after you import, download, or attach a file and the paper becomes file-backed.

  1. Select the paper to show Paper Files. Cards initially show File type and size. Click a card's size footer to show or hide Annotation and Source.
  2. Classify the available file. Use its small type, annotation, and source controls. Do not infer these facts from the filename alone.
  3. Add related material if you have it. Add a supplement, annotated copy, note, presentation, data file, code file, or other attachment. Import first, then classify the resource.
  4. Check the default file. Open in Default App and Library preview use the resolved default when applicable. Selecting Set as Default preserves the resource identity and content. The managed Default becomes the main file, including for non-PDF formats; the other files remain in Associated Files. An automatic fallback is available even before you choose a Default manually.
  5. Reveal one file in File Explorer. Choose Show in File Explorer and confirm the real managed file exists where the database expects it.
Cataloged and organizedThe shared paper record and Library placement are durable even when no local file has been added.
File-backedAfter a file is added, its independent file properties and physical bytes can be inspected separately from paper identity and folder context.

Optional: verify shared identity

Copy the paper to a second Library folder, then select it there. The title, Gewu Key, Paper Files, and metadata should remain the same because the second folder contains another placement for the shared paper—not an unrelated duplicate. Delete only the extra placement when you are finished with the check.

Next useful actions

  • Use Download when a better publication version is available.
  • Use Paper Files to classify imported PDFs or add notes, data, slides, and supplements.
  • Add the paper to another folder without creating a second independent work record.
  • Back up the project before a large import or migration.

Use the collection while writing

  1. Collect a working set. Create a project folder or Space and copy relevant papers into it. Copies share the same Gewu Key and Paper Files.
  2. Check the version you cite. Correct DOI/arXiv if needed, use Refresh Info, and inspect the actual Default PDF. Metadata refresh does not download a publication PDF.
  3. Keep reading notes with the paper. Add your Markdown notes through Add File, or explicitly ask an authorized AI connection to append an analysis. Review the note against the source.
  4. Reuse references. Use Copy Code for BibTeX or Copy Reference where shown. Check names, publication year and version in the resulting manuscript. Export List in My Publications exports your publication list; it is not a general manuscript editor.
  5. Preserve your baseline. Make a closed, complete backup before large maintenance operations. Normal reading and writing do not require repeatedly refreshing the whole Library.

Finish with a safe baseline

Your first session is complete when you can answer two questions for every paper: What is this work, and why is it in this folder? If the paper is file-backed, answer two more: Which file is the default, and where are the real bytes? Paper Details, Paper Files, and File Explorer should answer the applicable questions without contradicting one another.

Identity checkedThe title, authors, DOI, and arXiv evidence do not point to different works.
Placement understoodThe Library folder expresses personal organization, not a second scholarly identity.
Resource classified when presentIf the paper is file-backed, its files can have independent type, annotation, and source descriptions.
File visible when presentIf the paper is file-backed, the expected managed file opens from the app and can be revealed in File Explorer.
Create the backup habit earlyBefore a major import, upgrade, or migration, quit Gewu Insight and back up both the SQLite database and the managed file roots. A database-only copy lacks some bytes; a files-only copy lacks the relationships and state that make the workspace intelligible.

Understand the System

See the System Architecture at a Glance

Gewu Insight is a local research system that coordinates structured state, visible files, and a personal workspace. It is not simply a web page placed in front of a folder.

How the parts cooperate

The desktop window presents the local Python service and SQLite workspace. The Windows shell supplies File Explorer, file associations, Recycle Bin, PDF reading and WebView2 browsing. Network sources contribute metadata and files while the durable workspace stays local.

What each persistent layer answers

Browser is a separate web surface. Its native WebView2 views load websites directly, not through the Python service. The local service stores bookmarks and history in SQLite; WebView2 manages a separate persistent website profile. External pages do not receive the Library's local API bridge. Visiting a page, saving a bookmark, or downloading through Browser does not create a paper or assign a Gewu Key; import the paper explicitly.

LayerQuestions it answersWhat it does not decide alone
SQLiteWhat is this paper? Where is it referenced? Which resources belong to it? What happened in the last operation?It does not contain the bytes of your PDFs and attachments.
FilesystemWhich real files can the native file manager, PDF reader, or another application open?A filename or folder position alone does not define paper identity, version priority, or monitor membership.
Personal Research WorkspaceHow should the shared state be presented for discovery, reading, organization, and action?It is a projection of saved state, not a separate copy of the collection.
Persistent research workspace = structured SQLite state + visible research files, coordinated by the local application.

Why this separation matters

A paper can appear in a Monitor, the Library, a Space, and My Publications without becoming four unrelated papers. It can also acquire a DOI after first arriving as an arXiv preprint, or acquire a publication PDF while retaining earlier versions. The database preserves continuity across those changes; visible files preserve user ownership and inspectability.

TerminologyThis guide uses Personal Research Workspace for the on-screen projection and Visible Research Files for assets visible to the native filesystem. These are explanatory terms, not menu names. Together they form the visible workspace, but they serve different roles.

Understand the System

Understand the Persistent Paper Object

Gewu Insight treats a scholarly work as an object that persists through discovery, publication, file changes, and personal organization—not as a temporary search result or a single PDF.

One identity can accumulate evidence

The central record uses an internal paper identity. A DOI or arXiv identifier is important evidence attached to that identity, but neither is a safe universal primary key: an early preprint may have no DOI, an imported PDF may initially have no reliable identifier, and an incorrect identifier may later be corrected.

Do not collapse four different things

ObjectMeaningExample
Paper recordThe shared scholarly identity and normalized metadata.The work that later connects arXiv and a journal DOI.
Placement or relationWhy and where the paper appears in your workspace.A Library folder entry, a shortcut, a My Publications role, or an Author Monitor association.
Resource recordA described file or retrievable version belonging to the paper.Preprint v2, published version, supplementary material, peer review file, or data file.
Physical fileThe bytes stored at a real path on disk.A PDF under data/Library or an associated attachment.
Paper record ≠ workspace placement ≠ resource record ≠ physical file.

What happens when the same paper is found again

Journal, Subject, and Author Monitor can encounter the same work from different directions. Identity resolution is designed to reuse one shared paper record and add source or context relationships. Copying a paper to another Library folder likewise creates another placement rather than a second independent identity. Its metadata, Gewu Key, versions, and attachments remain shared.

When the available evidence is insufficient or contradictory, separate candidates can remain until their identifiers or metadata are corrected. Automatic metadata enrichment retains conflicting evidence instead of overwriting a saved identity or forcing a merge. File import follows a distinct preservation rule: a PDF matched to an existing paper is kept in its Paper Files and shown in the chosen folder, even if its detected metadata conflicts. Review that assignment and use the file reassignment commands when necessary. The shared-object model is the resolution target; it does not justify merging uncertain works merely because their titles look similar.

A network observation can be transient while acquisition is running. Once a result is cataloged as a shared paper record, it has a Gewu Key even if a particular Monitor view does not display that key. A Monitor result may still have no local Paper Files because no file has been downloaded or attached; adding it to Library creates a visible placement rather than inventing a new scholarly identity.

Gewu Insight also manages independent non-PDF files, such as Markdown overviews, spreadsheets and images. These ordinary files have an internal storage key so that their location and attachments remain trackable, but the App does not display a scholarly Gewu Key for them. A PDF paper can have a public Gewu Key before its DOI or arXiv identity is known; a standalone Markdown note does not become a paper merely by being imported.

Identity corrections should preserve continuity

Editing a DOI or arXiv identifier changes evidence on the existing paper. It should not silently make an unrelated second paper, rename every file, or discard your folder placements and read history. When evidence conflicts, inspect the title, authors, venue, and files before confirming the correction.

ImportantSimilar titles are not proof of identity, and matching filenames are not proof that two resources are the same. Use identifiers, metadata, file fingerprints, and provenance together.

Publication updates stay with the original work

A correction, erratum, retraction, expression of concern, withdrawal or addendum is a notice about an article, not a second research-paper identity. Its own DOI, title and date are retained as linked notice metadata under the original Gewu Key. A notice PDF is an associated file and does not become the automatic Default. A corrected full article is a different file type and may become Default through the normal version rules. See Check an article for publication updates.

Understand the System

Understand Why SQLite Is the Core

SQLite is the source of truth for Gewu Insight because it preserves the identity, relationships, resource registry, and operational memory that neither a filename nor an exported report can express.

Four families of structured state

The database does not store the PDF bytes themselves. It stores enough structured information to understand the files: which paper they belong to, what file type they represent, where they are, where they came from, whether they are annotated, and which one should be used by default.

Why a folder scan is not an equivalent database

File Explorer can show that paper.pdf exists. It cannot reliably say whether it is a published version or a preprint, whether it is annotated, where it came from, whether the same work is also in My Publications, or which file is the manual default. Those facts live in SQLite.

Transactions, relationships, and WAL

Database mechanismUser-facing purpose
TransactionsKeep a multi-step state change together so a partly applied edit is less likely to become the visible truth.
Foreign-key relationshipsConnect a resource or placement to the correct shared paper instead of relying on a coincidentally similar filename.
WAL (write-ahead logging)Lets foreground reading and background updates coexist more safely than repeated full-file rewrites.
Schema migrationAdds new structures and backfills required state during an upgrade rather than asking the user to rebuild the database.

WAL improves normal concurrency; it is not a substitute for a coherent backup. Close Gewu Insight before copying its live database, and back up the managed files with it.

Durable preferences and shipped defaults

Journal subscriptions are durable SQLite state as well. The database preserves which journals are enabled, their identifiers and source settings, and their display order. The journal catalog shipped with a newer app version is a set of defaults, not an instruction to overwrite your personal list.

On the first upgrade that introduces durable subscriptions, Gewu Insight seeds the database from the existing journal configuration and history. After that one-time seed, adding, disabling, restoring, or reordering a journal changes the database record. Replacing source code or rebuilding the app does not silently re-enable a journal you removed or discard journals you added.

Cross-layer changesSQLite transactions protect database state. A file move and its database update cannot be one native SQLite transaction, so the local service coordinates the steps and uses validation or compensating recovery when a filesystem operation fails.

Exports and provenance

JSON, HTML, Markdown, Word, LaTeX, and PDF outputs are derived artifacts. They can be regenerated, shared, or inspected, but editing them does not alter the source records. Raw source evidence may also be retained inside SQLite for provenance; this does not turn an external JSON export into a second source of truth.

Paper-level Monitor provenance

Normalized paper-source observations are the authority for how a canonical paper was encountered. Each observation identifies a source kind, provider name, and stable source key, and keeps first-seen and last-seen times. The same paper and effective source update one observation instead of increasing the provenance count indefinitely.

Journal Monitor also connects each observed paper to the relevant fetch run. The run supplies the journal, requested date window, status, and timing; the paper-level observation records that the reporting source saw this particular work. Subject and Author Monitor relationships can point to the same canonical paper, so three discovery routes add context without manufacturing three scholarly identities.

A bibliographic metadata refresh can add a newly proven source, but it cannot erase an earlier Journal, Subject, or Author observation. Display counts and the older raw-source list are compatibility projections of the normalized observations rather than an independent truth. When two paper identities are safely merged, their source observations move to the surviving canonical paper and duplicate observations converge.

Discovery is not storageA provenance relationship does not by itself create a Library placement or a local PDF. It records how the work entered view. Organization and file acquisition remain separate, explicit actions.

What the app does during an upgrade

On startup, the storage layer reads the database schema version, checks for required tables and fields, applies additive migrations in order, ensures required roots exist, and backfills stable keys or resource records where older data needs them. A normal migration preserves paper identities, folder placements, monitored-journal choices, fetch provenance, and file paths. This is why a project upgrade should preserve the existing database and files rather than replace them with an empty database.

Do not edit the live database manuallyA seemingly small manual change can violate a relationship that is not visible in one table. Use the app for normal work and make a closed, complete backup before any diagnostic intervention.

Understand the System

Understand Visible Research Files

Your PDFs and attachments remain real local files. Gewu Insight adds a resource model around them so several versions and related materials can belong to one paper without hiding them inside an opaque cloud library.

One paper, one file bundle

Managed and linked resources

Storage modeMeaningSafe expectation
ManagedThe active stored path is inside the Gewu Insight project data area.Move, classify, replace, or delete it through the app so paths and relationships change together.
LinkedThe active stored path remains outside the managed research workspace.Availability depends on that external path, and the app should not silently reorganize it.

A resource can be managed while retaining a separate external source path as provenance. The existence of that source path does not by itself make the managed copy a linked resource, and the external original remains protected.

Folder Loader is a migration-oriented workflow. It imports a visible collection as a collection instead of asking you to classify every incoming file as an attachment before identity resolution. The original source path and the managed result remain conceptually distinct.

How the default file is resolved

An explicit manual default takes precedence while it remains available and valid. Otherwise, usable files are ranked as Corrected published version, Published version, Accepted manuscript, then Preprint. If none is available, Unknown or Other files provide a stable fallback: prefer the existing main file, otherwise the earliest PDF, otherwise the earliest remaining eligible file. No publication type is inferred from this fallback.

Correction notices, supplements, peer review files, Perspective, News and Views, Summary, Analysis, Source Data and Source Code do not become the automatic default. You may choose an available valid resource manually. Missing files, Invalid file and unresolved identity-conflict files are excluded from automatic selection; some bundles can therefore have no eligible automatic Default.

Published filesThe user-facing type is Published version. A later formal correction can be classified as Corrected published version; the correction notice itself remains a separate peer.

Fingerprints and annotations

In the normal App PDF import, attachment and download workflows, exact SHA-256, content-oriented fingerprint, annotation count, and annotated state are computed as the resource is registered. They do not depend on a later refresh. Exact SHA-256 answers “are these bytes identical?” Adding a highlight or note normally changes those bytes. The content fingerprint is designed to recognize the same underlying document while discounting annotation-only changes, allowing clean and annotated copies to be related without treating them as blindly interchangeable.

Gewu Insight counts user-created comments and markup—such as highlights, notes, drawings, stamps, and form edits—as annotations. Structural PDF elements such as publisher hyperlinks, internal navigation links, and ordinary page actions do not make a freshly downloaded publisher or arXiv PDF Annotated.

An exact duplicate can be reused instead of stored twice. A clean PDF and an annotated copy may have different exact hashes but the same content fingerprint; both can be retained when the annotation state is meaningful.

Why File Explorer and the UI do not look identical

The filesystem must expose practical paths and folders; the UI must expose the meaning of one paper bundle. A Library paper can therefore retain a compatibility primary file in the visible topic folder while related files live under a mirrored Associated Files path. Paper Files deliberately presents all resource records as flat peers instead of mirroring those physical directories.

ImportantDo not manually move or rename managed resources in File Explorer. The bytes may still exist, but the saved path and live workspace can disagree. Use an app-supported move, repair, or restore; do not assume a restart will rediscover an arbitrary manual move.

The separate MCP import workflow requires metadata from the AI and performs file integrity checks without the full PDF identification or image-fingerprint workflow. It never starts Resolve as part of import.

See also

Understand Paper FilesChoose File Types and the Default FileHow Gewu Insight Stores Files

Understand the System

Understand the Personal Research Workspace

The five research views—Library, My Publications, Journal Monitor, Subject Monitor, and Author Monitor—share research objects. Browser is the sixth main tab, with its own website session. Moving between research views does not reset a paper's identity.

Views are relational projections

A Library folder answers “where do I organize this?” My Publications answers “how does this relate to my authorship?” Author Monitor answers “how does this relate to this researcher?” These are different relationships to the same possible work. The interface queries those relationships and projects the relevant controls, status, and files for the current task.

Library placements and shortcuts

A paper can have more than one Library placement. Copying it to another folder reuses the shared identity and resources. A shortcut tab is another entry point to a Library location, not another paper collection. A Space is an independent organizational root, but papers placed there can still reuse the same identity model.

Discovery does not require immediate file management

A Monitor result may remain a discovery relationship with metadata and status but no local Paper Files. A cataloged work already has a Gewu Key, which Author Monitor also shows. Downloading or attaching a file creates a resource relationship; adding the paper to Library creates a managed placement. Neither action should manufacture a second work merely because the user entered from another tab.

Why the same action can have different scope

Removing an author from Author Monitor removes that monitored-author relationship. Removing a shortcut removes an entry point. Moving a Library placement changes organization. Deleting a managed resource changes the paper's file bundle. The selected view supplies scope, while SQLite preserves what remains shared.

A useful mental modelThe UI shows a personal map of a shared object graph. It is “visible” because you can navigate and act on it, but SQLite—not pixels on the screen—preserves the graph.

See also

Folders, Shortcuts, and SpacesMy PublicationsState, Scope, and Safe Change

Understand the System

Move from Discovery to Durable Memory

Gewu Insight connects monitoring, identity resolution, version handling, and personal organization into one repeatable research loop.

A paper can change without losing its history

  1. Acquire an early work. Subject Monitor finds an arXiv preprint. Its source and discovery context are stored.
  2. Identify the work. The title, authors, and arXiv identifier connect it to one shared paper identity.
  3. Resolve its first resource. A preprint PDF becomes the automatic default because no higher-priority file is available.
  4. Remember your context. You add it to a Library folder, read it, and attach notes or data.
  5. Acquire new evidence later. Journal Monitor or a metadata refresh finds the published DOI. Use Download, or open the publisher PDF in Browser and choose Save to Gewu, to acquire the file.
  6. Resolve without erasing. The published file becomes the automatic default unless a manual choice is sticky; the preprint and its provenance remain peer records.

Operational state is part of scientific memory

A result count alone is ambiguous. The app distinguishes work that was never attempted from work that completed with no results, partially completed, failed, or entered a cooldown before retry. It also remembers imports, downloads, metadata refreshes, source tasks, and read state so the next action can be informed rather than blindly repeated.

StateMeaningReason to preserve it
Empty and completeThe requested source or date was checked and returned no matching records.Prevents “zero” from being mistaken for “not run.”
PartialSome sources completed while another did not.Allows a targeted retry instead of discarding useful completed work.
FailedAn operation produced a specific error.Makes the failure visible and avoids pretending the result is authoritative.
Cooldown or retry scheduledA remote service asked the app to wait or a transient error needs backoff.Reduces repeated traffic and protects normal foreground use.

Background work should not seize the foreground

Fetches, metadata refreshes, and imports report progress in reserved status areas and save their state. You should still be able to browse already stored material. Where callers share an online service, service-specific pacing, locks, cooldowns, and retry policies coordinate their requests. These controls reduce unnecessary traffic; they cannot guarantee that a publisher will never rate-limit or block a network address.

The loop is user-directedGewu Insight preserves the consequences of what you monitor, save, read, ignore, classify, and publish. It does not silently replace your research judgment with an invisible global keyword filter.

See also

Journal MonitorSubject MonitorAuthor Monitor

Understand the System

Understand State, Scope, and Safe Change

A safe local research workspace changes only the object and relationship you intended while preserving shared identity, resources, provenance, and recoverable state.

Eight invariants behind normal operations

One shared identityThe same scholarly work should not fragment merely because several sources or folders found it.
Many contexts, not blind copiesFolders, Spaces, monitors, and My Publications add relationships around the shared paper.
Deletion has scopeRemoving one relationship should not destroy unrelated relationships or shared resources.
State survives restartSaved reading and workflow state, retries, failures, versions, and provenance are durable.
Repeated operations convergeRefreshing, importing, or downloading the same evidence should not create endless duplicates.
Good metadata is protectedA weak or empty response should not silently erase stronger saved evidence.
Database and files agreeSaved resource paths should point to the intended real files after an app-managed move.
Failure remains inspectableDeletion, import, move, and network failure should preserve enough state to recover or retry.

Read an action by its scope

ActionIntended scopeWhat should remain
Remove an Author Monitor profileThe monitored-author relation and its profile context.Shared papers, Library placements, My Publications, and managed files.
Remove a shortcutThat fast entry point.The underlying Library folder and its papers.
Copy a paper to another folderAdd another placement.One shared paper identity and resource bundle.
Move a paper in the appChange its managed placement and corresponding stored paths.Gewu Key, metadata, versions, and associations.
Make another file defaultChange the reading preference; the selected managed file becomes the main file.Paper and resource identity, file contents and all other resources. The previous main file is retained in Associated Files, including when the new Default is not a PDF.
Delete an associated fileThat resource relationship and its managed file, subject to confirmation.The paper identity and unrelated resources.

Recycle follows active ownership. As long as any normal Library, Space or My Publications placement uses a paper, its original must remain outside the local Recycle directory. Removing a folder applies this rule to its whole subtree. Re-adding a recycled paper to a normal location brings its original back out, with SQLite paths and shortcuts updated together. See Delete and Recover Items for the separate rules for placements, individual attachments and permanent deletion.

Recovery is part of the design

Recycle keeps ordinary removals recoverable. Import batches and operation status provide evidence about what ran. Resource paths, hashes, and provenance help diagnose missing or duplicate files. The app can migrate older storage structure forward, but migration is not a reason to discard the previous database or original files.

Back up one coherent research asset

A reliable backup contains the SQLite database and the managed file roots from the same closed application state. Copying only the database preserves descriptions without every artifact; copying only folders preserves bytes without all identities, relationships, classifications, and operation history. A portable desktop copy is useful for sharing visible folder material, but it is not automatically a complete live-workspace backup.

Before a major update or migrationQuit Gewu Insight, preserve the complete selected Gewu Database and any external linked originals, verify the backup can be read, then update the software while keeping that database. Do not create a fresh empty database and attempt to reconstruct the workspace from export files.

See also

Delete and Recover ItemsBack Up and UpgradeTroubleshooting

Library

Understand the Library Layout

The Library uses a File Explorer-style column view, but the database—not the visible folder alone—defines the paper and its relationships.

Read the columns from left to right

  1. Source: the main Library, a shortcut, or a Space.
  2. Folders: each selection opens its children in the next column.
  3. Items: the papers and other files in the selected folder.
  4. Paper Files: shown only when a paper or managed file can expose related files.
  5. Paper Details: metadata and actions for the selected work.

Use the breadcrumb

The breadcrumb at the bottom displays the full managed path. A shortcut shows the real ancestry from Library or its independent Space root, including folders above the shortcut target. Its alias does not replace that path. Hover over the path to read it in full when space is limited. The segments are informational; use the columns or Left Arrow to navigate to a parent. The List View / Table View control at the lower right changes the representation of items without moving them.

Follow background work in the bottom bar

Folder Loader, batch Refresh Info, and individual downloads or refreshes have separate activity indicators. A long batch stays visible alongside a smaller operation instead of combining their messages. Indicators share the available footer width, shorten long text with an ellipsis, and keep navigation controls available. If many tasks no longer fit, scroll the indicator area horizontally. Hover over an indicator to read its full message and available task details. The activity dot marks work in progress; a paused task remains visible without that running animation.

The footer's Details opens the current Loader operation, or an active/paused Refresh Info task when no Loader notice is present. For a particular saved refresh, use Loader > Refresh All Metadata and select it under Refresh tasks. These task details are separate from the right-side Paper Details. See the complete close, return and stop workflow.

Folder Details

When you select a folder, the right side shows its name, type, and the number of child folders and items. This is informational; it is not another folder level.

See also

Folders, Shortcuts, and SpacesSearch, List View, and Table ViewUnderstand Paper Files

Library

Navigate with Mouse and Keyboard

Library and Space columns form one keyboard path with Paper Files. Focus moves into Paper Files with the Right Arrow and returns to the selected paper with the Left Arrow.

Move through folders and papers

  • Press ↑ or ↓ to change the selection in the focused column.
  • Press → on a folder to enter it.
  • Press ← to return to its parent.
  • Double-click a Library paper row to open its Default file: PDFs open in the Windows default PDF application; other formats use their Windows application. An unclassified legacy import falls back to its available current file.

Move between the source rail and Library columns

  1. Return to the leftmost Library column. Press ← once more to move focus to the vertical source rail.
  2. Press ↑ or ↓ on the rail. Move through Library, shortcuts, and Spaces. The highlighted source opens immediately; you do not need to press Return.
  3. Press →. Focus enters the first visible Library column for that source. Its active row changes from the quieter background selection to the stronger blue content selection.

While the source rail owns focus, the current row in the adjacent column remains visible in a quieter blue so you do not lose your place. The rail keeps focus while you move between sources and releases it only after you press →. Once you are navigating Library content, pressing ↑ at the first row stays in the Library instead of unexpectedly moving to the app tabs across the top.

Enter and leave Paper Files

  1. Select a paper in the main item column. Paper Files appears to its right. No Paper Files card is highlighted yet.
  2. Press →. Focus enters Paper Files and the active card gains a light-blue selection. The main paper remains visible with a quieter selection color.
  3. Press ↑ or ↓. Move through the flat Paper Files list.
  4. Press ←. Focus returns to the main paper. Paper Files no longer shows an active card.

The same focus rules apply in the main Library, a shortcut, and every Space. Paper Files is a database-backed view of the selected work rather than a physical child folder, but the keyboard transition is intentionally continuous: → enters the bundle, ← returns to the same paper, and the next ↑ or ↓ moves in the main item column.

Preview while navigating

In Paper Files, press Space to open Preview. While Preview is open, use ↑ and ↓ to follow adjacent files. Press Space again or close Preview to dismiss it.

Use the Preview window

  • For a PDF, use the thumbnail strip to jump to a page and scroll the page area independently.
  • Drag the title bar to reposition the preview. Drag its resize corner when you need more reading space.
  • Choose Open in Default App when you want the full the Windows default PDF application application.
  • When Preview is already open, changing the Paper Files selection updates the preview without requiring another open action.
NoteSingle-click selects a Paper Files item. Double-click opens it. This prevents an accidental external app launch while you are classifying files.

See also

Understand Paper FilesPreview FilesKeyboard Shortcuts

Library

Organize Folders, Shortcuts, and Spaces

Folders organize a root. Shortcuts provide another entrance to the Library. Spaces keep an independent root for a project or research context.

Renaming a managed folder or Space also renames its local storage. Use the App’s Rename command so its main directory, mirrored Associated Files paths and shortcuts stay consistent. Existing paper identities, file contents, classifications and Default choices are retained. A busy-file message means the operation could not finish yet; allow the active file operation to finish and retry. Renaming a Shortcut changes its label rather than its target folder.

Choose the right structure

StructureUse it forWhat it changes
Library folderA durable topic hierarchy inside the main collection.Creates or moves a managed path.
Shortcut tabFast access to a Library location you use often.Adds another entry point; it does not duplicate the paper record.
SpaceAn independent project, course, collaboration, or temporary collection.Uses its own managed root under data/Spaces.

Create, rename, or move

  1. Right-click the relevant folder area. Choose New Folder, Rename, Copy, or Paste.
  2. For a move, drag the item to its destination. Wait for the destination to indicate it can receive the item, then release.
  3. Check the breadcrumb and Paper Details. After the operation completes, the visible path and folder membership reflect the new location.

Shortcut and Space tabs can be dragged to change their order. Their inactive colors distinguish the tab groups; the active tab uses the common selected style. With the keyboard, press ← from the leftmost content column to focus this rail, use ↑ and ↓ to open another source, then press → to enter its content.

Use the Space or Shortcut heading

The persistent heading identifies the source in both List View and Table View, even after you open a nested folder. It spans that source's folder and content area, including Paper Files when visible, and stops before Paper Details. The nested folder keeps its own heading below it.

Open the … menu at the right of the heading, or Right-click the source tab, for Rename and source actions. Renaming a shortcut changes its navigation label, not the underlying folder. Spaces also offer Move Space to Library here. These commands replace the former toolbar of large buttons.

To add a paper inside the current folder, Right-click blank space in that folder and choose Add Paper. Library, shortcuts and Spaces use the same inline input. Add Paper from the source heading menu targets that source's root; check the destination before submitting.

Color folders and remove navigation entries

Right-click an ordinary folder and choose Color to change its folder color. Protected roots do not offer this command. On the source rail, Remove Shortcut removes only the shortcut, leaving its folder and papers intact. Remove Empty Space works only after both its managed contents and remaining files are empty; move the Space into Library if you want to keep its hierarchy.

Work with several entries

Ctrl-click to add or remove individual entries from a selection. Shift-click, or hold Shift while using the arrow keys, to extend a range in the current folder. Copy the selected entries with Ctrl+C, paste into the active destination with Ctrl+V, or press Delete to apply the normal reference-aware deletion rules.

To include an existing Library paper in your own publication list, select one or more paper rows, Right-click, and choose Add to My Publications. This adds the publication relationship to the same paper and Gewu Key; it does not remove the Library placement. Review authorship roles in My Publications afterward.

To update the information for one project or topic, Right-click its active folder and choose Refresh Info. The task includes every subfolder once per Gewu Key and follows the same cooldowns as the all-Library task. See Refresh Info: One Paper, a Folder, or the Library.

Copy a paper to another folder

A Library copy creates another placement of the same paper. Windows secondary main-file locations use .lnk shortcuts, and secondary Associated Files locations point to the canonical bundle. Versions and attachments remain associated with that paper; a placement copy does not create another unrelated identity.

Move an entire Space into Library

Use this when a temporary or project Space should become part of the permanent Library hierarchy.

  1. Select the Space on the left rail. Open the Space that you want to keep as a normal Library folder.
  2. Open the heading’s … menu and choose Move Space to Library. You can also Right-click the Space tab. The move sheet explains that the Space will become a folder with the same name.
  3. Choose Destination in My Library. Select the Library folder that should contain the moved Space.
  4. Confirm the move. The complete Space hierarchy, including its files and subfolders, moves together.

When the move finishes, the Space tab is removed and Library opens the moved folder. Canonical paper identities, folder placements, and Paper Files resource associations remain connected; the operation does not create duplicate paper records.

ImportantMove managed papers in Gewu Insight, not directly in File Explorer. The app updates the visible file, associated bundle, and live database paths together.

See also

How Gewu Insight Stores FilesDelete and Recover Items

Library

Search and Change Views

Search locates items across the managed collection. List View emphasizes browsing; Table View emphasizes metadata comparison.

Search the collection

  1. Select the search control in the top-right corner.
  2. Enter a title, author, journal, identifier, or filename. Results may come from the Library and Spaces.
  3. Select a result. Its Paper Details and managed path become available.
  4. Clear the search. Return to the previous Library location.

Edit the query and use fuzzy matching

Double-click a word, drag to select characters, or use Ctrl+A to select the focused query. Type to replace it or press Delete. Ctrl+F focuses workspace search; each research tab retains its own query.

Library matching tolerates small spelling errors, partial words and word endings, with exact matches ranked first. Server and visible-result matching share the same rules. It searches saved titles, authors, journals, identifiers and filenames, not every PDF's full text. Try a surname or title fragment if a long query finds nothing.

This is fuzzy text matching; it does not generate Chinese/English translations, acronym expansions or concept-level synonyms. Subject Monitor discovery uses separate, literal keywords. Library searches do not change those keywords or request online discovery.

Switch views

Choose View > List View or View > Table View. You can also use Shift+Ctrl+V. Changing the view does not rename, move, or rewrite files. Active Library search uses its result list and disables Table View. Clear the search to use Table View for the current folder again.

In either view, Right-click the folder contents and choose Sort by Name or Sort by Modified Time for folder ordering. These commands clear any active table-column sort.

Sort by a table column

  1. Click Title, Authors, Year, Journal, or Time added. The first click sorts ascending: displayed text alphabetically, Year numerically, or Time added from oldest to newest.
  2. Click again to reverse. The header arrow shows the direction.
  3. Continue navigating. Library, shortcuts and Spaces retain the chosen column and direction. Keyboard movement and range selection follow the visible order.

Folders stay above papers, and missing metadata stays below known values in either direction. Sorting preserves the selected paper, its identity and its files.

Time added shows when that folder or paper placement was added, in local date and time. It is separate from the publication date and the file’s modification time. A Shortcut shows the original placement’s time; renaming, moving or refreshing metadata does not reset it. A new copied placement has its own addition time. Click again for newest first. In a narrow window, scroll the table horizontally to reach all five headers; the headers and rows move together.

See also

Library LayoutKeyboard Shortcuts

Library

Add Papers and Files

A normal Library import creates a managed local copy and a database record. The original source file remains where it was.

Drag a paper into a folder

  1. Open the destination folder in Library.
  2. Drag a PDF from File Explorer into the item area. Drop it on the folder or in its contents.
  3. Wait for the item to appear. The app copies the file into managed storage and begins local identification.
  4. Review Paper Details. Confirm the title, DOI, arXiv identifier, and file classification.

Add a paper by DOI, arXiv ID, URL, or title

  1. Open the destination folder. The resolved paper will be placed in that Library, Shortcut or Space folder.
  2. Choose Add Paper. Right-click blank space in the folder contents and choose the command to open the inline lookup field.
  3. Enter a DOI, arXiv identifier, supported article URL, or title. A DOI or arXiv identifier is the strongest identity clue.
  4. Press Return or click Add Paper once. The app resolves the query and adds the paper to the displayed destination. A failed lookup leaves an error in the inline form.
  5. Review the added paper in Details. Check its title, authors, identifiers, journal and year, especially after using a title query.

If the identity already exists, Gewu Insight reuses the canonical paper and adds the selected folder placement rather than creating an unrelated duplicate.

NoteA paper record does not require a local PDF. Add Paper creates or reuses the metadata record; it does not automatically download a PDF. Use Download or Add File separately when you want a managed local file.
NoteA file added to an existing paper’s Paper Files bundle is an attachment or version of that paper. A normal folder drop creates or reuses a paper placement in that folder. When identity matching finds an existing paper, the incoming file joins its Paper Files; different PDFs are retained even when they share a DOI.

Folder drops and Folder Loader use the same import rules. An identity mismatch keeps the file with the matched paper, preserves its existing metadata and Default, and records the filename and identifiers in Details. It does not pause for a review decision. Import status stays in the bottom bar until dismissed; failed or stopped imports also refresh Library so completed items remain visible. A temporary progress connection failure triggers reconnection rather than reporting that the import stopped.

See also

Add and Classify AttachmentsUse Folder LoaderMove a Standalone File into Paper Files

Library

Use Paper Details

Paper Details combines actions, identifiers, metadata, and citation counts. Library, My Publications, and Author Monitor start with the paper title, without a separate heading bar. The available actions occupy two rows: Open in Default App, Download and Open Website first; Google Scholar, Get DOI and Refresh Info second. Each button label stays on one line.

Top actions

ActionWhat it does
Open in Default AppOpens the preferred local PDF in the Windows default PDF application.
DownloadRetrieves the best available paper file without overwriting a different preserved version.
Open WebsiteOpens the publisher, DOI, arXiv, or best known work page using Website Links: Gewu Insight Browser by default, or the system default browser.
Google ScholarSearches for the work in Google Scholar.
Get DOIExamines local paper files for DOI or arXiv evidence.
Refresh InfoRefreshes paper information using its saved DOI or arXiv ID. Hover over the button to see the latest result below it.

Check an article for publication updates

  1. Check that the article's saved DOI is correct, then choose Refresh Info.
  2. The refresh checks Crossref for explicit publication-update relations to that DOI, including notices published after you saved the article. Review the refresh result for source failures or conflicts.
  3. Inspect the notice summaries in Paper Files. Expand one to read its kind, date, title and DOI, then follow the DOI to the publisher's notice.

Refresh saves the notice relationship; it does not automatically download a notice PDF, replace the original article, change its Gewu Key or change your Default. A notice can therefore appear without a local file. When you obtain its PDF, retain it under the original article and choose the appropriate notice file type.

Coverage and timingSaved Library, Space and My Publications papers are not periodically checked merely because they are saved. Request Refresh Info for a paper or a folder when you need a fresh check. Detection depends on the publisher supplying an explicit relation and Crossref making it available. A successful check with no notice is not proof that the article has never been corrected or retracted; consult the publisher when that status matters. Missing or ambiguous original-article evidence requires review.

File management

Library uses the adjacent Paper Files column; Paper Details does not repeat a Files box. My Publications keeps its collapsible Files · n management panel. Author Monitor shows a compact local filename with the full path on hover; Get DOI appears when a local PDF is available.

Metadata rows

The title appears once at the top. The rows below include authors, journal, date, DOI, arXiv, Gewu Key, citation, fields, and folder membership when available. Gewu Key is the stable, human-visible storage handle for a cataloged work record. It is not a DOI, arXiv identifier, or the database's relational primary key.

Compare citation sources

Merged Citations brings together the counts returned by OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Crossref, NASA ADS, and saved Google Scholar data when those services have a match. Select a source label to show its saved count in the headline; this does not start a refresh. The merged estimate compares published, preprint, and already-merged records rather than simply adding every provider's total. Separate published/preprint estimates can be combined, so this is not a verified count of unique citing papers. The yearly histogram uses OpenAlex data and does not switch provider when you select another count. PubMed Details supplies identifiers and indexing information, not another citation-count source.

Inspect influential citations

When Semantic Scholar reports an Influential count, select it to inspect citing papers that Semantic Scholar classifies as especially meaningful to the cited work. This is Semantic Scholar’s classification, not a score calculated by Gewu Insight. The list can include citation context, intent, citing authors, venue, year, and citation counts when the service supplies them.

Influential Citations is fetched on demand and cached locally for several hours. A saved API key gives Gewu Insight an individual Semantic Scholar allowance, but it is still limited to about one request per second and can be temporarily throttled. If the service returns a rate-limit message, the app pauses repeat requests for a few minutes; the paper record, existing citation totals, and any previously displayed result remain unaffected.

Read and reuse the record

  • A representative first figure, when available, provides a visual checkpoint above the actions.
  • Abstract keeps the paper summary in the independently scrolling details pane.
  • BibTeX and Copy Code provide a citation record for reference software or LaTeX.
  • Nature Reference and Copy Reference provide a formatted reference string.
  • Folders lists every Library location for the shared work. Remove a location there only when you intend to remove that reference.
NoteGewu Key is assigned when a work is first cataloged in SQLite, before Add to Library. Its row remains visible in Author Monitor, including while details load; a missing value shows (undefined). Adding to Library reuses the existing key and updates the view without creating a second identity.

See also

Edit DOI and arXiv IdentifiersUnderstand Paper FilesHow Gewu Insight Stores Files

Library

Edit DOI and arXiv Identifiers

DOI and arXiv can identify the same work across publication stages. Correct either value in Paper Details before downloading or synchronizing versions.

Save or correct either identifier

  1. Select the DOI or arXiv value. Enter the identifier, including in an empty row. DOI URLs are accepted; arXiv accepts forms such as arXiv:2106.14849 and valid legacy IDs.
  2. Press Return. Wait for the server to save it, or review the two records if the DOI is already assigned elsewhere. After a normal save, the field leaves editing and the green message above the metadata reads Identifier updated, or Identifier saved if unchanged. Invalid input stays editable with an error.
  3. Choose Refresh Info. Saving alone does not request remote metadata. Refresh uses the saved DOI and/or arXiv ID; a DOI is not required for an arXiv-only paper. A changed DOI still in the editor is saved before refresh.
  4. Inspect the result. Hover over Refresh Info for its information box below the button: changed fields, last check, source outcomes and conflicts. Keyboard focus also reveals it; pointer departure or Escape dismisses it.

To clear either identifier, save an empty value with Return. Both rows remain available for later edits. The arXiv row also has an arrow to open its website and a download control for the latest available PDF.

Replace an incorrectly identified work

If an automatically recognized DOI belongs to the wrong article or book, replace it and press Return first. Clearing and then entering the correct value also records a correction. On the next Refresh Info, a primary source must return that exact corrected identifier before the old automatic bibliography can be replaced. The old information is retained in correction history; missing or mismatched responses leave it available while you retry. This is why an ordinary automatic conflict guard does not prevent a verified manual correction.

An ordinary correction keeps the same Gewu Key, paper locations, files, classifications, Default and user notes. A manual DOI edit that conflicts with another record opens the explicit review below before changing either record. After a correction is applied, later refreshes use the normal conflict checks again.

Review a DOI already assigned to another record

This review applies only when you manually enter or correct a DOI in Paper Details. It does not enable automatic merging during discovery, import, Refresh Info or arXiv editing. A matching DOI is a reason to compare the records, not proof that they represent the same paper.

  1. Open the paper from the Library or Space location you want to retain as its main location. Check its Default PDF before editing the DOI.
  2. Enter the verified DOI and press Return. Review DOI Conflict compares Current paper with Existing DOI record, including titles, authors, Gewu Keys, Default files, file counts, locations and Monitor sources.
  3. Choose the appropriate option only after checking the actual articles, then read and confirm the action. Cancel leaves both records and their files unchanged.
What you have verifiedChoice and result
Both records represent the same paperSelect These are the same paper, then Merge Records. Keep the current Gewu Key, selected main location and current Default PDF. Other managed files, including the other record's former main PDF, join its Associated Files bundle. Folder memberships and Monitor sources remain attached to the shared paper.
They are different papers, and the existing record wrongly owns the DOI that belongs to the current paperSelect These are different papers, then Correct DOI Assignment. Clear the incorrect DOI on the existing record and assign it to the current paper. Both records keep their separate Gewu Keys, files and Monitor entries.
The new entry is wrong, or the evidence is uncertainCancel. Do not use reassignment merely because the titles differ; it is only for a DOI verified to belong to the current paper.

A confirmed merge updates managed disk paths as well as the visible Library. The main PDF stays at the chosen current location, and the other managed files follow the corresponding Associated Files path. Other folder references are retained using the existing storage rules; externally linked originals are not moved or deleted.

If the existing record came from a Monitor, it remains visible there after merging. Its shared status shows that the paper is already in Library; the Monitor entry does not disappear. After either operation, inspect Paper Files and Paper Details. Metadata refresh remains a separate action.

Follow a preprint into publication

Explicit links from arXiv, Crossref, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar or configured ADS can connect a preprint and its published DOI. A newly linked DOI loads detailed publication metadata while retaining the arXiv ID. Title similarity alone cannot bind identifiers. Manual corrections and cleared values are preserved; a DOI owned by another Gewu Key is reported without merging records.

Saved Library, Space and My Publications papers are refreshed when you request it, including through a batch Refresh Info task. Saving a paper does not schedule periodic metadata refreshes. Author Monitor separately completes missing identifiers and abstracts for monitored publications, with bounded attempts and a daily allowance. This completion work does not download PDFs, change Paper Files or Default, create placements, or move your selection and focus.

The bottom bar shows a running refresh, then green Refresh complete. Partial results preserve successful updates; the hover report explains unavailable sources and retry times. For batch scope and shared cooldowns, see Refresh Info: One Paper, a Folder, or the Library.

ImportantConfirm an identifier before running a version sync. A wrong identifier can attach files from a different work.

See also

Download and Sync VersionsLiterature Data Sources

Papers and Files

Refresh Info: One Paper, a Folder, or the Library

Use one information-refresh service for a single paper, a selected folder, the active Library collection, or the metadata stage of an import. Choose the scope before starting.

Choose the operation you need

Entry pointScope and behavior
Paper Details > Refresh InfoOne paper, using Full. Either saved DOI or arXiv is sufficient; see identifier correction.
Folder context menu > Refresh InfoThe selected active Library/Space folder and all descendants, once per Gewu Key. Choose Quick or Full; default Full.
Loader > Refresh All MetadataActive Library and Space papers, excluding Recycle. It is not a refresh of every Monitor-only database record. Choose Quick or Full; default Full.
Folder Loader metadata modeImported papers use the chosen Skip, Quick or Full setting after file import and identifier recovery. File Explorer folder drops retain their separate import behavior.
Automatic background checksBounded completion of missing identifiers and abstracts in Author Monitor. Saved papers do not enter a periodic refresh queue.

Refresh known works

  1. Choose the scope. Use Loader > Refresh All Metadata, or Right-click a Library/Space folder and choose Refresh Info. A folder task includes all its subfolders. Recycle is excluded.
  2. Choose Quick or Full. Folder and all-Library tasks default to Full. Quick updates core information and DOI/arXiv links; Full adds detailed authors and citation sources.
  3. Choose Start Refresh. Each Gewu Key is checked once, even when it has several files or locations. The bottom status bar shows the task while you continue browsing.
  4. Review the log. Counts distinguish updated, unchanged, partial, failed, cooldown skipped and missing DOI/arXiv records. Missing identifiers remain visible; use the separate identifier search when needed.
  5. Pause, continue, or stop. Pause finishes the current paper and saves the remaining queue. Select the task under Refresh tasks and choose Continue, including after reopening or restarting. Stop ends the remaining queue permanently for that task while keeping completed results and history. Interrupted running refresh tasks reopen paused; stopped tasks cannot be continued.

Batch and import work skips compatible successful checks from any entry point within three days. A changed identifier does not inherit the old identifier's cooldown. Full satisfies a later Quick task; Quick does not block Full. Partial retries reuse recent successful source responses and retry failed sources. A direct Paper Details refresh can check again immediately, while shared source rate limits still apply. Author Monitor completion retains its separate retry limits and daily allowance; Google Scholar protections are unchanged.

Refreshing a shared Gewu Key updates its information in every location. Folder locations, PDF files, Paper Files classifications and Default selections stay unchanged. Multiple tasks wait in a queue; a direct single-paper refresh has priority between papers. The task log shows the most recent 200 entries; totals and the remaining queue are retained.

Pausing means the current paper is still finishing; it changes to Paused when the saved queue can resume later. Keep browsing while it settles. A completed refresh uses green Refresh complete in the bottom bar, including partial results. This reports that the operation ended, not that every source answered. Detailed outcomes remain in the task window and, for a single paper, below Refresh Info on hover. A transport failure or rejected operation still reports its error.

Jump from a log entry to Library, then return

  1. Click a paper entry in the scrolling log. Entries linked to a paper offer Show in Library on hover. You can also focus an entry and press Return or Space. General process messages and older entries without a saved paper link are plain text.
  2. Inspect the selected paper. The task window closes after the paper is revealed in Library. Its folder and paper selection are restored for this destination. Closing the window does not pause or stop the background job.
  3. Return through the bottom bar's Details. While the Loader or refresh task remains active or paused, reopen its progress window and continue reading the log. For completed refreshes, reopen Loader > Refresh All Metadata and select the saved task in Refresh tasks.

The same log navigation is available in Folder Loader after an entry has been associated with a saved paper. Selecting text in the log lets you copy it without opening the paper. If the referenced item is no longer available, the window shows an error instead of silently navigating to another work.

Close, pause, and stop are different

ActionWhat happens
Close the task windowHide the window and keep working. The task continues while the app is running; Details returns to it.
Pause / ContinueRefresh Info finishes the current paper, saves the remaining queue and can resume it later, including after an app restart.
StopEnd a running or paused Refresh Info task. Stopping lets the current paper finish safely. Completed changes and history stay, but the remaining queue will not resume. Start Refresh creates another task if needed.
Stop Import / Stop SearchFolder Loader or identifier search stops at its next safe checkpoint. Completed imports and identifier changes stay. Stop Import also ends that import's linked metadata queue; it is not Delete Import.
