A stopped task no longer leaves a resumable progress indicator in the footer. Folder import and identifier search use their own Stop controls; they do not offer the batch refresh's Pause/Continue pair.

Find missing identifiers

  1. Choose Loader > Find All Missing Identifiers.
  2. Choose Start Search. The app checks active Library and Space PDFs using Crossref, OpenAlex, and Semantic Scholar where available.
  3. Review uncertain matches. Refresh or recover DOI evidence as needed, and edit an incorrect arXiv identifier inline before downloading versions.

Verified “not found” checks and transient failures use cooldowns so a repeated run does not immediately send the same requests. Bulk missing-identifier work does not use Google Scholar.

Include later corrections and retractions

Quick and Full refresh both check explicit Crossref publication updates when the paper has a DOI. A folder or all-Library refresh can therefore discover a later notice for an older saved article. Existing refresh cooldowns, scope and partial-result reporting still apply. Linked notices appear in Paper Files; refreshing does not fetch their PDFs or replace existing files. See the single-paper workflow and its coverage limits.

See also

Literature Data SourcesPublisher and Network AccessEdit DOI and arXiv Identifiers

Library

Understand Paper Files

A paper is one work record that can own several PDFs and related files. Paper Files shows that bundle without pretending it is another Library folder level.

Compact cards for one flat bundle

The Paper Files column is a flat peer list, not a hierarchy of version or attachment folders. Each card shows its filename, File type, and size by default. Click the size footer or its chevron to expand Annotation and Source into separate rows; click again to collapse them. The chevron points down when collapsed and up when expanded. Each card expands independently, and the choice lasts for the current session. File type remains visible because it identifies a preprint, accepted manuscript, published version, supplement, or other resource. The Default marker identifies the preferred file.

Select, open, or act on a file

  • Single-click a card to select it.
  • Drag a Paper Files icon or filename to File Explorer or a compatible application to copy or open the real file. Library file icons use the same native drag. The receiving application determines its accepted formats and drag behavior; not every external destination has been verified.
  • Double-click a card to open it.
  • Double-click the paper row to the left to open the paper's Default file, independently of the highlighted resource card. PDFs open in the Windows default PDF application. For unclassified files, automatic selection uses a stable Unknown/Other fallback when available; you do not have to choose a Default manually first.
  • Press Space to use Preview.
  • Right-click a card for Open, Preview, Show in File Explorer, default-file controls, Change File Type, or Delete from Paper Files where allowed. Right-click blank space in Paper Files for Add File and, when the paper has an arXiv identifier, Sync Versions. Those bundle-wide commands do not appear on an individual file card.
  • Press Delete or Backspace while Paper Files has keyboard focus to remove only the selected removable resource after confirmation. This does not delete the parent paper or its other files.

The current main file remains protected from direct deletion. Choosing Set as Default makes that resource the preferred file for opening and preview. For a privately managed paper with an active folder placement, it becomes the main file and the other resources belong in Associated Files. This applies to PDFs and non-PDFs alike. File IDs, classification and bytes are preserved; unrelated same-name files are not overwritten. Use Automatic Selection releases a manual choice and returns to the priority and fallback rules in Default selection.

Library Paper Details no longer repeats this bundle. In My Publications, which has no adjacent Paper Files column, the collapsible Files panel keeps its file-management controls. Show in File Explorer reveals a physical file.

Deleting a private managed attachment uses Windows Recycle Bin and a verified recovery backup before its file registration is removed. Shared files and external originals remain protected. A failed operation stays visible; do not assume a failure deleted the file.

Attachment deletion is shared. Every placement of the same Gewu Key uses this Paper Files bundle. Deleting one attachment here removes it from that paper everywhere; it does not merely hide it from the current folder. The current Default and protected primary file must be changed before they can be removed. This differs from deleting a Library placement, which follows the reference-aware Recycle rules.

Correct a file's paper assignment

If an imported PDF was matched to the wrong paper, Right-click its card and choose Move to Another Paper. Search the destination in Library by title, DOI, or Gewu Key, select it, and choose Move File. To make it independent, choose Create Paper from File, enter a title, and choose Create Paper. The new paper appears in the current Library folder with a new Gewu Key and no guessed DOI.

Only the selected file changes ownership when using these card commands. Its bytes, file ID, classification and source information remain intact; a name collision may require a unique filename. A source with remaining files keeps its identity and selects another eligible Default. An emptied, unshared source is removed as an independent Library item rather than left as a fileless link. Protected shared relationships can prevent that removal. For a PDF, the new independent paper receives a new Gewu Key and uses the file as its Default. A detached non-PDF remains an ordinary standalone file with an internal storage key and no public Gewu Key in the App. Managed paths follow the change: an attachment goes into the destination bundle in Associated Files; a newly independent file goes into its main folder. Explicit reassignment is respected on repeat imports. Historical analysis text is not rewritten.

AI Access can perform file ownership moves and rename files only with the separate move or rename permissions described in AI Access. Reading and adding analyses do not grant these permissions. Existing file contents cannot be edited or overwritten through AI Access.

Understand a Missing File row

Missing File means that SQLite still has a resource record, but the file is not present at the recorded local path. Gewu Insight keeps genuine missing resources visible so you can identify and repair them; it hides only an older untyped migration alias when it can prove that the alias has already been replaced by the same paper's live canonical file.

A missing attachment is not another copy of the default PDF merely because both rows have a similar name. Check Show in File Explorer, the paper's Associated Files bundle, and Recycle before deleting or importing anything. The default resource and explicitly typed attachments remain visible even when their paths need repair.

Read linked publication notices

Expandable notice summaries appear alongside the file bundle when a correction, retraction or another supported update has been linked to the article. Expand a summary to read the notice title, date and DOI. This is notice metadata, so a summary can exist even when no notice PDF has been saved. A saved notice PDF remains an ordinary associated file with its own file type.

The original article, its bibliography, files and Gewu Key remain. Notices never become the automatic Default; a corrected full article follows its separate version rule. The same summaries are available in My Publications' expanded Files panel. Use Refresh Info to check for later notices, or add a discovered notice from Journal Monitor.

See also

Preview FilesChoose File Types and the Default FileAdd and Classify AttachmentsNavigate with Mouse and Keyboard

Papers and Files

Preview Files

Select a local Library or Paper Files item and press Space to inspect it inside Gewu Insight.

Read and navigate

  1. Select the resource and press Space. Up/Down follows the file list; Escape closes the preview.
  2. PDFs use continuous pages, a thumbnail rail and native wheel scrolling. Use Ctrl+wheel to zoom the PDF. Wider pages can be panned horizontally.
  3. Use Open in Default App for the Windows reader associated with the file. Double-clicking the Library paper row opens its Default file; double-clicking a Paper Files row opens that specific file.

Read Markdown notes

Markdown supports headings, lists, quotations, code, tables and offline mathematical formulas. Leading YAML appears under collapsible Properties; analysis provenance appears under Source record. These values belong to the note and do not overwrite Paper Details.

Text wraps to the reading area; wide tables and code scroll independently. Nearby images can display locally, remote images remain explicit links, and raw HTML is escaped. Large notes are limited to a 256 KiB preview with a truncation notice; the original file is unchanged. Open the original to read beyond the preview.

Other files and recovery

Supported images, media and text can be inspected in the workspace. Unsupported formats offer an Open File action using Windows file associations. If a preview stalls, close it, select the file again and retry; check that the original file exists. There is no macOS system Quick Look mode on Windows.

See also

Preview SettingsNavigate with Mouse and KeyboardUnderstand Paper FilesTroubleshooting

Library

Choose File Types and the Default File

The default file is the preferred local representation of the paper. Choose it manually or let Gewu Insight select it. Default appears first in the file list; Up and Down follow the visible order.

Automatic selection

The automatic order is Corrected published version, Published version, Accepted manuscript, then Preprint. Within a type, a later recognized version normally wins. If none is eligible, an available Unknown or Other file supplies a fallback: keep the existing main file where possible, otherwise choose the earliest PDF, otherwise the earliest remaining eligible file. This includes standalone RTF, image and other non-PDF imports; it does not relabel them as published papers.

Automatic and manual eligibility

The four publication types above take priority over the Unknown/Other fallback. Correction and retraction notices, expressions of concern, withdrawal notices, addenda, supplementary material, peer review files, Perspective, News and Views, Summary, Analysis, Source Data and Source Code are not automatic candidates. Missing, Invalid file and unresolved identity-conflict files are also excluded. You may manually choose an existing valid file, including a supporting file. A manual choice is sticky across rescans, metadata refreshes, and later downloads until you choose Use Automatic Selection. Newly arriving files remain peer rows and do not erase or silently reclassify older files.

Choose a file manually

  1. Enter Paper Files, or expand Files in My Publications.
  2. Select the file you want.
  3. Choose Set as Default. This file will be used by Open in Default App and paper preview. You can also pin the automatically selected Default this way.

The selected file becomes the manual default. In a managed paper with an active placement, it becomes the main file and the former main file moves to Associated Files. This applies to non-PDF defaults too. The article and file identities stay unchanged. External originals and files shared with another article are protected; existing names are retained unless a collision requires a unique name.

Return to automatic selection

Choose Use Automatic Selection for a manually selected default. Gewu Insight evaluates the eligible file types again.

Classify files without collapsing annotation state

In Library, File type stays visible on each card. Click the size footer to reveal Annotation and Source, then change each control independently. In My Publications, expand Files to see all three controls directly. File type uses exactly these labels:

  • Preprint, Accepted manuscript, Published version, and Corrected published version
  • Correction notice, Retraction notice, Expression of concern, Withdrawal notice, Addendum, Supplementary material, and Peer review file
  • Perspective, News and Views, Summary, and Analysis
  • Source Data and Source Code
  • Other, Unknown, and Invalid file

Use Perspective or News and Views for related commentary, Summary or Analysis for reading notes and interpretation, and Source Data or Source Code for the accompanying research material. These labels describe this file's role; they do not change the parent paper's publication type or Gewu Key. They are not automatically promoted to Default. File extension alone does not determine the role.

Annotation state is selected independently as Annotated, Unannotated, or Unknown. Source is independently recorded as Publisher, Preprint server, Institutional repository, User import, Other, or Unknown. Manual type and annotation choices survive later fingerprint rescans.

Publisher is used only when a recognized publisher host or a publisher-specific acquisition path provides that evidence. arXiv, bioRxiv, and medRxiv are shown as Preprint server; repository hosts remain Institutional repository; ordinary local additions are User import; and a generic web download with no stronger evidence remains Other. A real host can appear after the source label when useful. Internal migration or ingestion markers are never user-facing source details, and choosing a different source clears a stale provider detail rather than appending it to the new choice.

NoteChanging File type can change the automatic Default. The selected managed Default and its main file location are synchronized together. Annotation and Source remain independent properties; changing a label does not apply a filename template or rewrite the PDF.

See also

Download and Sync VersionsAdd and Classify Attachments

Library

Add and Classify Attachments

Import first, classify afterward. This keeps the add operation simple and lets you set type, annotation state, and source after seeing the file in context.

Add a file to the paper

  1. Right-click blank space in the Paper Files area and choose Add File. In My Publications, expand Files and use Add File.
  2. Select one or more local files. Confirm the file chooser.
  3. Wait for the new row. A new item begins as Unknown unless its source proves a more specific type.
  4. Select its compact controls. Choose File type; in Library, click the size footer to expand Annotation and Source. My Publications shows those controls directly in its Files panel.

Attachment types

The same file-type choices apply to every row and to Browser capture. Use Summary or Analysis for notes, Source Data for research data, and Source Code for code; use Other when none fits. File extension and MIME type remain separate from this classification. Existing files keep their saved labels until you change them.

Adding the same unchanged file to the same paper again reuses its existing resource, including when its source path or filename has changed. Matching uses exact file contents; an edited or annotated PDF with different bytes remains a separate version. A shared DOI alone does not make two files duplicates.

Add by drag and drop

Drag one or more File Explorer files anywhere in the visible Paper Files column: over its heading, an existing card, or the empty gray area. No card needs to be expanded. Wait for the whole-column drop highlight, confirm the selected destination paper, then release. The files are copied into that paper’s associated bundle and appear in Paper Files. The same behavior applies in Library, shortcuts and Spaces.

ImportantInvalid or unreadable PDFs are rejected at file ingress. Existing migrated records that can be proven invalid remain visible as Invalid file for audit and repair, but cannot become a default.

See also

Move a Standalone File into Paper FilesHow Gewu Insight Stores Files

Library

Download and Sync Versions

Downloads add a version to the paper bundle. They do not silently overwrite a different preserved PDF.

Paper downloads accept verified publisher or authorized repository sources and check redirects. Unverified destinations stop. Use your legitimate institutional or publisher access; Gewu does not bypass subscriptions or website verification.

Download the best available paper

  1. Verify DOI and arXiv. Make sure the identifiers belong to the selected work.
  2. Choose Download at the top of Paper Details. Gewu Insight first tries the best available published file, then supported alternatives.
  3. Wait for the status message. Existing files are preserved if the incoming file is a different version; a manual default stays selected.
  4. Inspect Paper Files. Every preserved file appears in the same flat list. Automatic ranking may select the new PDF as Default and synchronize its main file location; a manual default remains unchanged. Earlier files stay in the bundle.

Keep downloading while you work

You can select other papers, switch workspaces or add another Monitor result to Library while a download runs. The running state belongs to each paper, and completion updates that paper without selecting it or returning to an earlier tab. Repeating Download for the same running paper shares its request; another paper has its own request. Ordinary Download reuses an existing valid local PDF. Downloads do not resume automatically after quitting the App.

Direct download and background webpage fallback

Downloads try the configured direct routes first. Supported publisher requests can then use Gewu's background WebView2 page to discover the article PDF without replacing your visible workspace. It shares the standalone Gewu Browser session. Missing access or an unsupported route remains an error; use an authorized publisher page to obtain the PDF.

If the background attempt still cannot retrieve a PDF

  1. Choose Open Website and open the article in Gewu's Browser. If Website Links is set to the system browser, open the address in Gewu Browser to use its shared session.
  2. Complete the publisher's normal verification or institutional sign-in yourself, and check whether the main PDF actually opens. An abstract page alone does not establish full-text access.
  3. Return to the paper and retry Download. Alternatively, with the PDF open in Browser, use Save to Gewu, verify the Key and loaded PDF in Details, then save.

A legitimate local PDF can also be attached with Add File. A timeout or authorization error leaves existing files intact; repeated retries do not create access rights. See Save an article and PDF to Library and Publisher and Network Access.

Download arXiv files

  • Use the download icon in the arXiv row to retrieve the latest arXiv PDF.
  • Right-click blank space in Paper Files and choose Sync Versions to retrieve all available arXiv revisions such as v1, v2, and v3. In My Publications, use Sync Versions inside the expanded Files panel. The command is available when the paper has an arXiv identifier.
  • Each revision is labeled with its arXiv version when known.

Duplicate protection

Gewu Insight computes exact SHA-256 and PDF content fingerprints as each new resource is registered. An exact duplicate is reused instead of stored twice. A clean PDF and a genuinely annotated copy can share a content fingerprint while retaining different exact hashes, annotation counts, and labels.

Validation before replacement

A response is not accepted merely because it begins with %PDF-. Structural PDF validation rejects empty files, HTML responses, truncated downloads, missing valid endings, and content that cannot be parsed as a PDF. A download is written to a temporary file and replaces the destination only after validation succeeds. If the request or stream fails, an existing valid file remains untouched and a partial file is not registered as a resource.

Classification follows the file that actually arrived

A publisher download is classified from the file and source actually returned. A corrected published version outranks a published version automatically; a publisher reference or accepted preview remains an accepted manuscript. Science PDFs recognized as First Release are classified as Accepted manuscript in Gewu, even when the paper metadata already names Science. A correction notice remains a separate peer and never becomes automatic merely because it came from a publisher.

A PDF URL stored in bibliographic metadata is only a retrieval lead. It does not create a Paper Files row until a download actually succeeds, the returned bytes pass validation, and a local resource is registered.

If a download is skipped because the local bytes already exist, that skipped operation does not relabel the existing file from metadata or a newly discovered URL. Correct the file type explicitly if the saved classification itself is wrong.

NoteA Monitor result is not forced into a Library placement. Where download is available, a local resource can belong to the cataloged paper even before you add that paper to Library or My Publications.

Science and Nature main articles and supplementary PDFs

The Science and Nature-family workflows distinguish the main article from supplementary PDFs and can append retrieved PDF supplements to the combined reading file. A supplement, reporting checklist or supplementary-only response cannot stand in for the main article. If the main PDF cannot be obtained, the download reports failure instead of registering a supplement as a successful article download.

Inspect the combined PDF and any download message to check what was actually retrieved; access to the article webpage does not guarantee access to every PDF. Non-PDF material is not converted into PDF pages. The file type follows the main article’s version, while the displayed filename uses the returned publisher name or a meaningful paper-based fallback. Re-downloading preserves other files and an explicitly chosen Default.

Non-PDF supplements do not make the article fail

Automatic supplement handling is PDF-only. MP4 videos, audio, archives, spreadsheets and other non-PDF attachments are skipped; they are not required for a successful main-PDF download. Nature review files, reporting summaries and source-data files are also excluded from the supplementary reading merge. You can obtain other useful files separately and attach them to Paper Files.

If the main PDF succeeds but an optional supplement is unavailable, the main file is kept and the message describes the missing supplement. A message such as main PDF unavailable; downloaded 1 PDF supplement(s) means the main article could not be retrieved, not that a video caused the failure. A not a PDF response may be an HTML access or verification page. Supplements alone are never presented as a successful main article.

See also

Choose File Types and the Default FilePublisher and Network AccessEdit DOI and arXiv Identifiers

Library

Move a Standalone File into Paper Files

If a data, image, presentation, or other file was imported as its own Library item, drag it onto the correct paper’s Paper Files area to make it an attachment.

Convert an independent item

  1. Select the destination paper. Keep its Paper Files inspector visible.
  2. Begin dragging the standalone item. The main paper remains the active destination while you drag.
  3. Move the pointer into the Paper Files drop zone. Wait for the drop feedback that identifies the target paper.
  4. Release the pointer. Gewu Insight validates the move, adopts the file into the paper bundle, and removes its independent Library position.
  5. Classify the attachment. Choose Supplementary material for an actual paper supplement, Source Data for data, Source Code for code, Summary or Analysis for notes, or Other when none fits. Expand the size footer to set Annotation and Source separately. See the complete current file-type list.

The physical file and database link now belong to the destination paper; the former standalone entry is gone.

Make a Paper Files resource independent again

Drag a resource's icon or filename from Paper Files onto a Library folder or that folder's content area. The file leaves its former paper and moves from Associated Files into the destination's main folder. A PDF becomes an independent paper with a new Gewu Key; a non-PDF becomes an ordinary standalone file with only an internal storage key. Right-clicking the resource and choosing Create Paper from File performs the same separation in the current folder, with an editable title. The former paper keeps its remaining files.

To transfer just one resource between existing papers, use Move to Another Paper or drag it into the other paper's Paper Files area. A Library paper-row drag adopts the source paper's files as a group; it removes the former independent identity only when the conversion is safe. A single-file RTF therefore disappears from its former folder and becomes one resource of the destination paper.

Check the destinationDragging within Gewu Insight changes ownership or location. Dragging a file to File Explorer or the Desktop makes an external copy and leaves Paper Files intact. Dragging from File Explorer into Paper Files imports a managed copy and keeps the external original.

If the conversion cannot finish

The file moves and database changes are coordinated as one recoverable operation. If any step fails, Gewu Insight restores the original standalone files and rolls back the paper, Library item, resource relationships, and fingerprint fields. The source should remain usable rather than becoming a half-converted attachment.

ImportantIf the source item is shared by another Library reference or protected relationship, Gewu Insight may refuse a destructive conversion. Add a copy with Add File instead.

See also

Add and Classify AttachmentsFolders, Shortcuts, and Spaces

Library

Delete and Recover Items

Deleting a paper reference either removes only that reference or moves the last active Library/Space reference to Recycle. Final deletion inside Recycle is reference-aware and uses the Windows Recycle Bin for managed files.

Delete a Library reference

  1. Right-click the item.
  2. Choose Delete.
  3. Check the result. If another active Library or Space location, or My Publications, still refers to the same work, only the selected reference is removed. Otherwise the item moves to Recycle and remains recoverable.

What happens to the original and attachments

A paper's original can move into the local Recycle directory only when no normal Library, Space or My Publications placement still uses it. The same check applies when you delete or drag a whole folder: retained papers keep their originals in normal storage, or move to a surviving location. Recycle entries can remain shortcuts to those retained originals. Other paper records sharing the registered bytes are protected too.

Recovering, copying or adding a recycled paper back to an active location brings its original out of Recycle. This includes Monitor additions, Browser saves and Add to My Publications. If a recovery parent has also been recycled, an active fallback is used. The app synchronizes SQLite file paths, Associated Files and File Explorer shortcuts while retaining Gewu Keys, file IDs, classification, Default and file contents. These checks apply during file operations; they do not silently sweep historical disk remnants.

Deleting a single removable Paper Files attachment is a different action: its private managed copy goes directly to Windows Recycle Bin and its file registration is removed from the shared paper. Other files and the parent paper stay. All placements of the same Key see this attachment change. Shared bytes and external originals remain protected.

Delete from My Publications

Select one or more publications and choose Delete. If a Library, Space, Shortcut or Recycle location still refers to the work, its shared article record, Gewu Key and files remain. Otherwise, deleting this last placement also removes the article record and its identifier tasks from SQLite; private managed files move to Windows Recycle Bin. External originals and bytes shared with other articles are preserved. Import history does not keep an otherwise unreferenced article alive.

Removing every currently saved article of a running profile import pauses that import. Continue Import does not restore previously removed source entries. An explicit Add All Publications recheck after completion can add those articles again.

Recover an item

  1. Open Recycle.
  2. Right-click the item and choose Recover.
  3. Confirm the restored location.

Delete permanently

Final deletion of Library items takes place inside Recycle. Choosing Delete on a folder moves that folder intact, including its subfolders and unregistered contents, to Windows Recycle Bin. The confirmation lists the folders and files to move. Original imported source files outside Gewu Insight are not touched. If another Library, Space, Recycle or My Publications location still refers to the paper, its shared record, Gewu Key, Paper Files and Default remain; any required local files are retained outside the folder being removed. Only papers with no remaining references are removed from SQLite.

Empty RecycleRight-click the Recycle root folder or blank space directly inside it to choose Empty Recycle. This clears every Recycle entry and moves all contents of its local disk directory to Windows Recycle Bin, including unregistered files, empty folders and broken shortcuts. The Recycle root remains. This command is not offered on files or folders inside Recycle.

The deletion confirmation has a bounded height and an independently scrolling item list. Read the selected scope, then confirm. A failure remains visible for retry instead of reporting success. Empty Recycle clears the application's Recycle; it does not empty Windows Recycle Bin.

See also

Back Up and UpgradeHow Gewu Insight Stores Files

Import and Transfer

Use Folder Loader

Folder Loader imports an existing directory tree into managed Library storage while preserving relative paths.

For a Zotero library, use Loader > Import from Zotero instead. It reads collections, attachment relationships and notes from Zotero; selecting Zotero's storage directory in Folder Loader does not preserve that library structure.

Import a folder

  1. Choose Loader > Open Loader. In Browser, Ctrl+L focuses its address field; use the menu to open Loader.
  2. Choose the source folder. Review the displayed path before starting.
  3. Select a metadata mode.
    • Skip metadata — fastest; import files and structure only.
    • Quick refresh — recommended for most migrations.
    • Full refresh — more network work and a longer run.
  4. Choose Import. Follow progress in the live log. Use Stop Import if necessary.
  5. Review the result. Open previous logs or the result guide when items need attention.

Follow a folder drop without keeping Loader open

Dropping an external folder into Library starts Folder Loader in the background; it does not need to open the Loader window first. The Library footer shows import progress. Choose Details beside the activity indicators to open the live Loader window, inspect progress and read the log. Closing it leaves the import running, and Details opens it again. When the import has finished, Details still opens the retained result until you choose Dismiss; previous reports remain available in Loader.

Click a log entry linked to a paper to Show in Library. The window closes after the item is revealed, without interrupting the job. General progress messages cannot identify a Library item. Use the footer's Details to return, or Loader > Open Loader to review saved reports. See log navigation and task controls.

Stop Import finishes at the next safe checkpoint, preserves completed files and ends any linked metadata queue. It does not undo the import. The separate Delete Import command has a different, destructive purpose.

What Folder Loader preserves

  • The source folder’s relative hierarchy.
  • Existing managed targets and files on repeated imports.
  • An existing main file rather than overwriting it, plus edited versions with different contents.
  • A verified exported Paper Files relationship when a Gewu Insight manifest is present.

Folder Loader copies into Gewu Insight’s managed storage. It does not move, rename, or delete the external source files and folders you selected. Loader, Paper Details, folder and all-Library refresh use the same service and refresh history. Quick refresh updates core information (title, authors, journal and date) and verified DOI/arXiv links; Full refresh adds detailed authors, citations and other source data. Recovered identifiers use the selected mode. Partial source failures remain visible in the log and are not recorded as a fully successful refresh.

Identity mismatches and partial imports

Loader and File Explorer folder drops share the same matching and file-preservation policy. When a DOI, title or existing identifier disagrees with the matched paper, the incoming file is still saved in its Paper Files and the paper is placed in the target folder. Existing metadata and Default are preserved. PDFs with different bytes but the same DOI are kept as separate files; an exact unchanged copy already owned by that paper reuses its existing resource even after a source rename or move; the import continues without a mandatory review prompt.

The live log and Result Guide identify each mismatch by filename, detected DOI, existing DOI and Gewu Key. Correct a wrong assignment later from the file card's Move to Another Paper or Create Paper from File command. This preserves the PDF; it does not certify that the identified DOI is correct.

A disk or other import error can still stop a batch. Completed items remain available, and the result shows the failing file and actual progress. For a background drop, use the bottom bar's Details to reopen its current result and Dismiss when finished. Previously saved results remain available in Loader logs.

Delete an import batch

Delete Import is a rollback for the selected Loader batch, not a way to forget a log. Stop an active import first. The command removes database records created by that batch, eligible empty folders, its Loader reports, and managed local copies associated with the batch; eligible paths are sent to the Windows Recycle Bin. It never deletes the original external source directory.

ImportantReview the selected batch and make a backup before using Delete Import, especially if you have already reorganized or reused imported items.
NoteFor an ordinary folder, Loader does not guess paper-to-attachment relationships from similar filenames. A verified Gewu Insight export manifest can restore those relationships. After paper identity and ownership are known, the normal Default and Associated Files rules determine where that paper’s managed files belong.

See also

Make a Portable Desktop CopyRefresh Info: One Paper, a Folder, or the LibraryBack Up and Upgrade

Import and Transfer

Import a Zotero Library

Copy a Zotero library or selected collections into your current Gewu Database, with collection hierarchy, Paper Files and readable notes. Zotero's records, original attachments and annotations stay unchanged.

Choose the workflow you meanOpening the Gewu tab in Zotero displays your existing Gewu workspace. It does not import Zotero's own library. Import from Zotero makes an explicit copy from that separate library into Gewu; it is not continuous synchronization.

Before you start

Use a Gewu App with companion 0.4.0 or later and keep Zotero running during preview and import. Check the Windows release notes for tested Zotero versions. Third-party plugin configurations and missing external attachments may need individual review. In the standalone App, Plugin > Zotero Integration shows the bundled and installed versions. Follow its installation guide or use Update Plugin when offered.

Download cloud-only attachments in Zotero first, check that linked files open on this Windows computer, and allow enough free space for independent copies and any exported annotations or notes. You do not need to export a Zotero database or locate its internal storage folders.

Open the importer in either interface

Where you workEntry point
Standalone Gewu InsightWindows menu: Loader > Import from Zotero.
Gewu Insight tab inside ZoteroUpper-right … > Loader > Import from Zotero.

Both open the same importer for the same selected Gewu Database. You do not import once for the App and again for the plugin. Connect Zotero or Reconnect Zotero connects this import session to Zotero's loaded library; it is separate from the workspace's Connection Settings.

Choose scope and destination

  1. Open the importer, choose New import if needed, and click Connect Zotero. Wait for the library choices to appear.
  2. Choose Zotero library. Group libraries appear only when available in your local Zotero profile.
  3. Keep All collections and unfiled items selected to copy the whole library, or clear it and select collections. A selected collection includes its subcollections; unselected ancestors are not added above the selected subtree.
  4. Click Gewu destination. Browse the columns from Library or a Space into the required folder. Read the full path at the bottom and click Confirm. This selects the import target; it does not change your default Save to Gewu destination.
  5. Set Import folder, for example Zotero — My Library. This folder contains the imported hierarchy beneath the selected destination.

Preview, then start the copy

  1. Click Preview Import. This reads the source and prepares a saved preview. It does not create Library papers, collection folders or their disk directories.
  2. Check the source, destination, item count, available attachments and original file size. Expand What's included and read Items to review. Available attachments are local source files, not a promise that every item has a PDF; original file size is not a complete estimate of exported notes and annotated copies.
  3. Repair missing source files or uncertain identities before proceeding. Files or papers deliberately removed from Gewu are not silently recreated. A changed Zotero item or repaired file needs New import and a fresh preview.
  4. When the scope and review results are correct, click Import into Gewu. The importer creates the selected hierarchy and verified copies, then reports completed and unfinished entries.
  5. Inspect the result in the chosen Gewu folder. Check a nested collection and its Paper Files; use File Explorer to inspect the corresponding managed directories if needed.

How collections and files are stored

In ZoteroIn Gewu
Collections and subcollectionsFolders under the import folder, in the same selected hierarchy. Empty collections also become real directories, with matching Associated Files directories, when import starts.
One item in several collectionsOne paper and Gewu Key with several folder memberships. Secondary placements follow Gewu's existing shortcut rules.
Stored or linked attachmentsIndependent, verified copies in Paper Files. The source remains in its original location.
Multiple PDFs and supplementsSeparate Paper Files. The Default file occupies the canonical Library or Space location; other files belong in its mirrored Associated Files bundle. Existing manual Default choices and classifications are retained.
Item without a local PDFA metadata record. Import does not fabricate a DOI or automatically download a missing PDF.
Notes and PDF annotationsReadable notes plus original archives; native PDF annotations can produce a separate annotated PDF and annotation text. Annotations already embedded in a PDF remain in its copied bytes.
Tags, citation keys and extra fieldsPreserved in Zotero Metadata and the migration record. This does not add a new tag editor or reproduce every plugin's interface.

For example, choosing Library / Research as the destination and Zotero — My Library as the import folder places Materials / Empty collection beneath that root both in Gewu and under data / Library / Research / Zotero — My Library / Materials / Empty collection. The matching hierarchy exists under data / Associated Files. A Space target uses its existing Space storage rules. The importer does not clone Zotero's internal storage directory layout. See How Gewu Insight Stores Files for canonical files and secondary aliases.

Original note archives retain richer formatting and embedded assets. Zotero-specific interactive annotation links, saved searches, Trash, sync credentials and plugin settings are not recreated as Gewu controls.

If you use ZotFile, ZotMoov or Attanger

The importer follows the attachment registered in Zotero, including stored files, absolute linked paths and paths relative to its Linked Attachment Base Directory. The arrangement used by a file-management plugin can therefore be imported when the file is registered and locally accessible. It does not scan an unrelated plugin folder, reproduce that folder's arbitrary hierarchy, or claim compatibility with every plugin version.

External tablet or backup copies that are not registered as Zotero attachments are not included. Better Notes content stored as ordinary Zotero notes follows the note mapping; external synchronized Markdown files and custom plugin state are not reconstructed. Fix missing links or legacy Mac aliases in Zotero, then prepare a new preview.

Pause, resume and repeat safely

Pause Import keeps completed copies. Resume Import continues the saved session; Retry Unfinished retries incomplete entries. You can close the window and reopen it through Loader, then choose the session from Import session. After either app or its service restarts, use Reconnect Zotero before resuming.

Repeated imports recognize previously mapped source records and unchanged files; they do not make a second full copy. Mapped folders are reused, while changed file versions may coexist with earlier copies. Later Zotero collection renames or deletions do not rename or delete Gewu folders. Folder Loader's Delete Import belongs to that separate workflow, not this importer.

Source safetyImport copies and verifies files rather than moving Zotero's originals. It does not edit Zotero's library records, transfer away PDF annotations or rewrite linked paths. A blocking file, shortcut or conflicting destination is reported without being overwritten. Manage the resulting Gewu copies through Gewu's normal file controls.

See also

One Workspace, Two InterfacesInstall, Update, and Remove the PluginHow Gewu Insight Stores FilesEdit DOI and arXiv Identifiers

Import and Transfer

Make a Portable Desktop Copy

Make Copy Desktop creates a self-contained copy for transfer, inspection, or re-import.

Create a copy

  1. Right-click the non-root Library folder you want to export.
  2. Choose Make Copy Desktop.
  3. Wait for the completion message. Open the resulting Desktop folder in File Explorer.
  4. Confirm representative files. Check a paper with versions or attachments as well as a normal folder.

What is included

The export replaces managed filesystem shortcuts with real files, includes relevant Associated Files, and writes a verified manifest describing paper-file relationships. This lets Folder Loader restore the bundle on another installation without guessing from filenames.

ImportantDo not edit or discard the export manifest before migration. Without it, Loader correctly treats the files as an ordinary folder and does not infer hidden associations.

See also

Use Folder LoaderBack Up and UpgradeHow Gewu Insight Stores Files

Import and Transfer

Back Up and Upgrade

Back up the selected Gewu Database and keep the installer for your current version. The executable alone is not your Library.

Keep the three locations separate

LocationPurpose
Installed programNormally %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Gewu Insight. Setup updates the application, bundled runtimes and guide.
Selected Gewu DatabaseContains data, reports, config and backups, including SQLite, managed Library/Space files and notes. It stays in place during a program update.
Source checkoutDevelopment code and build tools. Daily use starts the installed App from the Start menu; editing source does not update the installed App.

Create a consistent backup

  1. Use File > Open Gewu Database to find the selected folder. Save website drafts and finish or stop background tasks.
  2. Close the Gewu Insight tab in Zotero first, then open the standalone Gewu App and choose File > Exit. Wait for the App and service to stop. Copy the entire database folder from this closed state, including hidden files, data/paper_monitor.sqlite, any accompanying WAL/SHM files, managed Library/Space files, Associated Files, notes, configuration and backups.
  3. Preserve external originals used by Shortcuts separately. Keep Windows .lnk files intact; a shortcut does not contain its target's bytes. Historical import-source paths are provenance and need not be active file dependencies.
  4. Keep %USERPROFILE%\.gewu-insight\database-location.ini, the current installer and relevant AI-client configuration as separate recovery material. Browser profiles are separate from the research folder.
  5. Verify SQLite integrity, the copied file list and representative files on a separate copy. Store the backup outside the live database and keep the original until the replacement has been checked.

SQLite is authoritative. Copying only JSON exports, the program folder or a database file while it is changing is not a full backup. Do not replace the active database with an older file just to address a display problem.

Update the installed application

After a verified backup, close Gewu Insight and run the newer versioned Setup.exe. Open Gewu Insight from the Start menu, then check the selected data folder, existing papers and file access. Check the application version and build in Help > About Gewu Insight. Windows Settings > Apps also lists the installed version. Keep the previous installer and backup until verification is complete. Do not open the Library with an older incompatible version.

Move a database

For a collection already separate from the program, a routine App update keeps the same folder, identity, Gewu Keys and file classifications. Uninstalling retains research data, the locator and browser sign-ins. A move to another path needs an offline, verified migration of operational file paths and Windows shortcuts; retain the original and do not merge two populated database folders. Do not run the source service and installed App against the same collection.

Browser and credential boundaries

Bookmarks and history are in SQLite. WebView2 website profiles live separately under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Gewu Insight\Databases\<identity>\Browser; logs and cache use the adjacent Logs and Cache folders. The profile is not a portable sign-in export. Expect to sign in again on another computer. Browser tabs and unsent forms are memory-only and are not restored after quitting.

Metadata API keys and AI Access information can be present in workspace data. Keep full backups private. Exporting bookmarks produces bookmark HTML, not cookies, passwords or browsing history.

Transfer selected research files

Use Make a Portable Desktop Copy for a selected collection. Retain its export manifest and use Folder Loader to restore the file relationships. A portable collection is not a full backup of settings, monitor history and the database. Whole-workspace macOS-to-Windows migration requires separate validation of paths and platform files.

Update Gewu Insight for Windows

Windows 1.0.0 has no in-app updater. Download the newer Windows x64 Setup.exe from the project's Releases page, close Gewu and its Zotero tab, and run Setup over the existing program. Keep Use existing Gewu Database and its current folder. You only need this manual upgrade once to obtain the new update feature.

  1. In Windows 1.1.0 or later, choose Help > Check for Updates. The updater reads the stable Windows channel. Mac releases and prereleases are not Windows update candidates.
  2. If a newer version is available, choose Download Update. Gewu verifies the complete file size and SHA-256 before offering installation. Closing the update window cancels an unfinished download.
  3. Close the Gewu tab in Zotero, pause a Zotero import if one is running, and let downloads and file operations finish. Choose Install Update. If work is still active, Gewu keeps the current App open and asks you to retry later.
  4. Gewu stops its service and opens Windows Setup. Follow its normal pages, retain the existing program and database locations, and leave Open Gewu Insight selected on the final page.

Check automatically once a day checks when the standalone App starts and the last check was at least 24 hours ago. It announces available updates; it does not automatically download or install them. Turn it off in the Software Update window to use only manual checks. If the network check fails, retry later; a failed check does not mean the App is up to date.

Updating replaces program files, not your Gewu Database or original PDFs. Keep a recovery backup before upgrading. Windows packages remain unsigned; checksum verification checks the downloaded bytes against the project update feed and is not a Windows publisher signature.

Update Plugin in Plugin > Zotero Integration is a separate action. It installs the companion bundled with your current Gewu App. After a program update, use it only if the integration window offers a newer plugin.

See also

Make a Portable Desktop CopyStorage ReferenceTroubleshooting

Publications and Monitors

Use My Publications

My Publications keeps a managed publication list, citation sources, author-role statistics, and export tools for your own work.

Choose your profile

  1. Enter a name, optional affiliations, or an exact Google Scholar profile URL. For a name search, use Name; affiliation A; affiliation B.
  2. Choose Find Profile. Review candidate profiles carefully.
  3. Choose Use Profile to review candidates individually, or Add All Publications to import the complete profile. The saved strip shows the active name and profile photo. Select the photo to open the profile using Website Links; use the remove control to forget it.

Already have the paper in Library? Right-click its row and choose Add to My Publications. Multiple selected papers can be added together. The publication list and Library then refer to the same work, files, and Gewu Key.

Add all publications or choose individual papers

Use Profile opens a candidate list where each article retains its own Add button. To import the author's entire profile, choose Add All Publications beside the correct search profile or at the top of its article candidate list. These controls appear only inside the search/add area; the normal publication table keeps its original layout. The complete import reads successive source pages until the profile ends; it is independent of the 200-title candidate preview and has no 300- or 5,000-paper cutoff. Existing canonical articles and My Publications entries are reused.

The bottom status bar continuously shows active import counts and DOI/arXiv progress, including running, processed, paused, and retry-needed states. Completed imports move into Import history, which distinguishes original import counts from articles currently saved in My Publications. When only history remains, the footer entry reads History. Old imports do not appear in a new author search; its own status or error stays visible in the search panel. Choose Details in that bar to view full progress and import controls without searching again. The search/add panel opens when searching or choosing a profile and stays open until you choose its Close button; clicking a publication or completing a task does not dismiss it. Closing the panel keeps background work running and preserves the table position. Pause Import preserves completed work; Continue Import resumes it. An interrupted source page is retried without adding its successful articles twice. A blocked, unreadable, repeated, or interrupted source page is reported as incomplete with a short reason and guidance to try again later. Technical connection details stay in the diagnostic log. Individual identity conflicts do not stop later articles and remain reported for review and retry. Adding all again after completion explicitly checks the profile from its first page for additional articles.

Both individual Add and Add All automatically queue missing DOI/arXiv identifiers. Articles are saved first, and identifier completion runs separately in the background. Its progress distinguishes matched, unmatched, failed, and pending work. Switching tabs does not stop either task; unfinished work resumes after app restart. Identifier updates preserve the article's Gewu Key and file relationships. The existing per-candidate Retry ID remains available. When saved articles have unmatched or failed identifiers, Retry Unresolved IDs appears with progress inside the search/add area. Pausing the profile import does not pause identifier work already queued. Articles without a confident match remain saved. This operation does not automatically download PDFs.

After Scholar reports an access restriction, Gewu Insight applies a shared 24-hour pause to Scholar requests. The prompt shows the local retry time; this is an application pause, not a Google-provided IP-ban deadline. Changing authors or restarting does not clear it.

Add and update publications

  • Use the identifier/title field and Add to add a DOI, arXiv record, supported identifier, or title.
  • Choose Refresh Metrics to update citation services and PubMed data.
  • First as listed is calculated automatically from the active profile name and the resolved author order, including the profile's English and Chinese name forms.
  • Use Co-1st, Co-corr., and Rev. in Paper Details to mark co-first authorship, corresponding authorship, and review/perspective papers. Leave Co-1st unchecked for a solo first-author paper. These manual roles are preserved during metric refresh.
  • Use the star to highlight a paper. Star state is independent from citation refresh and export inclusion.
  • Drag rows into a manual order when a curated sequence matters more than date or citation sorting.
  • Choose Comments to build or open a citation-comments report from citing-paper metadata. This is not a personal note field.
  • Use Hide or Show in the context menu to control export inclusion. Use Open in File Explorer or Delete for the corresponding local action.

Edit manual records and author marks

A publication without either a DOI or arXiv identifier exposes Manual Metadata. Edit Title, Authors, Journal, Date, Volume, Issue, and Pages, then choose Save Metadata. Separate author names with semicolons or new lines. Once an identifier is present, use identifier-based metadata controls instead.

Select an author name in the publication's author list to inspect affiliations and set First author, Co-first author, or Corresponding author for that named author. Checkbox changes save immediately. These individual author marks are separate from the publication's Co-1st, Co-corr., and Rev. summary controls.

Build a citation-comments report

Comments gathers citing-paper metadata and available Semantic Scholar citation-context sentences, then writes a local report that groups strong praise, positive impact statements, cautions, and unmatched citing records. It helps you review how later literature describes a publication; it does not modify the publication metadata or replace your own notes.

The report is a generated local reading artifact. Network services may return fewer contexts than citation records, and a temporary rate limit can leave some entries without quoted context. Reopen or rebuild the report later to retry the available sources; an existing report remains on disk until you deliberately replace or remove it.

Work with files

My Publications uses the same Paper Details and flat Paper Files model as Library. Expand Files · n within the details to inspect its resources; Library instead has an adjacent Paper Files column. The publication Files panel shows File type, Annotation, and Source controls directly; the size-footer expansion belongs to Library cards. A publication can keep a default PDF, earlier versions, supplements, notes, presentations, data, and other attachments under the same Gewu Key.

Read the summary

The lower summary includes publication counts, identifier coverage, h-index and i10 information, journal distribution, merged citation maxima, and major-paper role counts. Select a role statistic to filter the table where supported.

Export a list

Choose Export List, then select LaTeX PDF, LaTeX source, Overleaf project ZIP, or Word document. Papers excluded from export remain visible in My Publications but are omitted from the generated list. The export follows the current visible table, including its search, role/journal filters, and row order, and excludes rows marked Hide. Clear filters and search first if you want the full included list. Exporting never replaces the SQLite source.

The Overleaf option creates a project ZIP, copies it to the Desktop, and opens Overleaf using Website Links. The status message reports the saved path. It does not upload your files or create an Overleaf project automatically; import the ZIP yourself on the website.

See where a reordered row will land

When dragging a publication to change its manual order, a translucent copy follows the pointer. A blue circle and horizontal line mark the insertion position. The other rows stay in place during the drag; release to apply the order. This changes the publication list order, not the paper’s file location.

See also

Literature Data SourcesUse Paper DetailsLocal Data and Privacy

Publications and Monitors

Use Journal Monitor

Journal Monitor collects papers for a selected publication date and lets you narrow the result by journal, preprint source, and field.

Refresh a date

  1. Select a day in the calendar. Small numbers below a day show stored result counts.
  2. Choose Refresh. The app requests all configured journal sources for that date.
  3. Right-click the journal in Journal Filter and use Refresh This Journal when only that journal needs another attempt. This avoids re-requesting journals that are already complete.
  4. Choose arXiv separately if needed. This keeps journal and preprint work explicit.
  5. Watch the bottom status area. It reports the current source and completion without changing the page height.

Manage monitored journals

Open Journal Settings to add or manage a journal by name, ISSN, or known publication history. When an ISSN is missing, the app can look up a matching journal record before saving it. Review the match rather than relying on a similar title alone.

Drag journals vertically in Journal Filter or Journal Settings to set their order. The saved order controls the filter list and the journal groups in the report. Removing a journal disables the subscription without erasing its previously collected papers or its saved history.

Your enabled list, disabled history, ISSNs, source identifier, section policy, logo source, and display order are saved in SQLite. Product updates can add better built-in source definitions, but those defaults do not replace this personal state. Adding a previously removed journal restores it at the end of the active order.

Understand counts and filters

The count beside a journal in the left Journal Filter is its stored total for the selected day, independent of Field Filter. The journal tabs above the cards count the currently visible papers after filtering. Monitor Summary distinguishes total from shown. A left-side journal count can therefore be nonzero while the current fields hide all its cards. Counts describe results; blue dots describe unread state.

Calendar counts summarize stored day results. A zero count is meaningful only after the relevant source completed successfully. Read the source status before interpreting zero as “the journal published nothing.”

Blue dots follow the papers you select

Late-arriving discoveries can have an unread blue dot. Click an individual paper or use Up/Down to select it with the keyboard to mark that paper read. Opening a date, journal or subject, changing fields, refreshing, or automatically highlighting the first card does not mark the whole list read.

A journal or subject tab's blue dot counts only unread papers currently visible under its filters. It disappears after all those visible papers are read. Hidden papers keep their own unread state; if you change fields or another filter to reveal them, the tab's dot can return. Read state is shared for the same paper between Journal and Subject Monitor. Author Monitor retains its separate New and Read All workflow.

The calendar runs Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday. Small numbers show stored results, not unread totals. The late-arrivals section links to earlier publication dates whose results arrived later; it is separate from publication notices.

Daily scheduled updates

Journal Monitor is designed to keep a daily cached record through its scheduled update workflow. A scheduled run and a manual refresh use the same stored day results, so opening a date does not require downloading it again. Use a manual refresh when a scheduled source was missed, partial, or needs verification.

The scheduler belongs to the running local UI service; it does not wake a sleeping computer or run while that service is stopped. See When automatic updates run for the current timing and restart boundaries.

Journal logos and mathematical text

Configured journal logos are downloaded into a local cache and reused from disk. The first successful request may require network access; changing dates and later launches should not repeatedly download the same logo. The cache is presentation data and can be rebuilt without changing subscriptions or papers.

Supported inline LaTeX in titles and abstracts is typeset after the math renderer becomes ready. On a cold launch, raw source may be visible briefly, then the current day is rendered again automatically; changing to another date and back should not be necessary. Title normalization also preserves recognized proper names and source capitalization such as Su–Schrieffer–Heeger and Monte Carlo while still cleaning all-uppercase metadata and formula spacing.

How discovery provenance is preserved

Each stored Journal result is related to the canonical paper, the fetch run, and the source that reported it. The run preserves the journal, requested date window, status, and timing. Seeing the same paper from Crossref and OpenAlex records both source observations against the same paper identity; seeing it again within one run does not create a duplicate relationship. Later runs remain separately traceable.

The same canonical paper can also acquire Subject Monitor and Author Monitor relationships. These discovery paths explain why the work is visible; they do not automatically add a Library placement or create a local Paper Files resource.

Filter and inspect

Use Journal Filter, Preprint Filter, and Field Filter. Journal and field choices combine to determine the visible cards, while the left Journal Filter counts continue to describe the full selected day. Enable Figures to show a representative image when available. Selecting a result opens its report and actions.

Act on a result

  • Open Website opens the publisher or best known record using Website Links: a new built-in Browser tab by default, or the Windows default browser when selected.
  • Add to Library begins the placement workflow described below; after that, Show in Library returns to the managed paper.
  • Download retrieves the paper file. PDF opens an existing local PDF in Preview, and Delete PDF removes that managed download and resets its status.
  • When a reading note exists, Note opens it in the right-side drawer. The list compresses but keeps its own scroll position. Delete Note removes the note and resets analysis status.

Read an existing Note

Note appears when a reading note has already been generated. It opens the saved note on demand in a right-side drawer; the report area compresses and each side scrolls independently. Drag the divider to resize the note. Hide list gives the note more space; Show list restores the report. Closing the drawer keeps the note. Delete Note is a separate action that removes it and resets its analysis status. Links in the note follow Website Links.

Add a Journal result to Library

  1. Choose Add to Library on the result. The Library destination chooser opens without leaving the selected date.
  2. Choose the target Library folder. This is the visible folder placement for the managed paper.
  3. Complete the add. The card changes to Show in Library; use it to reveal the existing placement later.

The operation links the Journal discovery to the canonical paper, preserves its source and run provenance, and adds the chosen Library placement. It does not automatically download a PDF. Choose Download separately when you also want a local file. If the paper is already managed, Show in Library reveals it instead of creating a duplicate identity.

Per-paper status text and the bottom progress area make completed downloads and background work visible, which helps avoid repeating the same action.

Note“No matching papers” and “source fetch failed” are different outcomes. Check the source status before concluding that a date is empty.

The destination chooser initially selects your Settings > Add to Library default, initially Library / unsorted. You can confirm another active Library or Space folder for this addition. The choice does not change the global default.

Journal tabs identify the journal by a supported wordmark or by text. APS titles, including Physical Review Letters, Physical Review X and Reviews of Modern Physics, use readable journal names rather than a publisher icon or a page image.

Review corrections and retractions

Publication updates is a collapsed section in the left sidebar below Monitor Summary and any late-arrivals section. Expand it to see notices for the selected publication date. Both its count and list follow Journal Filter and Field Filter. A linked notice uses the original article's fields; an unresolved notice uses its retained classification. With no matching notices, the section is hidden.

  1. Choose Open Website to inspect the notice and its original-article relation.
  2. Choose Add to Library on the notice to associate it with the original work. An existing original retains its Gewu Key. If absent, Gewu can retrieve the explicitly identified original's metadata and create its paper record without a PDF.
  3. Read the result below the action, then inspect the original's Paper Files. The notice keeps its DOI, title, date and kind; it does not receive an independent research-paper Key. This action does not automatically download its PDF.

Missing or conflicting relations stop the association for review; a similar title alone is insufficient. The notice does not replace the original bibliography or Default. Encountering a notice during discovery does not stop processing the journal's later research articles. To check an older saved paper directly, use Refresh Info.

See also

Subject MonitorPublisher and Network AccessAdd Papers and Files

Publications and Monitors

Use Subject Monitor

Subject Monitor discovers papers for reusable topics. Each subject stores a name and literal discovery terms; an optional copied prompt can help you draft those terms outside the app.

Create a subject

  1. Choose Add Subject.
  2. Enter a clear name and discovery keywords. Describe the field broadly enough to find variants, but avoid unrelated general terms.
  3. Use Copy Suggested Prompt if you want Codex-assisted wording. Review the prompt before using it.
  4. Save and arrange the subject. Subjects can be edited, deleted, and reordered.

Keywords use case-insensitive literal matching. Enter the words or phrases you expect to appear; they are not regular expressions and are not silently expanded into unrelated concepts.

Edit keywords without losing history

Right-click a subject and choose Edit. Saving a new name or keywords keeps its existing paper list, calendar counts, selection, and reading position. New keywords apply to future retrieval. Existing date windows, including empty and incomplete results, remain preserved after a keyword change; background retries and later local arXiv matching do not silently reclassify those windows.

Choose Refresh This Subject explicitly to rebuild that subject's selected date with the current keywords. A successful refresh replaces only that result window; other dates and subjects remain unchanged. An incomplete refresh preserves previous results. Editing during an active retrieval discards the obsolete result instead of replacing history. Deleting a subject still clears its Subject Monitor matches, without deleting the underlying shared papers or Library files. Previously cleared matches from an older software version are not automatically reconstructed by this fix.

Keep one subject selected across dates

Selecting a subject makes it the active topic until you choose another one. Moving to a date with no result does not switch the tab back to the first subject, and a subject with zero papers remains selectable. The calendar's day numbers describe the active subject, so you can see which dates contain papers for that topic rather than a total across every subject. The count beside each subject tab describes that subject on the selected date.

The calendar shows the stored count as a number, including 0, for the selected subject and date. Counts have no completeness marker. A date with no stored results and no fetch record remains blank. While a fetch is running, the progress indicator remains visible.

The Discovery row describes the recorded retrieval status for the selected subject. A completed retrieval is not a guarantee that every relevant paper has been found. Switching subjects changes the counts and recorded status; reopening the app preserves the status stored in SQLite.

Refresh subjects

  1. Select a calendar date. Selecting a date only loads the result already stored for that day; it does not start a network request.
  2. Choose Refresh. The command refreshes every configured subject for the currently selected date. The arXiv display option is enabled by default; clear it when you want to hide arXiv cards without changing what is stored.
  3. Read source status. A source can be complete, partial, empty, or failed. Source-level retries are managed by the background scheduler.
  4. Cancel if necessary. Completed results remain distinguishable from unfinished work.

Refresh one subject

Right-click a subject and choose Refresh This Subject when only that topic needs another pass. Use the main Refresh command when every configured subject should run for the selected date.

The current candidate layer can draw from local arXiv data, local APS RSS data, OpenAlex, Crossref, Semantic Scholar, and PubMed. It does not depend on a fixed number of feeds. Results still pass topic filtering and deduplication before display.

Inspect and keep a result

Select a paper to read its title, authors, abstract, source, date, identifier, topic score, and matched subject terms. Use Open Website, Download, PDF, and the note controls in the same way as Journal Monitor. Choose Add to Library to create a managed reference, or Show in Library when one already exists.

Add a Subject result to Library

  1. Choose Add to Library on the matching paper. The subject and selected date remain in place while the destination chooser opens.
  2. Select the target Library folder. The same canonical paper can be placed in a durable topic hierarchy without losing the Subject relationship.
  3. Complete the add. Use Show in Library on later visits to reveal the managed placement.

Adding the result preserves the matched subject, score, terms, and discovery provenance. The paper remains visible in Subject Monitor immediately after adding it; its action becomes Show in Library, while the selected subject, date, and reading position stay in place. It does not automatically download a PDF; use Download separately. Repeated discovery of the same identity updates relationships rather than creating unrelated paper records.

ImportantSubject Monitor rejects Zenodo records during ingestion and when cached results are displayed. There is no Zenodo show/hide option.

The destination chooser initially selects your Settings > Add to Library default, initially Library / unsorted. You can confirm another active Library or Space folder for this addition. The choice does not change the global default.

Read state, calendar and publication notices

The calendar runs Sunday first through Saturday last. Its counts remain plain numbers for the selected subject. Selecting an individual paper by mouse or Up/Down acknowledges that paper only; opening the topic or date does not acknowledge all its papers. A subject or journal tab's blue dot reflects only its currently visible unread papers. Hidden results remain unread and can restore the dot when shown. See the shared Journal/Subject rules.

Subject ingestion separates recognized correction and retraction notices from ordinary research-paper candidates and continues processing later results. Notices do not acquire independent research-paper Keys. The expandable Publication updates panel described in this guide is in Journal Monitor; for a saved original use Refresh Info and Paper Files.

See also

Journal MonitorPublisher and Network Access

Publications and Monitors

Use Author Monitor

Author Monitor follows researchers and separates a first-import baseline from newly discovered work.

Add an author

  1. Choose the add-author control.
  2. Enter a name and optional affiliations, or an exact profile URL. Google Scholar and ResearchGate profile URLs are supported where the profile can be resolved.
  3. Confirm the correct person. The initial result set becomes the baseline rather than a batch of unread “new” papers.

Understand profile and publication sources

Google Scholar profiles refresh through Scholar with shared pacing and cooldown. A ResearchGate URL identifies the public profile; its publications are matched separately through OpenAlex when configured. If unavailable, Gewu Insight automatically falls back to Semantic Scholar. Confirm the proposed person, especially for similar names.

Without a verified publication-data match, the ResearchGate profile and homepage can be saved, but automatic publication refresh remains unavailable. Profile, publication, and citation sources remain distinct evidence; a fallback does not change the author identity.

Reorder monitored authors

Drag an author in the left list to change its order. A translucent preview follows the pointer, and a blue circle with a horizontal line shows where it will be inserted. Other authors stay in place until you release. The order does not change the author’s profile source or publication records.

Review updates

Later refreshes can mark newly discovered publications as unread. Use the New filter and other author/result controls to focus the list. Select Date or Citations to sort; selecting the active sort reverses its direction. Conferences · n opens conference publications in a separate, independently scrolling popover, so they are not missing from the ordinary article list. Close the popover with its close control or Escape.

Right-click New and choose Read All. For one selected author, it marks every unread publication as read, including offscreen papers; other authors keep their unread state, even for a shared paper. With All Authors selected, it marks all authors' new publications as read. Papers and Library placements are preserved. The New filter remains active; click New again to see read papers. Read state persists after reopening.

Background work and status

Opening this tab reuses available local cards, including older cached lists, while the background checks for changes. It does not start another Scholar fetch. Background list updates retain your selection, reading position, open controls and details.

The bottom bar keeps publication checks separate from Author metadata · All authors. Checking status... means that these summary counts are still loading; it does not mean all papers are being repaired. Metadata counts cover all monitored authors, not just the selected author, and are recalculated from current missing information even during a daily pause. Ready work, retry waits and papers needing manual lookup are distinct; hover over shortened text for its full message.

Automatic DOI and abstract completion uses other metadata services, independently of Scholar profile checks. It rotates between authors and reuses shared paper identities: up to 20 papers per batch and 80 per local day, yielding between papers after about two minutes and resting at least five minutes between batches. Recent attempts wait seven days before automatic retry, with at most three automatic attempts per paper. Papers still unresolved then need manual lookup; completed papers are not periodically refreshed. Progress reservations and rest times survive restarting; explicit identifier commands remain available separately.

Scholar requests remain serialized, with 4–8 seconds between requests, 12–24 seconds between profile pages and 45–90 seconds between automatic author checks. Every request checks the shared workspace cooldown again before sending, including My Publications imports. Access restrictions pause Scholar for 24 hours; manual actions and restarts do not bypass or reset that pause. This is Gewu's protective waiting period, not a promised unblock time from Google.

A red Google Scholar paused message means the shared Scholar access cooldown is active. New restriction messages may identify HTTP 403, HTTP 429 or a verification page; an older generic message may lack that detail. A VPN exit can affect access, but the pause text alone cannot identify the cause. Changing networks or restarting does not clear the saved waiting period. Cached papers and non-Scholar metadata sources remain available.

A refresh reports identity review

If one publication conflicts with an existing identity, the refresh preserves existing papers and files and continues with the remaining publications. The result reports how many need review and identifies the first affected record, Gewu Key and reason. Read the full message before editing: incomplete identity evidence, contradictory metadata and a protected merge are different cases. Compare the title, authors and identifiers; do not delete files or create another copy to silence the warning. A review message can persist after the refresh finishes and is not itself a running repair task.

Recover after a network interruption

A temporary connection failure shows Google Scholar temporarily unavailable in the bottom bar. Hover over it for the author, error and retry details. Cached publications remain available.
