After the connection returns, keep the App running: failed transport requests have a paced automatic retry queue, including before the normal 10:00 daily check. The message clears after a successful retry, not immediately when Wi-Fi reconnects.

An unreadable Scholar publication list is a failed check, not evidence of no publications. Saved papers and the last successful check are retained. Automatic checks stop probing other Scholar authors in that pass, wait an hour, and allow at most three unsuccessful page probes per day before waiting for the next daily check. An access restriction has its separate cooldown. You can use Refresh This Author for a deliberate retry when permitted.

Refresh one author or find missing identifiers

Right-click the author and choose Refresh This Author to update that person's publications. Find Missing Identifiers checks eligible papers for that author. To check only one unidentified paper, Right-click the paper and choose Find Missing Identifier; it is disabled when an identifier already exists or a lookup is running. These online lookups differ from Get DOI, which uses an available local PDF.

Update citation profiles

For a Google Scholar author, use the circular arrow beside the name or Right-click the author and choose Update All Scholar Citations. Review the request estimate, then confirm Update All Citations. This rereads only that author’s Scholar profile, updates citation counts and discovers new publications. It does not start a Library-wide metadata refresh. Follow the bottom progress status until it finishes.

Manage the profile image

Right-click an author and choose Edit Homepage to edit the website, or Change Photo / Add Photo to choose a local portrait. Downloaded Scholar avatars are saved locally. Opening the author list does not need to reopen SQLite or contact the image host for every row; a manual photo takes precedence. Without a valid local photo, the list can show initials until you refresh or replace the image.

Discovery entries and managed papers

An Author Monitor result is a cataloged shared record, with a Gewu Key shown in its details even before it has Library placements or local files. A missing key displays (undefined) until record data is available. Add to Library preserves the existing key and updates the view; downloading or attaching a file creates a resource relationship.

When repeated discoveries identify the same work

Stable Scholar entries, normalized DOI and version-independent arXiv identities are reused across discovery and later metadata updates. When two existing records are safely confirmed as one work, Author Monitor keeps one card for that author. The same paper can still appear under several different authors. Unread state is retained if either repeated entry was unread.

Reconciliation preserves Library and publication relationships, source history, registered files, classification and manual Default. Old Gewu Keys continue to resolve to the surviving paper. Contradictory manual identifiers, competing manual Default choices or insufficient identity evidence keep records separate for review. A shared DOI is not permission to indiscriminately merge every historical duplicate; startup performs no historical merge sweep.

Add an author result to Library

  1. Select the publication and choose Add to Library. This opens the Library destination chooser without removing the author from view.
  2. Choose the target Library folder. The selected placement becomes the durable organizational path for the shared paper record.
  3. Complete the add. The action becomes Show in Library, which reveals the managed paper later.

The author-publication relationship and canonical identity remain intact. Adding a placement does not automatically download a PDF, and a paper already managed elsewhere is reused rather than duplicated.

Remove a monitored author

Right-click the author and choose Remove from Monitor. Removing an author deletes the monitoring relationship and its monitor state. It does not delete papers already added to Library, their managed PDFs, or their Paper Files bundles.

NoteGoogle Scholar requests are paced and protected by a cooldown. Repeated manual refreshes during a block do not improve the result.

The destination chooser initially selects your Settings > Add to Library default, initially Library / unsorted. You can confirm another active Library or Space folder for this addition. The choice does not change the global default.

See also

My PublicationsPublisher and Network AccessLocal Data and Privacy

Browser

Browse, Bookmark, and Revisit Websites

Browser is the sixth main tab, after Author Monitor. By default, website links across Library, My Publications and all three Monitors switch here, opening a new webpage tab without replacing existing pages. This includes Open Website and Google Scholar links. Choose Settings > Website Links to use the system default browser instead.

Search and navigate

  1. Open Browser. On first use, Home displays your local Favorites folder. Later switches return to your selected webpage; use Home to return to Favorites. A paper link opens its destination directly in the unused first tab. No Google webpage is loaded for Home.
  2. Use the address field. Enter a website address or search terms. Plain search terms go to Google; an address opens directly. Use Ctrl+L to focus the field.
  3. Navigate normally. Back, Forward, Reload/Stop, and Home act on the selected tab. Home uses the content area for Favorites; websites, search results, sign-in pages and PDFs use it for browsing.
  4. Switch between workspaces. Returning from Library or a Monitor preserves the current page and browsing position without reloading merely because the main tab changed.

Return to the source workspace: Ctrl+[. After a website link in Library, My Publications, Journal Monitor, Subject Monitor, or Author Monitor brings you here, press Ctrl+left bracket to return to that workspace's retained selection and scroll position. The physical left-bracket key also works with a Chinese input method selected. It works from the webpage or address field and leaves Browser tabs open; it is not webpage Back. Each linked webpage tab retains its own source for this App session, including related PDF tabs. Switching tabs selects the corresponding return destination. Library links retain the original paper and occurrence; an unrelated address entered in the toolbar clears that tab’s association. Entering Browser directly does not create a source. Close any open dialog first.

Local Home, online search. Favorites is available without loading Google, even after restarting the App. Home has no Google logo, search box or account controls; use the toolbar address field to search. Reload on Home refreshes local bookmarks, not a website. Site icons may need a connection; missing icons show initials. Webpages and sign-in remain online and share Browser's existing profile.

When you search or follow a link from Home, Home remains visible while the destination begins loading, then gives way to that destination. It should not flash the page you visited before Home. A cancelled or failed pending navigation leaves Home available rather than presenting that older page as the result.

Ctrl+F opens Find on Page. Enter selects the next match and Shift+Enter the previous match. Browser is part of the Windows desktop application; a separately hosted web UI does not embed a second browser engine.

Favorites on Home. Favorites/Favourites (including localized names) supplies the tiles; use Create Favorites Folder if missing. Open nested folders and return through breadcrumbs; use Add Favorite or right-click to edit. The grid uses the whole main area, without a Google section or divider. Excess tiles use Previous/Next, not vertical scrolling. Bottom bars align; hiding the sidebar keeps Favorites visible. Opening google.com explicitly shows an ordinary webpage, without Home-specific styling or zoom. Bookmarks are not sent to Google.

Use multiple webpage tabs

Below the address toolbar, adjoining rectangular tabs show × at the far left of each tab, with its icon and title centered together, above the webpage column only. The sidebar begins directly below the toolbar; it is not pushed down by the webpage tabs. The top-right + (New Tab, Ctrl+T) opens Home. Switching preserves each page, position and Back/Forward history without reloading or stopping background loads.

Right-click a webpage link and choose Open Link in New Tab. Bookmarks, Favorites and History provide Open in New Tab in their context menus. Ordinary clicks open in the current tab; new-window links can create another tab.

× or Ctrl+W closes a tab; closing the last opens Home. Left/Right switches focused tabs. Up to 32 tabs stay in memory, not restored after App quit. Save drafts before closing; bookmarks, history, downloads and sign-ins remain.

Save and organize bookmarks

The sidebar's top tabs switch between Bookmarks and History, without a repeated heading. The compact B (Bookmarks menu), + (New Folder), and Search sit along the bottom, even at the minimum sidebar width. History shows Clear History and Search there instead. Drag the sidebar's right edge to resize it or use the toolbar to collapse it. Width, tab, and expanded folders are saved locally.

  1. Add a page. Use the bookmark toolbar button, Share > Add Bookmark, or Ctrl+D. The native sheet starts with the page title and address.
  2. Choose a location. Edit the name or address and choose a folder under Add to. The previous destination is remembered. Saving the same address in the same folder reuses the existing bookmark.
  3. Create nested folders. Use New Folder, or right-click a folder to create a child folder. The editor can also rename a folder or choose another parent.
  4. Arrange the tree. Drag an item into the middle of a folder row to move it inside, or to a row edge to reorder it. Drop on the top Bookmarks tab to move to the root. A folder cannot move inside itself or its descendants.
  5. Save by dragging. Drag the website icon beside the address field, or a webpage link, into a bookmark folder. Confirm the name and destination in the same native sheet.

Search filters bookmark names and addresses. Right-click a bookmark for Open, Edit Bookmark, or Delete. Deleting a folder requires confirmation and removes its contained bookmarks, not websites, browsing history, downloaded files, or papers. A bookmark is a saved link, not an offline webpage copy.

Import and export bookmarks

Choose B > Import at the bottom of Bookmarks and select a Safari or Chrome bookmark HTML file. Safari versions with File > Export Bookmarks produce HTML; newer Safari versions may use File > Export Browsing Data to File and produce ZIP. Select bookmarks only when exporting. Gewu accepts a ZIP containing exactly one bookmark HTML file and ignores all other members. In Chrome, use Bookmark Manager > menu > Export Bookmarks.

Imports go into Imported Bookmarks, retaining folders, order, names, and supported links. Repeating an import merges matching folder names and reuses the same URL in the same folder; existing bookmarks are not overwritten. The result reports added bookmarks, new folders, duplicates, and skipped links. Local addresses, application links, and recognized authorization links are skipped. Limits are 10 MB, 20,000 source entries, and 64 folder levels; invalid files do not partially import.

B > Export saves the full tree as standard bookmark HTML; right-click a folder for Export Folder. Safari and Chrome can import this format. Exports contain no history, cookies, or passwords, but their bookmark names and URLs are readable by anyone with the file. Keep personal exports private.

Sync one source folder into Gewu

  1. Choose B > Sync from Chrome. This is a manual, one-way operation; it does not watch the source or write changes back to Chrome.
  2. Select Chrome's Bookmarks file from the intended local profile, normally under %LOCALAPPDATA%/Google/Chrome/User Data/Default/ or a Profile directory. Only that selected file is read. Choose its folder/subtree, then confirm the manual one-way sync.
  3. Choose one folder. The next sheet lists source folder paths and bookmark counts. Sync Selected Folder includes that folder and its descendants, not its siblings or the whole profile. Cancel leaves Gewu bookmarks unchanged.
  4. Review the result. New links and folders are added. Stable source identifiers allow later source title/address changes to update entries created by sync. Pre-existing matches and items edited or moved in Gewu are kept. Source deletions do not delete local bookmarks. The result reports additions, updates, local changes kept, and skipped links.

The selected folder is placed at the Bookmarks root; matching folder names and same-folder URLs are reused. Sync tracking lives in SQLite, independently of papers and website sessions. Legacy source entries without stable identifiers merge by folder/name/URL rather than overwriting local edits. Switching source files or profiles is a separate source. Limits match import (10 MB, 20,000 entries, 64 levels), with at most 2,000 folders in the chooser. Invalid input or a failed transaction leaves no partial sync.

Windows supports manual Sync from Chrome using one selected local bookmark file and subtree. Safari source sync is not offered. Import an exported bookmark HTML file when no supported local source is available; source files are not modified.

Navigate Browser with arrows

From the top Browser workspace tab, press Down to enter the toolbar. Left/Right moves among available toolbar controls; Enter activates one. At the address field, Enter or typing starts editing; its arrows then edit text or browse address suggestions. Escape returns to the toolbar. Up from the toolbar returns to the top Browser tab, where Left/Right changes workspaces. The Library exception is unchanged: Up within Library content does not ascend to its top workspace tab.

Down from the toolbar selects the current webpage tab. Left/Right selects adjacent webpage tabs; Down enters Favorites or the native webpage. Favorites uses directional tile selection and Enter to open. At the left edge, Left enters the visible sidebar on its currently active Bookmarks/History tab; Down traverses its list and footer controls. Right returns to the main area. A hidden sidebar is never selected. In the sidebar header, Left focuses the other collection tab and Enter activates it.

Inside an ordinary webpage, arrows remain WebView2 scrolling controls. Once Up reaches the document top, it can hand focus back to webpage tabs; two more Up presses reach the top Browser tab. Left at a document's left boundary can enter the visible sidebar. Inputs, editable text, framed/PDF content, and recognized or uncertain custom widgets keep their own keys; no form values are read or filled. A boundary check runs only after an eligible arrow press, without background polling. Use Ctrl+L, then Escape, to return to the toolbar from a document that retains its own arrows.

Website icons

Bookmarks, Favorites and webpage tabs use a disposable local icon cache, separate from SQLite. Icons come directly from sites (at most two concurrent requests), without cookies, credentials, whole-article fetching or third-party icon services. Visits may supply a nonstandard icon URL. Missing icons use globes or Home initials; bookmark lists are never sent to an icon service.

Revisit and clear history

History groups loaded main pages by Today, Yesterday, and date, with names, sites, visit times, search, and pagination. Subresources, main-tab switches, and cached Home returns add no visits; Reload updates the existing record. Click to revisit; right-click to bookmark or delete a visit.

Clear History confirms Last hour, Last 24 hours, Last 7 days, or All history. It preserves bookmarks, downloads, cookies, and sign-ins. History remains until deleted; authorization callbacks and recognized signed-download URLs are excluded.

Address suggestions from your history

As you type in the toolbar address field, Gewu searches saved local visit titles and URLs. Address prefixes rank first, followed by matching titles; visit frequency and recency help order the results. A matching address can complete the typed prefix with its remaining text selected. These are local history suggestions, not live Google suggestions, and typing does not send a suggestion request to a search engine.

Use ↑/↓, then Enter to open a result, or click it to open directly. Escape dismisses suggestions and restores your typed query. Without a chosen completion, Enter opens an address or searches Google normally. Clearing history also removes those visits from suggestions; bookmark search remains a separate sidebar control.

Read PDFs and save downloads

Viewable PDFs stay inline, including attachment/download links, with article/PDF Back/Forward navigation. In a publisher's HTML viewer, click its PDF download link: Browser receives the PDF using its current website session and opens it in that tab, including supported page-generated files. Opening PDF… shows progress. Switching tabs does not interrupt it or let completion take focus; leaving the source page or closing its tab cancels that pending preview. Website sign-in and consent pages remain visible.

Preview uses temporary browser storage, not your Downloads folder or Library. PDF attachment previews accept up to 128 MB and two minutes per transfer. Save to Gewu and the bottom-right Save Download arrow reuse a complete loaded PDF; they do not silently download it again. Both the bottom-right arrow and the PDF viewer’s own download arrow open a native save dialog, initially in Downloads. Confirm the filename and destination to write the file; Cancel leaves it unsaved. Original-file copies are temporary and bounded; navigating to another document or closing its tab releases them. To import a PDF, use Save to Gewu below or import a saved file. Library PDFs still open in the Windows default PDF application.

Choose the right save action

ActionResult
Save DownloadSave the browser file to a location such as Downloads. This alone adds no Library placement or Paper Files record.
Save to GewuReview the article, optional PDF and destination, then save them to Library. An article can be saved without a PDF and receive or reuse its Gewu Key.
Download on a research resultRun Gewu's managed download workflow for that paper, with supported direct routes and background webpage fallback. Add to Library remains a separate placement action.

System networking and Clash rules

Browser uses WebView2 and the current system network configuration. Gewu does not change proxies or Clash rules. Verify the actual route for publisher, PDF, login and CDN hosts independently; institutional access remains subject to the website.

Save an article and PDF to Library

Save to Gewu opens a compact dialog with File type, Add to Library, Cancel and Save to Library. Click the double-arrow Details to expand article identity and PDF controls. Set its default under Settings > Website Links.

  1. Open the article or PDF. Follow Open Website from a research workspace, or find the article directly in Browser. Wait for the page to finish loading and click Save to Gewu.
  2. Review identity in Details. Check the title, DOI and Gewu Key. An existing DOI or known arXiv identity reuses its paper record, including a record discovered only in a Monitor. A new article receives its own Key when saved. If needed, enter a DOI/arXiv ID and click Identify. Without an identifier, enter the article title and choose Use this title; metadata can be completed later.
  3. Choose the PDF in Details. For a directly opened PDF or a detected embedded PDF (such as an IEEE full-text viewer), Gewu reads the loaded original and parses its information again. It does not request the PDF from the publisher again. If several loaded PDFs are present, select the intended one first. Use Loaded PDF retries this local read. If WebView2 cannot supply the complete original, an error is shown; Download PDF Again explicitly requests another download. On an article page, select a detected link and click Get PDF, or choose a local PDF. Each file must be readable and no larger than 128 MB. Check the filename and leave Include this PDF in Paper Files selected to attach it.
  4. Choose the destination. Click the folder button under Add to Library. The same column picker used by Journal and Subject Monitor shows My Library and Spaces on the left, then subfolders in successive columns. Check the full path and click Confirm to select the destination. Choose the file type, then click Save to Library to import. Recognized publisher article PDFs suggest Published version, while recognized Science First Release PDFs suggest Accepted manuscript. Recognized arXiv, bioRxiv, medRxiv, ChemRxiv and Research Square preprints suggest Preprint, regardless of the article’s journal metadata. Review the suggestion; uncertain files remain Unknown. The first article PDF becomes Default in the main folder, even if Unknown. Supplements stay separate, and manual Default is preserved. Source follows the PDF’s actual website: Publisher, Preprint server, Institutional repository or Other. Local files use User import without a webpage source.

Opening Details, identifying or cancelling imports nothing. Save reuses an existing active Library or Space placement, preferring the selected occurrence of that same paper. Attaching a PDF does not add a root-level entry. To add another location, explicitly choose and confirm its folder. Papers with no active placement use the folder saved in Settings > Add to Library, initially Library / unsorted, unless you confirm another folder. An unavailable saved default falls back to unsorted. Review creates no placement; the destination is checked again on Save. Paper Files refreshes immediately. Exact duplicates retain their existing source and settings; distinct versions stay separate, and manual Default is preserved. Show in Library selects the saved occurrence. Browser keeps the webpage.

Save a correction or retraction under its original article

A normal article PDF that resolves to an existing work can be attached to that work, including one with both DOI and arXiv identifiers or placements in several folders. Check the title and Gewu Key in Details, keep Include this PDF in Paper Files selected and save. The selected placement and existing identity are reused.

When Browser recognizes a correction, retraction, expression of concern, withdrawal or addendum, it resolves the explicitly related original article during review. Details shows the original that will receive the file. If that original is not yet cataloged and its DOI can be resolved, Save can create the original's record and attach the notice there. The notice retains its own metadata and file type; it does not receive a separate research-paper Gewu Key or replace the article's automatic Default.

If the original cannot be determined, use an existing original's Gewu Key and click Use Key. Review the target and confirm the explicit attachment when prompted. Automatic returns to automatic identification. Resolve missing or conflicting evidence before saving to avoid attaching a notice to the wrong paper. Opening Details or reviewing a target does not itself save anything. MCP and Journal Monitor retain their own notice-import workflows.

Save a Science ePDF already open in Browser

Science's online ePDF reader displays the PDF inside a webpage. Once the document has loaded, Save to Gewu can read that reader's original PDF, including pages whose download control is an icon. This is the article file, not a screenshot or a printout of the webpage.

  1. Wait for the actual Science PDF to load. An abstract page or access screen is not a loaded article PDF.
  2. Open Save to Gewu > Details. Check the article title, DOI, Gewu Key and PDF status. If needed, choose Use Loaded PDF. Each original must be complete and no larger than 128 MB.
  3. Check File type and the destination, then save. A byte-identical file already attached to that paper reports Existing PDF reused; it keeps the existing resource and your manual Default.

Keep the source document open during review. If it changes, reopen Save to Gewu for the new document. After Save or Cancel, the Science reader resumes displaying its pages. If the original cannot be read, wait for loading to finish and retry, or choose a PDF you have saved locally. Download PDF Again requests a fresh transfer and can still fail even when the browser has a readable copy. This workflow shares your existing article access; it cannot supply a missing subscription.

Use the original paper or correct the target

A tab opened with Open Website or the arXiv arrow remembers its source paper and Library occurrence, including related PDF tabs. Save to Gewu uses that existing paper when the current evidence agrees or provides no conflicting identifier. Manually corrected DOI/arXiv values take precedence over old automatic matches. If the page identifies another work, the source is not forced onto it.

  1. Enter the correct existing Gewu Key in Details. Press Return or choose Use Key.
  2. Wait for Target updated. Check the displayed title, Key, existing-article status and Add to Library path. The review switches to that paper's active location when available. An unknown Key produces an error and creates nothing.
  3. Review any conflicting evidence. If the page or PDF identifies another work, explicitly confirm that this file belongs to the selected target before saving. Changing the identifier afterward requires another review.
  4. Check the PDF and File type, then save. Selecting a target attaches the file without replacing that paper's DOI, metadata or manual Default. Choose Automatic to return to automatic identity detection.

What Article only means. No PDF is currently included in the review. Article identification and PDF attachment are separate: identifying a DOI can find the existing paper without attaching a file. Expand Details and inspect the PDF controls. A loaded complete PDF can be reused through Use Loaded PDF; otherwise open the site's actual PDF or choose a local file. This status alone does not mean the publisher has no PDF.

If PDF retrieval fails: retry after opening the site's PDF, choose a downloaded local PDF, or save the article alone. Errors stay visible; missing or conflicting identity opens Details. If storage fails after saving the article, retry reuses its record and placement. Browser capture uses its current WebView2 session without exporting sign-in cookies. It cannot bypass a site's login, access rights or embedded-browser restrictions. The collector currently belongs to Gewu's built-in Browser; a Safari extension is not included.

Privacy and compatibility boundaries

Bookmarks/history use local SQLite; cookies/cache use Browser's persistent profile, not Chrome synchronization. Browsing/search reaches websites, but external pages have no Library/credential bridge. Local/file/application addresses are blocked. Standard internal child documents use WebView2's origin and sandbox rules; they cannot become address-bar destinations. HTTP recovery retries once as same-host HTTPS GET, without replaying forms or bypassing certificates; errors include reason/code. The local server rejects cross-site API requests and unrecognized hosts.

Website sign-in on Windows

Complete normal publisher or institutional sign-in yourself in Browser. Its WebView2 profile is separate from Chrome and Edge. Gewu does not import their cookies or credentials. Apple Passwords and its AutoFill trigger are not available in this Windows application.

Website data on Windows

Browser uses its own WebView2 profile. It does not use Apple's Keychain or transfer sign-in cookies from another browser. Complete normal sign-in yourself; use Open in Default Browser if a site does not support this embedded browser.

Share article access with background downloads

Supported Windows publisher downloads use a bounded background WebView2 page with Gewu Browser's website session. Complete required sign-in or verification yourself in Browser, then retry Download. External browsers and Zotero have separate website sessions. Access controls and verified source restrictions still apply.

Review PDF identity before saving

Save to Gewu matches the PDF to the selected article. An article's correction metadata pointing back to its own DOI does not by itself make the article a notice. A genuine correction or other publication notice is reviewed under its original article; check the displayed target and file classification. If the original article cannot be resolved, enter its Gewu Key and confirm the attachment.

If PDF drawing order joins a distant ellipsis to a title-page DOI, Gewu checks the layout of that same page. It accepts the complete DOI only when the evidence is unambiguous. Different article identifiers still require review, and the saved PDF bytes are unchanged.

Settings and Safety

Configure Literature Data Sources

Use Literature Data Sources to configure services for literature discovery, metadata, citations, and version matching.

Built-in sources work without setup. Optional credentials improve access or coverage for supported services.

Open settings

Choose Settings > Literature Data Sources. The dialog provides provider settings and separate connection tests.

Available services

ServiceConfiguration
Crossref, arXiv, DataCiteBuilt in; no key field is required.
OpenAlexOptional OpenAlex API key.
Semantic ScholarOptional API key. Anonymous access remains available.
NASA ADSOptional API token for astronomy and physics coverage.

Save a credential

  1. Paste the credential into its service field.
  2. Choose Save beside that service. Each service has its own Save, Test, and Clear controls.
  3. Choose Test and read the status underneath. This checks service access; it does not refresh every paper. Then refresh one paper to inspect the available citation evidence.

A configured field shows fixed round dots by default, while the detailed status below continues to report saving, connection, or quota information. The dots do not expose the key or its length. Click Show inside the field to reveal the saved key, or inspect a newly typed key; click Hide to mask it again. A saved key is retrieved only on Show, and its displayed value is cleared on Hide or when settings closes. Type a replacement and choose Save to change the key; Clear removes the locally saved key. A configured environment key can remain available. Avoid screenshots or screen sharing while a key is visible.

Semantic Scholar sends its key in the official x-api-key header. Requests share a low-rate queue and use exponential backoff after rate limits or temporary failures.

OpenAlex status reports the remaining daily free allowance and its reset time when available. Gewu uses only that free allowance and falls back to other metadata sources when it is exhausted; it does not spend paid OpenAlex credits. A saved key is not proof that every remote request will succeed.

ImportantCredentials are local-only: store them in local SQLite or approved environment variables. Do not place keys in source files, logs, exported reports, tests, or Git.

Settings and Safety

Choose arXiv Discovery Scopes

Choose one or more arXiv subject archives for discovery. Selections can span several research fields or combine several groups within one field.

Open arXiv Scope Settings

Choose Settings > arXiv Scope Settings. The window lists every supported primary subject and its archive groups. Select at least one group, then choose Save.

Understand the hierarchy

The first level identifies a broad arXiv subject such as Physics, Computer Science, Mathematics, Economics, Electrical Engineering and Systems Science, Quantitative Biology, Quantitative Finance, or Statistics. Each checkbox represents an archive group beneath that subject. For example, Physics > Condensed Matter includes all cond-mat.* leaf categories.

You may select several groups under Physics, or combine groups across primary subjects. Categories shared by more than one scope are fetched only once.

Default and saved behavior

  • The default selection is only Physics > Condensed Matter.
  • Restore Defaults changes the selection in the window; choose Save to apply it.
  • Saving changes future arXiv refresh coverage and rebuilds the available Preprint Filter categories.
  • Previously saved papers remain in SQLite. Changing scopes never deletes earlier discoveries.
NoteThe category checkboxes in Journal Monitor are display filters. They do not narrow the discovery scope selected here.

Preview Settings

Choose the Default Add to Library Folder

Choose where a newly added paper starts. The initial default is Library / unsorted; existing Browser captures keep their active paper location.

Set or restore the default

  1. Open Settings > Add to Library.
  2. Choose Choose Folder, select an active Library or Space folder in the column picker, and confirm it.
  3. Choose Save. Closing the settings window without saving discards the new choice. Restore Default immediately saves Library / unsorted again.

How each entry point uses it

Entry pointDestination
Journal, Subject or Author Monitor > Add to LibraryThe picker preselects the saved default. Confirm another folder to override it for this addition.
Browser > Save to Gewu, existing active paperReuse that paper's active Library/Space placement, preferring the originating selected occurrence of the same Key. The new default does not create another location.
Browser > Save to Gewu, no active placementUse the saved default, unless you explicitly choose and confirm another folder.
Folder Add Paper, File Explorer drop or Folder LoaderKeep the destination of that explicit operation. This preference does not redirect an import already aimed at a folder.

The preference follows the selected folder when it is renamed or moved. If it is deleted, recycled or unavailable, a later default addition falls back to Library / unsorted. Recycle cannot be chosen. If an explicitly selected destination becomes unavailable before Save, choose a valid destination again.

This affects future additions only. It does not relocate existing papers, change Gewu Keys, copy PDFs, alter file classification or change Default. Choosing a local disk path is not the same as choosing a managed Library folder.

Choose Where Website Links Open

OptionBehavior
Gewu Insight Browser (default)Opens a new built-in Browser tab, preserving existing pages. Press Ctrl+[ to return to the source workspace.

Restore Default saves Gewu Insight Browser and collapses Save to Gewu Details by default.

Settings and Safety

Connect an AI to Your Papers

Give an AI client access to selected papers through their stable Gewu Keys, without navigating the interface.

Settings > AI Access is off by default. Normal App use needs no AI token. Enabling it does not start a model, analyze papers or upload your library. Requests happen only when a connected AI client calls the local service.

One MCP interface, multiple AI clients

Gewu Insight uses the standard MCP interface to work with compatible AI clients. Codex and DeepSeek Harness are two configuration examples. Claude Code and other clients that support local stdio MCP servers can use the same adapter, connection settings and permission model. The client provides the AI; Gewu provides access to the authorized papers and operations.

Choose a client that can start a local process on the same computer as Gewu. Copy the generated command, args and env into that client's configuration format. The local API address belongs in GEWU_API_URL; it is not a remote MCP server URL. Create a separate named connection for each client so that permissions, expiry, activity and revocation can be managed independently.

API, MCP and your token

NameMeaning in this connection
APIApplication Programming Interface: the operations another program can request from Gewu Insight.
MCPModel Context Protocol: a shared way for an AI client to discover and call tools. Gewu's local MCP adapter translates those calls into its API requests.
Access tokenA private credential issued by Gewu Insight. It authorizes a connection's paper collection and permissions; it is separate from your AI account login and from text tokens counted by models.
Gewu KeyThe stable identifier of a paper. It selects the article; the access token authorizes access to it.

Methodology: a stateful information infrastructure

Gewu Insight gives people and AI clients a shared, persistent research workspace. Stateful means that cataloged papers, their identities, registered files and saved analyses remain available between tasks. SQLite is the source of truth for records and relationships; the documents remain local files. The Gewu Key lets a person or an authorized AI return to the same paper across conversations and clients.

The API exposes supported operations with defined inputs and structured results. An AI can retrieve a paper by key without navigating the interface or depending on the internal database schema. MCP makes those operations discoverable as tools; a script can use the HTTP API directly. Both use the same underlying records and authorization rules. Gewu supplies the material and stores approved results; the connected AI performs the analysis.

Design choiceHow it helps research work
Stable paper identityUse one Gewu Key to connect the article, its files and analyses across tasks. A title or filename is not the identity, and knowing a key does not grant access.
Explicit, bounded operationsSearch with pagination and read selected pages or text chunks. Programs can compose these steps and limit unnecessary retrieval without relying on screen coordinates.
Persistent, traceable resultsSave a Markdown analysis under the same key with source file references. People can inspect it in Paper Files, and another authorized session can retrieve it later.

This provides a foundation for continuing literature analysis and reusing saved knowledge. It does not automatically preserve an AI's conversation or reasoning, build a semantic memory index, or synchronize model memory. A later session must explicitly retrieve the records and notes it needs; access still depends on its current grant and the continued availability of those records and files.

Two API routes, one authorization boundary

RouteWhere permission is checked
AI client → MCP adapter → Gewu APIThe adapter sends the connection token to the API. MCP does not grant additional access.
AI client or script → Gewu APIThe caller supplies the same kind of token directly. Skipping MCP does not skip API authorization.

For either route, the API checks that AI access is enabled, the token is valid, unexpired and unrevoked, the requested paper is in the connection's collection, and the operation is permitted. Metadata access alone does not authorize directory browsing, file reading or analysis writing. The native App uses a separate private workspace session for normal human use; an AI token cannot call those internal UI endpoints.

Interface authorization and local file permissionsAI Access controls requests through Gewu's interfaces. It does not encrypt or isolate SQLite and document files from software that already has operating-system permission to read them. Such software can read the disk without contacting MCP or the API; administrator privileges are not necessarily required. Turning off AI Access or revoking a token stops access through that grant, but does not revoke independent filesystem permissions. This broader local access is outside the AI Access permission boundary.

Create a connection

  1. Keep Gewu Insight running and enable AI access.
  2. Expand New Connection and enter a name you will recognize.
  3. Choose Library, Spaces and My Publications; one folder and its subfolders using the usual folder picker; or specific Gewu Keys. A folder connection follows current membership.
  4. Article metadata and file names are readable by default. Separately allow directory browsing, file contents and/or adding new Markdown analyses when your task needs them.
  5. Choose an expiry, then Create Connection. The default is 30 days.
  6. Use Copy MCP Configuration to obtain the local adapter path, Python executable, port and token. Enter these in your AI client's MCP settings using its required format. The Codex and DeepSeek Harness examples below show two ways to use these same values.
Keep the connection privateThe token is shown only after creation. Store it in client configuration, not in a chat message or shared document. If it is lost, revoke that connection and create another. An AI client may send authorized content to its model provider.

What an authorized AI can do

ToolResult
search_papersSearch authorized titles, DOI, Gewu Keys and abstracts, with pagination.
list_foldersList authorized Library and Space roots, or a folder's direct children, with stable IDs, logical paths and filtered counts. Requires directory-browsing permission.
list_folder_papersList each authorized paper placement and its Gewu Key in a directory, directly or recursively. Includes pagination and minimal metadata. Requires directory-browsing permission.
get_paperGet the article metadata, file inventory and Default file ID for a Gewu Key.
get_paper_fileGet an original PDF or registered attachment as a read-only temporary copy on the local AI client's machine, with paper metadata, file ID and actual SHA-256. Requires file-reading permission.
get_file_delivery_statusShow used and remaining temporary capacity, file slots and active delivery IDs for this MCP connection.
release_paper_fileRelease a temporary copy by its delivery ID after reading finishes, and show the restored quota. Original Paper Files and saved analyses are preserved.
read_paperExtract PDF text by page or read text/Markdown chunks. Use get_paper_file for the original file when text extraction is insufficient.
save_analysisAdd a new Markdown analysis to the same paper's Paper Files when writing analyses is allowed.

For example, give the AI a Gewu Key, ask it to read the Default PDF, and save a Chinese analysis with source page references. The saved note records its connection, time, key, request ID and supplied source file hash/pages. It remains an ordinary associated Markdown file, available in built-in Preview. Returning to Library refreshes the selected paper's file panel.

Saving an analysis preserves the article identity, existing files, metadata and Default choice. A retry using the same request ID and identical content reuses the saved file. A new analysis needs a new request ID. Existing file contents, including earlier AI analyses, cannot be edited or overwritten. Creating folders, importing files, moving or renaming existing items and filling missing metadata require separate permissions.

New analyses are registered as Markdown notes: File type: Other, Annotation: Unannotated, and Source: Other with AI analysis and the connection name as source detail. File size, content hash, creation time and analysis provenance are recorded. These categories are assigned by Gewu; the AI cannot relabel its note as a published paper.

Let an AI import a prepared collection

Open Settings > AI Access and expand Edit write permissions for the intended connection. Choose operations, then click Library or root Space names under Writable collections. Selected rows stay blue and include all active subfolders; click again to deselect. My Publications is not a write destination in this editor. Choose Save Write Access, then reconnect the AI client to refresh its tools.

Saved remains beside the editor title even when collapsed. Saved selections survive closing Settings and restarting the App. Unsaved changes requires saving; Not saved retains your draft for retry. Earlier child-only grants show Some subfolders only and stay limited until you explicitly select their root. No write permission is added automatically.

Selected write collections also become readable; other existing read permissions and tokens stay unchanged. An empty selection grants no existing write destination. Create Spaces grants access only to each new Space this connection creates. Choose directory browsing separately if the AI needs to explore the tree.

ToolPurpose
create_spaceCreate a new Space and return its folder ID.
create_folderCreate a nested folder under a writable Library or Space folder.
move_folder / rename_folderMove a complete folder subtree or rename a folder/Space, synchronizing the actual directories.
move_file / rename_fileMove an item or Paper File, or rename its placement/filename under the existing file ownership rules.
upload_fileTransfer one prepared client-local file to temporary staging and return its upload ID.
import_paperSave a paper with AI-supplied metadata in the chosen folder, with or without a PDF.
import_fileImport an independent non-PDF file in any format, such as a direction overview in Markdown.
add_paper_fileAppend a file of any format to the specified existing Gewu Key.
update_paper_metadataFill missing fields from AI-supplied facts and a source URL; preserve existing values and report disagreements.
get_upload_status
release_upload		Check upload capacity or release an unused staged upload.
resolve_paper
get_resolve_status		Start or check a separately requested Resolve job for one existing paper. Never part of an import.

The AI must bring the paper metadata. A paper import requires title, authors, publication type, journal or repository, known publication date or year, DOI and arXiv status, and the source URL. A genuinely absent identifier uses an explicit null value. If required facts are missing, the AI must find them using its own sources and retry. Import does not search a PDF for identifiers, fetch metadata online, call Resolve or queue enrichment. Supplied facts retain their source and connection provenance; Gewu does not claim to have verified them. A PDF is optional: omit upload_id and file_type to save the paper and receive its Gewu Key without a placeholder file or automatic download. Later, upload the PDF and call add_paper_file with that key. Supplied PDFs still receive integrity checks; annotation status initially remains Unknown.

Choose ownership explicitly. Import an independent Markdown overview with import_file. Attach a paper-specific analysis, spreadsheet, image or code file with add_paper_file and the owning Gewu Key. An ordinary non-PDF file retains its internal storage key but has no public Gewu Key field in the App. It does not become a scholarly paper simply because the AI imported it.

Reuse the existing paper identity. A matching DOI or arXiv identity reuses the existing Gewu Key and adds its placement in the requested folder. A different incoming PDF is retained as another Paper File. A valid manual Default remains; otherwise eligible versions use the normal priority: Corrected published version, Published version, Accepted manuscript, then Preprint. This also applies to add_paper_file. The automatic Default becomes the managed main file; other versions stay in Associated Files and folder aliases are synchronized. Supplements and analyses do not take automatic Default. Identical bytes reuse the file and its classification and record the import source. Similar titles alone never merge papers. Uncollected provider/Monitor records, including managed download PDFs, reuse the same Key through a writable destination and the normal archive workflow. Unreadable private collections, notes or external files still require user access review. DOI and arXiv pointing to different records remain an identity conflict.

Publication notices belong to the original article. Corrections, errata and retraction notices retain their own DOI, title and date as associated notice metadata. They do not create another research-paper Gewu Key or become the automatic Default. For MCP import, the AI must supply publication_notice with the notice kind, original article DOI and an evidence URL; import the original first if absent. Missing or ambiguous relations require review and never trigger Resolve. Paper Files shows linked notices while retaining the original article and its files.

When a file is present, the main file goes in the selected Library or Space folder. Its other files go in the existing mirrored Associated Files bundle. Multiple placements share that bundle and use the normal aliases. The AI supplies folder IDs and file ownership; Gewu calculates and maintains the physical paths according to the same storage rules used by the App.

Complete one file at a time. Upload one file, immediately register it with the appropriate import or attachment tool, then proceed to the next. Each successful file import immediately releases that file's staging; it does not wait for an entire folder or batch. Do not upload a whole collection before registering files. Capacity limits apply to currently retained files, not the total number or size of a literature collection.

Upload staging allows up to 256 MiB per file and 512 MiB or 16 currently staged files per connection. If it fills, register ready uploads or release unused ones, then continue without reconnecting. Failed transfers remove their partials; unused ready uploads expire after 24 hours, while active transfers are retained. Read copies have their separate limits below and must be released only after all readers finish. Actual free disk space and single-file limits still apply.

Keep a stable request ID for every write and a separate ID for its upload. Retry an interrupted response with the same arguments and ID to reuse its result. Existing files are never overwritten. If the result says alias synchronization is pending, retry that same import to finish the folder shortcuts.

Resolve remains independent. Enable its separate permission only when needed. It operates on one existing writable paper, requires an explicit standalone purpose, and returns a job immediately. Known DOI/arXiv is used first; PDF identifier extraction also needs file-reading permission. Results fill missing fields while preserving existing values and Default. At most two jobs run concurrently, and their network lookup does not block imports. The AI must never use this tool to prepare or complete import metadata.

Let an AI organize files and folders

Enable Move folders, Rename folders and Spaces, Move files and change Paper Files ownership or Rename files separately. Select the source and destination collections, save, and reconnect the client. Every affected location must be writable, including other placements of the same record. My Publications remains outside these write permissions.

Use a folder ID to move a whole subtree or rename a folder/Space. The actual directory and its mirrored Associated Files move together; empty folders and existing contents are retained. Library, Unsorted and Recycle are protected. A folder cannot move into itself or a descendant. A Space root may be moved into Library using the same conversion rules as the App.

For files, select either a membership ID from directory browsing or an exact Gewu Key and numeric file ID from Paper Files. A membership moves the whole item to another folder, or attaches its files to another record. A specific Paper File moves to another record or becomes an independent item in a folder. Independent non-PDF files keep their ordinary-file behavior. Renaming a membership changes its label and disk projection; renaming a Paper File changes that filename and must retain its extension. The bibliographic title stays unchanged.

File contents, IDs, classifications and provenance stay intact. The main file stays in its owning directory; other files use Associated Files. Transfers follow the App's existing ownership rules: the source chooses a remaining Default if necessary, the target keeps its existing Default, and an emptied source may retire. Final-file transfers from records with multiple placements are rejected. Moving into a folder that already contains the same record reuses that membership without losing files.

Operations do not run Resolve, upload existing files again or consume transfer staging. Use identical arguments and the same request ID to retry an interrupted response or finish pending shortcut synchronization. Unrelated files are never overwritten. External originals cannot be renamed through MCP; a permitted ownership transfer of an externally linked file keeps the original and uses the App's managed-copy rule.

Browse a directory and its papers

Directory browsing is a separate, read-only permission. For a new connection, select Browse authorized directories and paper memberships. For an existing connection, select Allow directory browsing beside its name. This adds folders:read without replacing the token, changing the paper collection or granting file reading or analysis writing. Existing connections are not expanded automatically. Reconnect the AI client's MCP connection to discover the two new tools.

These directories are the logical folders in Library and Spaces, not disk paths. A Space uses a stable folder_id just like any folder. Shortcuts lead to the original target; they do not duplicate its membership. My Publications-only papers remain available through search and get_paper. Recycle and trashed folders or items are excluded.

Selected collectionVisible directories and memberships
Library, Spaces and My PublicationsAll active Library and Space folders, including empty ones, and their active paper placements.
One folder and its subfoldersOnly that folder and its active descendants. The displayed path starts there; parents, siblings and outside placements stay hidden.
Specific Gewu KeysOnly folders containing those papers and the parent paths needed to reach them. Enabling directory browsing allows these folder names to be read; unrelated branches and their counts stay hidden.

For example, ask the AI to list the papers in your AI Space and preserve their folder classifications:

  1. Call list_folders without a parent to discover visible roots. Follow next_cursor until it is null, and identify AI by its name, kind and path.
  2. Use AI's returned folder_id as parent_id in list_folders to inspect its children. Repeat as needed to map the folder hierarchy.
  3. Call list_folder_papers with that folder_id. By default it returns direct members; set recursive to true to include descendants. Follow every page. Each page defaults to 50 entries, with a maximum of 100.
  4. Keep the returned membership_id, folder_id and gewu_key together. One paper can have several placements; use the Gewu Key to avoid reading it repeatedly while retaining its classifications. Call get_paper for the selected key before reading files.

Names can repeat, so use folder IDs and the returned ID/name path segments instead of treating a display path as a unique identifier. Each call states its directory explicitly; navigating in another task does not change a shared current directory.

Keep a multi-page collection walk consistentPass the first returned revision with subsequent directory calls. A visible rename, move, deletion or membership change returns collection_changed; discard the incomplete walk and start again without the old cursor or revision. Folder IDs survive renames and moves, while deleted and recreated folders get new IDs. A folder grant follows its root ID, but descendants moved outside it lose access. Ordinary metadata refreshes do not interrupt membership pagination; bibliography fields remain current, not a historical snapshot.

Give the original PDF to the AI client

Use get_paper_file with the Gewu Key and a file ID from get_paper, or default. When no Default exists, choose an explicit file ID. Gewu checks the connection and transfers the original bytes. The client receives a read-only temporary copy, title, authors, DOI, file classification and actual SHA-256. Its own tools can read the PDF, inspect pages and figures, or run OCR. Gewu does not render pages, run OCR, upload the file to a model or fetch a replacement from the DOI.

The delivered copy is separate from Paper Files and never syncs changes back. Write rendered pages and intermediate results separately. A file is limited to 64 MiB, with up to 256 MiB or 64 retained copies per MCP session. Each delivery returns a delivery_id and quota showing used and remaining bytes and file slots. Use get_file_delivery_status to check capacity and find active delivery IDs.

Remaining capacity is reported to the AI client in these tool results; it is not a separate Library or AI Access status meter. Ask the connected assistant to check file-delivery status when you need the current amount.

After every reader, rendering and OCR task finishes with a copy, call release_paper_file with its delivery ID. This frees its temporary quota immediately; original Paper Files, saved analyses and derived outputs remain unchanged. Keep the source file ID, SHA-256 and page references for citations and saving analyses. Active repeat delivery shares the same copy and ID, so finish all its users before release. Repeating a release is safe. No files are automatically evicted: when quota is full, release finished copies and retry.

Unreleased copies last until normal MCP process exit. The two local management tools also work offline or after grant expiry; they cannot retrieve new files. Reconnect MCP once after upgrading to discover them, after finishing work with old copies. A client needs access to the adapter's local filesystem; a returned path is not a cloud PDF attachment. If unavailable, report that limitation rather than reading the source Library directly.

Revocation, expiry or disabling AI Access prevents new deliveries. Copies already delivered to a client cannot be recalled. File transfer uses local disk and memory; PDF processing done by a client on the same computer can still compete for resources. Gewu adds no automatic whole-document OCR workload.

A repeatable research workflow

  1. Identify. Give the AI an authorized Gewu Key, or use search_papers to find candidates and confirm the intended paper with get_paper.
  2. Read. Inspect the file inventory, then use get_paper_file to obtain the original PDF and read its temporary copy with the AI client's tools. For text-only requests, read_paper remains available. Retain the returned file ID, SHA-256 and page references.
  3. Analyze and save. Ask the AI to produce a Chinese Markdown analysis. With analysis-writing permission, call save_analysis under the same key and include the source references. Reuse the request ID only for an identical retry; changed source bytes require a fresh read before saving.
  4. Release. Once all work using a temporary copy finishes, call release_paper_file with its delivery ID. Check the returned remaining quota, then proceed to the next paper without restarting MCP.
  5. Review and continue. Inspect the note in Paper Files. In another task, retrieve that same paper and explicitly read the saved note before continuing. Each session works with the current authorized state.

These steps can be combined into a scripted workflow or repeated over a selected collection. Pagination and bounded reads help control how much material is retrieved; they do not guarantee model accuracy or a particular speed. Review the analysis against its cited sources.

Keep AI connections after an App or database move

Codex, DeepSeek Harness, Claude Code and other compatible clients connect to the same running Gewu service. Moving research data through a verified migration preserves connection records, their scope and permissions; it does not require a new token merely because the database folder changed.

Keep the updated App open on the intended database. If the adapter's code path, Python executable or service port changed, update the existing client's command, args and GEWU_API_URL from the installed App's configuration, preserving its own connection token and other client settings. If those values did not change, they can remain as they are. Do not point the MCP command at the database folder.

After reconnecting, list the available tools and perform a read-only lookup of a familiar authorized paper. Check its Gewu Key and available Paper Files. This verifies the existing collection without creating a new paper, changing grants or saving a test analysis.

Connect a local MCP client on Windows

  1. Keep Gewu Insight running on the intended database. In Settings > AI Access, enable access and create a named connection with only the required collections and operations.
  2. Use Copy MCP Configuration. Copy the generated command, arguments and environment values into your client's local STDIO server configuration. Keep each path, including spaces, as one argument.
  3. The installed application provides its own Python runtime and MCP adapter. Use the exact generated paths; no separate Python installation is needed.
  4. Preserve GEWU_API_URL_FILE and GEWU_DATABASE_IDENTITY when generated. They follow the current local port and bind the connection to the selected database. Keep GEWU_API_TOKEN private; the token is shown only at creation.
  5. Reload the client's MCP connection, list tools and check a familiar authorized Gewu Key and its Paper Files before requesting writes.

Codex, DeepSeek Harness, Claude Code and other clients supporting a local STDIO MCP server can use this adapter. Map the generated command, arguments and environment into that client's configuration format. Create a separate named Gewu connection for each client. Client model login or API keys are separate from the Gewu token; GEWU_API_URL is a local API address, not a remote MCP server URL.

Reconnect after an App or database move

A verified migration preserves connection permissions and scope; moving the folder does not itself require a new token. Keep the installed App open on the intended database. Update changed runtime, adapter or endpoint paths from its generated configuration, retaining the existing client's own token and unrelated settings. Preserve the database identity and URL-file fields. If these values did not change, keep them. The adapter command points to the installed program, not the research folder.

The client must run where it can access the adapter's local files. A returned file path is not a cloud attachment. This manual does not change your AI client's configuration or its model settings.

Connect another local MCP client

Use Settings > AI Access > Copy MCP Configuration and enter that generated configuration in your Windows client's local STDIO MCP settings. Use the installed Python and adapter paths exactly, preserve the database identity and endpoint-file fields, and keep the generated token private. Do not paste a macOS path or assume a fixed port.

Use the same settings in another client

For Claude Code or another compatible client, add a local stdio server named gewu-insight using the same generated command, argument list and environment variables. Follow the client's own configuration syntax; Claude Code's MCP documentation includes local stdio setup. A model subscription or API key belongs to the AI client; the Gewu access token separately controls access to your papers.

Verify a real paper, then request an analysis

These steps work in Codex, DeepSeek Harness and other connected clients. First ask for a read-only search_papers call; an empty result can simply mean the authorized collection has no matching papers. Replace YOUR_GEWU_KEY below with the exact key of an authorized paper that has a local PDF, then send:

Use the gewu-insight MCP tools to get the paper with Gewu Key YOUR_GEWU_KEY. Show its title and Default filename. Use get_paper_file to obtain the original PDF, then read the first three pages of its delivered copy with your PDF tools and summarize them in Chinese. Preserve the file ID and SHA-256; do not access the source Library directly.

This checks both metadata access and PDF reading. When analysis-writing permission is enabled, you can follow with:

Read the relevant remaining PDF pages, then save a Chinese Markdown analysis to this same paper through save_analysis. Include the source file ID, SHA-256 and page references, and use a unique request ID.

The saved analysis appears as an associated Markdown file under that paper's Paper Files; the Default PDF stays unchanged. Check the returned Gewu Key and file ID, then inspect the result in the App. When requesting a new Space or a prepared collection, enable the corresponding write operations first and specify the destination. For example:

Create a Space named Reading Project. Add the authorized paper YOUR_GEWU_KEY to it using its existing DOI or arXiv identity and complete metadata. Preserve its Gewu Key and existing files. Report the destination folder ID and saved paper key, and stop if a required permission or metadata field is missing.

This example writes to your collection; run it only when you want that new Space and placement. A PDF is optional for the import, so no upload is needed just to add an existing paper to the destination. A retry of the same write uses the same request ID and identical arguments; a different operation needs a new request ID. See the prepared-collection instructions above for file uploads and classification.

If a tool is missing, check that connection's permissions and reload MCP. If the service is unavailable, start Gewu; if access is rejected, check the AI switch, expiry, revocation and selected paper collection. A replacement connection supplies a new token, which must also be updated in the AI client's settings. Client changes do not transfer permissions from another connection.

Pause, revoke and review

Turn off Enable AI access to pause all connections. Revoke stops one connection and removes it from the active Connections list; expired connections also stop working. Re-enabling access resumes connections that are still valid. Expand Recent Activity to review requests and outcomes as separate rows in an independently scrolling list, and choose Refresh to update it. Tokens, prompts and full file text are not included in that activity log.

Limits and troubleshooting

The AI client must run on the same computer, and Gewu Insight's local service must be running. The local MCP adapter supports protocol 2025-11-25 and earlier negotiated versions. There is no remote MCP endpoint in this version. Developers can retrieve the authenticated API v1 specification at /api/v1/openapi.json.

Original file delivery has a 64 MiB file limit and includes every page. PDF text extraction through read_paper is limited to ten pages per request and a bounded extraction time; text attachments are returned in chunks. Scanned PDFs may need OCR in the AI client; no OCR or model runs automatically in Gewu. Analysis notes are limited to 256 KiB. A busy response means retry later. An unavailable paper or file may be outside the connection's collection, missing, or no longer accessible.

Source editing, building and temporary tests require no AI token; calling this API against your collection does require one. Configure each client with the collection and operations its task needs. The interface and filesystem permission boundary is explained above.
