Settings and Safety

Set Naming and PDF Rename Rules

Display naming and physical PDF renaming are separate choices. Review metadata before renaming files.

Choose the Library naming rule

Choose Settings > Naming Rule > Use Title or Use Citation. The choice is saved immediately and supplies the default name for a newly added Library placement that has no name yet. It does not rename the existing collection. The default rule is Use Citation; physical PDF renaming uses the separate template below.

Configure PDF renaming

Open Settings > PDF Rename Settings. A template can use tokens such as:

  • {author} or {authors}
  • {year}
  • {title}
  • {journal}
  • {doi}

Edit Filename Template and inspect the sample Preview, then choose Save or press Return. Default immediately saves the standard {author}_{year}_{title} template. Saving a template does not rename existing PDFs; apply it through the Library rename action below.

Rename one item from metadata

  1. Confirm its DOI, title, author, journal, and year.
  2. Right-click the item.
  3. Choose Auto rename from Metadata.
  4. Verify the result in the Library and File Explorer. To rename several PDFs, select only local PDF paper rows, Right-click, and choose Auto rename n selected. Each file uses its own metadata; the progress message reports renamed, already named, and skipped items.
NoteChoosing a Default PDF can move it to the main file folder and archive the previous main PDF in Associated Files. This does not apply the filename template or rewrite file contents; name conflicts use a unique filename. Use a naming or rename action to apply your preferred naming rule.

Long filenames retain their extension

Managed import and attachment names preserve the file extension, such as .pdf, when shortening a long basename to fit filesystem limits. A long title does not require losing the suffix. File type, Gewu Key and title are separate from the filename; renaming a file does not create another work or identify its scholarly version. Use the App's file controls for managed names so recorded paths and aliases stay consistent.

See also

Choose File Types and the Default FileFolders, Shortcuts, and Spaces

Settings and Safety

Understand How Gewu Insight Stores Files

The visible Library stays simple: each file-backed paper has a main managed file at one canonical location, while its other privately managed resources live in Associated Files. Paper Files presents these resources together as one flat list.

One work, several representations

Each managed paper has one database identity and a stable Gewu Key. DOI and arXiv are external identifiers attached to that identity; neither is used as the sole storage identity.

Where the files go

  • The Default is the main file in the visible Library, Space, or My Publications tree. It may be a PDF or another file type.
  • Other PDF versions belong in the associated bundle, usually under Versions.
  • Supporting information goes to Supplements.
  • Other resources use the bundle’s Figures or Files areas as appropriate; the file-type label remains separate from its physical subfolder.

The associated bundle mirrors the paper’s managed path under data/Associated Files. When you move the paper in the UI, Gewu Insight moves the associated bundle and refreshes live paths.

Why the UI and File Explorer look different

The UI presents a paper as one item with a flat Paper Files list inside it. File Explorer shows the Default as the main file in the normal tree and the remaining managed resources in Associated Files. Choosing a different Default synchronizes both locations, including for non-PDFs, while preserving file identity, classification and bytes. With no manual Default, the automatic priority and fallback rules still select the main file when an eligible resource exists.

Copies and filesystem shortcuts

When one Gewu Key appears in several folders, it shares one Paper Files bundle. The main file stays at its canonical location. Other Windows placements use .lnk shortcuts and their associated directories point to the canonical bundle. Make Copy Desktop resolves these pointers into real files for a portable export.

A surviving normal Library, Space or My Publications placement keeps the original outside the local Recycle directory. Deleting or dragging a folder checks each paper; restoring or re-adding a recycled paper migrates its original back to normal storage. SQLite resource paths and secondary shortcuts follow. See Delete and Recover Items.

The canonical location stays stable while it is still an active placement. If that location is removed or moved, Gewu Insight uses a surviving Library, Space or My Publications placement and updates its aliases. External originals, files shared with another paper, and occupied destinations are protected; do not replace an unrelated file to force a layout change.

ImportantDo not manually move an Associated Files bundle or replace an alias in File Explorer. Use Gewu Insight so the database and physical paths change together.

See also

Storage ReferenceMake a Portable Desktop CopyUnderstand Paper Files

Settings and Safety

Know What Stays Local

Gewu Insight runs a local interface and keeps its authoritative library database on your Windows computer. Network requests occur only for the features that need external metadata, pages, profiles, or files.

Local components

  • The Windows desktop starts its local service on a free loopback port. Its current address is recorded for MCP discovery; do not assume port 8765. The service is local to this computer.
  • SQLite stores papers, identities, relationships, settings, and operational state.
  • Browser bookmarks, folders, history, and sidebar preferences also live in SQLite. Browser cookies and cache use a separate persistent WebView2 profile; they are not shared with Chrome or Edge or exported with the database.
  • Managed PDFs, attachments, photos, and generated reports stay in your selected Gewu Database. The App, source code, browser profile and machine preferences have separate locations.
  • JSON files are exports or diagnostics; they are not the authoritative database.

External requests

Metadata refresh, citation counts, journal/subject/author discovery, profile images, website opening, and downloads can contact their named services. The app paces services that require strict request limits.

Protect credentials

Optional service credentials belong only in Literature Data Sources or approved environment variables. They must not appear in a screenshot, support message, Git commit, or exported diagnostic file.

Windows Browser uses a separate WebView2 profile. Zotero has its own website session. Gewu does not copy credentials from other browsers or grant AI connections access to website passwords.

See also

Literature Data SourcesBack Up and UpgradePublisher and Network Access

Zotero Integration

Use One Gewu Workspace through Two Interfaces

Keep one Gewu Insight installation and one selected Gewu Database on your computer. Choose whether to work in the standalone Gewu App or in its Zotero tab.

One Gewu, not two copiesThe plugin is a companion interface to your existing Gewu Insight. Zotero displays the workspace and adds actions such as Save to Zotero; Gewu's local background service still runs the workspace. Installing the plugin does not create another Gewu Library, duplicate your Paper Files, or require a second set of monitor settings. Keep Gewu Insight installed even if you normally use it through Zotero.

What stays shared

Part of your workWhat happens when you change interfaces
Gewu Library, Spaces and Paper FilesBoth interfaces read and change the same records, folder placements and files in the selected Gewu Database.
Monitors, My Publications and settingsSaved journals, subjects, authors, profiles, resource API settings and preferences remain available in either interface.
AI Access and MCPExisting connections and their permissions remain attached to the same Gewu workspace. The plugin does not require an AI connection or grant additional access.
Browser page tabs and website loginsThese belong to each interface. You may need to sign in to a publisher again inside Zotero.
Zotero's own libraryThis is a separate collection. Save to Zotero copies a Gewu paper into it; Import from Zotero copies selected Zotero content into Gewu. Neither is continuous synchronization.

For example, add a journal in Gewu's Journal Monitor inside Zotero, then close that tab and open the standalone App: the journal remains monitored. Change a saved setting in the standalone App, then open the same workspace in Zotero: that setting remains in effect. These are changes to the same data, not a synchronization process between two Gewu databases.

Open and switch interfaces

  1. After installation, choose Plugin > Zotero Integration > Open in Zotero in the standalone App. This prepares the connection to the database you are using.
  2. Once Zotero confirms that the workspace has opened, the standalone App quits. The Gewu background service keeps running, so files, settings and monitors remain available. If opening fails, the App stays open.
  3. For later sessions, use Tools > Gewu Insight in Zotero. With background startup enabled, the plugin starts the installed Gewu service when needed; you do not need to open the standalone window first.
  4. To return to the standalone App, close the Gewu Insight tab in Zotero, then open Gewu Insight. You can leave Zotero itself running.

Why the standalone window may be paused

While a connected Gewu tab is open in Zotero, the standalone main window and its editing menus pause. This prevents editing through a stale view in two windows. Closing the Gewu tab refreshes the standalone view before restoring interaction. Switching to Zotero's My Library tab is not the same as closing the Gewu tab.

This pause affects the interface; background monitoring and jobs can continue. Closing the Zotero tab also leaves the shared service running. It does not delete your workspace or require exporting and importing your data.

See also

Install, Update, and Remove the PluginSave Papers and Preview PDFsConnection Settings and Troubleshooting

Zotero Integration

Install, Update, and Remove the Zotero Plugin

Start in the standalone Gewu App: choose Plugin > Zotero Integration. The installation guide stays available in that window whenever you need it.

Install for the first time

  1. Install and open Zotero. In Gewu, open Plugin > Zotero Integration. Zotero app: Detected means that Zotero is present; it does not mean the Gewu plugin is installed.
  2. Click Install in Zotero. Gewu opens its persistent guide and reveals Gewu Insight for Zotero.xpi in File Explorer. This XPI file is the plugin package bundled with your Gewu App.
  3. In Zotero's top menu, choose Tools > Plugins to open Plugins Manager.
  4. Drag the selected XPI file from File Explorer into the Plugins Manager window. Do not drop it into Zotero's literature list: that adds a file attachment rather than installing a plugin. If File Explorer is no longer open, click Show Plugin File in Gewu's guide.
  5. Confirm Zotero's installation prompt. Check that Gewu Insight is enabled in Plugins Manager. When Gewu's integration window reports Installed, choose Open in Zotero.

Understand the primary button

ButtonWhen to use it
Install in ZoteroNo installed plugin is detected. Follow the guide and confirm installation in Zotero.
Open in ZoteroThe plugin is installed and ready for everyday use with the current Gewu database.
Update PluginYour Gewu App includes a newer plugin. Replace the installed companion with that bundled version.

Update an existing plugin

After updating Gewu Insight, check this window. If it offers Update Plugin, click it and follow any displayed instructions. For an installed 0.2 or later plugin, the update is applied without dragging the XPI again. Previously saved Zotero items and Gewu data are retained.

Update Plugin uses the package already included with your Gewu App; it is not an online update check and is not required every time you open Zotero. Reinstalling after removal, or replacing the earlier 0.1 preview, uses Plugins Manager again. A future Gewu change may require a companion update; compatibility is checked when the plugin connects.

Disable or remove it yourself

In Zotero, open Tools > Plugins, find Gewu Insight, and use its menu to disable or remove the plugin. Close any remaining Gewu tab. Removing the plugin leaves your Gewu Database and previously saved Zotero items in place. To install it again, follow the first-time steps above.

Installation and updates are managed from the standalone App. The embedded Gewu menu in Zotero does not contain another Plugin > Zotero Integration window.

Companion versionThis Windows edition bundles companion 0.4.2. The installed App reports the exact bundled and installed versions. Windows and Zotero version compatibility should be checked against the release validation notes.

See also

One Workspace, Two InterfacesConnection Settings and Troubleshooting

Zotero Integration

Save Papers and Preview PDFs in Zotero

Choose where to keep a paper. Saving to Gewu uses your existing Gewu Library; Save to Zotero creates or reuses an item in Zotero's own library.

ActionResult
Save to Gewu / Add to LibraryUse the normal Gewu destination and Paper Files workflow. The paper is available in the standalone App because it uses the same database.
Save to ZoteroCopy the paper's metadata into a selected writable Zotero library or collection, optionally with its available Default PDF.

Save a paper to Zotero

  1. Find a paper in a Gewu monitor or select an existing paper in the Gewu Library, then click Save to Zotero.
  2. Choose the destination library or collection in the dialog. Only destinations you can write to are available.
  3. Leave Include the Default PDF checked to copy the existing local Default PDF, or uncheck it to save metadata only.
  4. Confirm Save to Zotero. Read the result notification; Show in Zotero reveals the saved item in Zotero's library.

The PDF is copied, not moved. Gewu retains its original and the rest of its Paper Files. This option does not copy every attachment, supplementary file or analysis note. If no local Default PDF is available, the item is saved with metadata only. A copy failure is reported separately so you can retry it.

To obtain a missing PDF, use Gewu's normal download workflow first, then save again. Publisher access requirements still apply. Repeated saves try to reuse a matching Zotero item and add it to the selected collection while preserving existing Zotero metadata edits and PDFs. Conflicting matches are reported instead of automatically merged.

Two libraries are not automatically synchronizedSave to Zotero is an explicit, one-way copy. Later edits, annotations, notes or attachment changes in Zotero do not flow back into Gewu, and later Gewu edits do not continuously update the copied Zotero item. Opening Gewu inside Zotero still uses the shared Gewu database; it does not merge the two products' libraries. To copy existing Zotero collections, files and notes into Gewu, follow Import a Zotero Library. That explicit import is also separate from continuous synchronization.

Read without importing into Zotero

In the Gewu Library or Paper Files, select a PDF and press Space for Preview. Scroll through the pages, click thumbnails to jump, or select text. Press Space or Esc to close the preview. Open in Default App opens the Windows default PDF application.

The companion renders PDFs inside Gewu's preview using Zotero's PDF components. Previewing does not create a Zotero item or copy the file into Zotero storage. The standalone Gewu App keeps its own native preview behavior.

Zotero Integration

Understand Connection Settings

Connection Settings tells the Zotero companion which existing Gewu workspace to open and how to reach its background service on this computer. Normal use does not require changing these settings.

To bring Zotero's own library into Gewu, use Loader > Import from Zotero. Its Connect Zotero action connects a source library for import; this Connection Settings dialog selects which existing Gewu workspace the tab displays.

Open the connection dialog

In Zotero's Gewu tab, click the upper-right … menu, then Connection Settings. The standalone App's Open in Zotero action normally configures this connection for you.

ControlMeaning and use
Gewu DatabaseThe folder containing the Gewu papers, Paper Files and settings you want to use. Change Database selects an existing database root, not its data subfolder. This does not copy or migrate a database.
Advanced > Local addressThe address of Gewu's service on this computer, using an automatically selected loopback port. It is not a Zotero account or cloud-server address. Leave it unchanged unless troubleshooting a known local service configuration.
Start Gewu in the backgroundAllow the plugin to start the installed Gewu service when needed, without opening the standalone App window. Keep this enabled for routine use through Zotero.
ReconnectRetry the connection using these settings. It does not import papers, merge libraries, or create an empty replacement database.

If something looks wrong

  • The Library is empty or different. Compare Gewu Database in this dialog with File > Open Gewu Database in the standalone App's menu. Close the Gewu tab, open the App with your usual database, then use Plugin > Zotero Integration > Open in Zotero again. Do not create a fresh database to repair a connection.
  • The workspace does not connect. Check that Gewu Insight is still installed, the selected database folder is accessible, and background startup is enabled. Try Reconnect; use the standalone App to inspect a startup error if necessary.
  • The Gewu tab remains but its menu is missing. Check Tools > Plugins for an enabled Gewu Insight plugin. Close an old tab left after uninstalling, then open a new one through Tools > Gewu Insight. Reinstall through the guide if the plugin is absent.
  • The standalone window cannot be edited. Close the connected Gewu tab in Zotero and allow the App to refresh. Merely switching to another Zotero tab does not end the companion session.
  • A PDF asks to download instead of previewing. Check the installed plugin version and update from the current Gewu App. The current companion provides an embedded PDF preview; no global Zotero PDF setting needs to be changed.

Existing source API settings and AI Access permissions belong to the Gewu database. Reconnecting does not require entering them again, creating a new MCP connection, or widening its permissions.

About Gewu Insight

Visual Identity and Cultural Elements

The name Gewu Insight (格物洞见) expresses a way of doing research shaped by the practice of physics: begin with the real world, and seek to see what lies behind its phenomena.

Gewu (格物) means investigating things. Here, it emphasizes starting from concrete phenomena, experimental observations, and questions that nature presents to us. Research should remain in contact with the world it seeks to understand. Abstract ideas and theories gain their purpose from that contact; they should not become castles in the air, sustained only by further abstraction.

Insight (洞见) means seeing through phenomena to the patterns and mechanisms beneath them. It values physical pictures, intuition, imagination, and the ability to make an insightful guess—to recognize what may be happening before every step has been expressed in equations. A useful physical picture can reveal which features matter, suggest a mechanism, and open a direction that formal derivation alone might not make apparent. Mathematics serves as a tool for thinking, expression, and calculation. Absolute formal rigor, axiomatic completeness, and mathematical elegance are not ends in themselves, nor should they constrain the search for physical understanding.

This outlook also shapes the purpose of the software. Research literature brings us into contact with other researchers’ experiments, observations, interpretations, and ideas. Gewu Insight keeps these materials connected: a paper retains its identity across versions, its figures and supporting files remain accessible, and related work and research notes can be organized together and revisited over time.

These functions support the everyday work from which insight can emerge: returning to an experimental result, comparing competing physical pictures, noticing an unexpected connection, or recording a conjecture worth pursuing. The researcher brings the questions, intuition, and judgment; the workspace helps keep the material close at hand and the developing line of thought connected to its sources.

Investigate nature through experimental phenomena; seek insight through physical pictures and intuition.（从实验现象中格物，以物理图像和直觉求洞见。）

The calligraphic Chinese name, the app icon, and the seal-script watermark give this research outlook a visual identity.

The marks do not decorate every surface. Each has a different job: the icon identifies the application, the calligraphic name gives the product a human signature, and the quiet seal-script pattern belongs to transitional or otherwise empty space.

The calligraphic name

This is a 祝枝山行草集字 composition, assembled from separately acquired character images attributed to the Ming-dynasty calligrapher Zhu Yunming (祝允明, 号枝山). It is a modern collection and arrangement of character forms, not “a title written by Zhu Zhishan.” No surviving single inscription titled 格物洞見 is being claimed.

Historical sources of the four characters

Reading orderCharacterAttributed hand and scriptOriginal work
1格祝允明 · 行书Original work not yet identified.
2物祝允明 · 草书Original work not yet identified.
3洞祝允明 · 草书草书前后赤壁赋卷, Shanghai Museum.
4見祝允明 · 草书Original work not yet identified.

The selected 洞 character matches the form in 客有吹洞簫者 in the first Red Cliff Rhapsody of Zhu Yunming's 草书前后赤壁赋卷, held by the Shanghai Museum. This identification follows comparison with the complete scroll, rather than the mere occurrence of the same character in a text. The original works for 格、物、見 remain to be established.

The selected glyphs were optically balanced into a common line: scale, spacing, ink tone, edge cleanup, and transparent alpha were normalized while the characteristic strokes were retained. The production preparation used a Codex-assisted image workflow. The interface and accessibility text use the contemporary simplified product name 格物洞见; the artwork deliberately preserves the traditional character 見 and traditional right-to-left composition.

Provenance and reuseHistorical authorship and the modern arrangement are distinct. The museum reference identifies an underlying work; it does not claim that the production image was extracted directly from the museum's photograph. The remaining original-work identifications are still open. Gewu's software License grants only rights held by the project, not independent rights in external reproductions.

The app icon and the seal-script watermark

Why the three marks are used differently

Icon · recognitionUse at application scale: taskbar, startup identity, About, and platform packaging.
Calligraphy · signatureUse where the Chinese name can be read deliberately, especially the About panel and identity materials.
Seal script · atmosphereUse at very low opacity in startup transitions or quiet lower-right space, never where it competes with paper details.

Together the three registers establish the product's visual identity: the icon is contemporary and operational; the calligraphy is personal and gestural; the seal-script watermark is historical in reference but restrained in use. Their common purpose is to make the name visible without turning the research workspace into a themed illustration.

Reference

Handle Publisher and Network Access

Publishers can rate-limit shared VPN addresses or automated-looking traffic. Gewu Insight reduces overlap and request rate, but it cannot remove a publisher block.

If a publisher page is blocked

  1. Stop repeated refreshes. Additional requests can extend a temporary block.
  2. Try your direct connection. If the page works with VPN off, investigate the VPN route, quota or exit address before treating it as a product or certificate failure.
  3. Use Open Website or an external browser. Complete any normal institutional login or publisher interaction yourself.
  4. Download only when authorized. Add a legitimately obtained PDF with Add File.

Why figures may arrive later

Figure and article-page retrieval is queued behind discovery work and uses caching. This reduces simultaneous RSS, page, and image requests to the same publisher. A paper can appear before its representative image.

Browser and your system network

The Browser tab uses native WebView2 requests and does not proxy pages through the Python server. System proxy or TUN capture can send its traffic into Clash; only then do the active rules determine DIRECT or proxy routing. A DIRECT rule uses your current physical network, which must itself provide institutional access. Gewu Insight neither changes these rules nor guarantees a particular route; use Clash connection records to verify the actual route. See Browse, Bookmark, and Revisit Websites for downloads, sign-in limits, and the separate browser profile.

Check access to the actual main PDF

An article's title and abstract can be public while its PDF requires a subscription. A working webpage, a DIRECT rule, or a successful open-access download does not establish access to every article. Away from campus, direct traffic uses your present network; use your institution's authorized access method when needed. Gewu does not force Science through a proxy or change Clash/VPN rules.

Article pages, PDF services and content-delivery hosts may follow different network routes. APS Harvest is the first direct APS download route; a denied or unavailable response can fall back to background browsing. Science, Nature and ACS also have supported background fallbacks in the native App. These attempts share Gewu Browser's session, but cannot supply missing institutional rights or complete human verification. A clear access-required or timeout message with preserved files is preferable to saving an HTML page as a PDF.

Secure-connection failures and VPN interruptions

A secure-connection error can reflect network, VPN, routing, system time or certificate problems. Restore the connection, then reload once. The error alone does not prove an expired site certificate. Certificate verification remains enabled.

Service rate limits

Semantic Scholar, Google Scholar, and some publisher sources use shared pacing, cooldowns, or exponential backoff. Let the bottom status area settle before starting the same action again.

ImportantDo not attempt to bypass a paywall, CAPTCHA, browser verification, or access control. Use your authorized browser session or attach a file you obtained legitimately.

See also

Journal MonitorDownload and Sync VersionsTroubleshooting

Manage Startup, Monitor Cache, and Text Size

The Windows shell starts a local service for your selected workspace and opens the research interface when it is ready.

Before the first launch

Install the Windows x64 Setup.exe. Open Gewu Insight from the Start menu. No separate Python or .NET installation is required for daily use. Keep the program and your selected Gewu Database in separate folders.

Find the database you are using

Choose File > Open Gewu Database to open the active research folder in File Explorer. This command reveals the current database; it does not create or move one. If startup reports a missing folder or identity mismatch, locate the intended database before changing anything.

Use the installed shortcut

Open Gewu Insight from the Windows Start menu. You can pin that installed shortcut to your taskbar. An old development checkout is not the daily application. Upgrading the program retains the existing database selection.

Normal startup

Open Gewu Insight from the Start menu and wait for the startup screen to finish. Use one window for a workspace; its lock prevents a second desktop process from writing to the same Library. If the selected database is missing, startup stops instead of silently creating an empty replacement.

The installed application includes its runtime dependencies. Keep the selected Library available. If startup fails after an interrupted installation, close the application and rerun its versioned Setup.exe.

Missing, read-only, identity-mismatched or newer-schema databases stop startup with an explanation. Locate the correct database or use the required newer App; do not delete the database to clear an error. When closing, Gewu waits for active requests and database work before releasing its locks.

Startup is not a Library cleanup

Ordinary startup does not reorganize the whole Library, merge historical duplicate files, or make a new full database backup. A pre-schema SQLite snapshot is created only when a schema upgrade is needed; it does not include the research files. Managed layout and duplicate protections apply when you import or change the affected paper and files. Keep your own regular Back Up and Upgrade.

If a file move was interrupted before its database and disk changes finished together, startup recovers only the recorded unfinished operation before background workers start. A launch with no unfinished move goes directly to normal preparation. An ambiguous conflict is reported and preserved for repair rather than overwriting a destination or triggering a full-library sweep.

Automatic local-server recovery

The Windows shell retries an unexpectedly stopped service within a bounded restart budget. Workspace-renderer recovery is also bounded. Repeated failures show a recovery message instead of restarting indefinitely.

The separate Browser process can keep tabs and unsent website forms during service recovery while it stays alive. This does not guarantee recovery after an operating-system crash or App exit. Unsaved research-form edits can be lost when the workspace reloads.

When automatic updates run

Automatic monitoring runs inside the local UI service with startup delays, periodic checks and saved completion/retry state. Keep Windows awake and Gewu Insight running. Closing the standalone window stops its service unless a connected Gewu tab in Zotero still needs it. A late launch checks due work; it does not guarantee a run at the exact scheduled minute.

MonitorCurrent automatic schedule
Journal MonitorDaily work becomes due from 09:00 in the computer's local time zone; stored completion and pending retry state determine what still needs work.
Subject MonitorDaily work becomes due from 09:00 local time; incomplete sources have their own bounded retry state.
Author MonitorChecks due authors from 10:00 local time; already checked authors are not blindly fetched again on every scheduler tick. Failed transport checks use a separate paced retry queue, including before 10:00. Unrecognized Scholar pages use an hourly delay and a daily failure cap; access cooldowns still apply. Opening an author does not force a full profile fetch each time.
arXivUses its separate announcement-ready schedule and buffer, not the journal's 09:00 rule. Read the displayed update/countdown state.

These are local scheduler rules, not guarantees of remote source completion or a hosted monitoring service. Manual Refresh remains available for the selected scope; repeated broad refreshes can worsen a source's rate limit.

If the app cannot start

  1. Close the existing Gewu Insight window normally before reopening the selected database. If startup still fails, inspect %LOCALAPPDATA%/Gewu Insight/Databases/<identity>/Logs/windows-launcher.log; do not remove the database or start an older incompatible App.
  2. For startup errors, inspect %LOCALAPPDATA%/Gewu Insight/Databases/<identity>/Logs/windows-launcher.log and windows-service.log. Keep credentials out of any report you share.
  3. Allow the first startup to finish. After an upgrade, wait through the migration window before treating the preparation panel as a failure.
  4. Start the app again once if recovery does not complete. Avoid opening several copies while the first is still preparing.
  5. Preserve the database. Do not delete SQLite as a startup fix.

Clear a stale interface

Choose Settings > Clear Monitor Cache if a monitor still shows stale downloaded images or rendered web assets after an app update. This clears disposable monitor presentation cache, not the SQLite database, saved paper records, or managed PDFs.

This is not Browser's Clear History command and does not clear Browser sign-in cookies or external browser data. Use Browser > History > Clear History for visit records only.

Choose a comfortable text size

Choose Settings > Font Size, then select Compact, Standard, Large, Larger, or Extra Large. The workspace previews the choice immediately while keeping panel dimensions, icons, and window controls unchanged.

Cancel, the Escape key, or clicking outside the sheet restores the previously saved size. Restore Default previews Standard and still requires Save. Choose Save to keep the preference in the local SQLite settings. New app sessions apply the saved size automatically.

Troubleshoot Common Problems

Start with the visible status and the selected work. Avoid broad repair actions until you know whether the problem is network, metadata, database state, or a local path.

An upgrade appears to open a different or empty Library

Use File > Open Gewu Database to check the selected folder. Do not import again or recreate records before confirming that it is your intended database. Preserve both locations if they differ. The default program folder and the research data folder are separate.

The database cannot be opened

For a missing folder, reconnect its disk or locate the existing workspace. For a newer schema, use a compatible newer App. For a database identity mismatch, check that the folder is the intended one rather than replacing the saved identity manually. For an already-open database or busy port, quit the other Gewu process normally. Do not remove a lock file, reset the database or terminate unrelated processes as a shortcut. See Startup for logs.

A PDF cannot be found after a move

  1. Reselect the paper and try Show in File Explorer.
  2. If the move happened in Gewu Insight, close and reopen the item to refresh the view.
  3. If the file was moved manually in File Explorer, return it if possible, then organize it through the app.
  4. Check Recycle before importing another copy.

Paper Files shows Missing File

This label is a path-state warning, not a failed metadata lookup: SQLite still knows the resource, but the recorded file path does not currently exist. Check Show in File Explorer, the corresponding data/Associated Files bundle, and Recycle. If the file was moved outside Gewu Insight, restore it before reorganizing it through the app. Do not delete the row merely because its filename resembles the default PDF; explicitly typed attachments and the default resource remain visible for recovery.

Preview is slow on the first open

A large or previously unseen PDF may need an initial structural read and thumbnail render. The main document should appear before the full thumbnail strip. Leave the preview open briefly instead of pressing Space repeatedly; later opens can reuse page information and cached thumbnails. If the viewer never produces a page, use Open in Default App to check whether the file itself is valid.

Markdown stays on Loading Markdown

The note is read and formatted locally. Unchanged notes may reopen from a validated memory cache; first opens and changed files need a fresh render. A stalled preview shows an error after about 15 seconds. Close and reopen it to retry, or open the file directly in its normal application. Very large notes show a bounded, marked preview. No metadata refresh, DOI lookup or reimport is needed just to preview Markdown.

Markdown begins with unexpected metadata

Collapse Source record and Properties to read the body. If a header is malformed, the reader may show its escaped source instead of properties. The preview does not rewrite the original note. Wide tables and code blocks have their own horizontal scrolling.

PDF switching flashes in built-in Preview

Switching files can briefly expose loading while a new document is prepared. Let it finish or use Open in Default App to read the file separately. Windows has no macOS system Quick Look mode; Preview Settings cannot switch to it.

The wrong file is the default

  1. Open Paper Files and verify every file type.
  2. Correct a mislabeled Corrected published version, Published version, Accepted manuscript, or Preprint; expand the size footer to set annotation separately.
  3. Choose Set as Default for the desired valid file, or choose Use Automatic Selection to resume automatic selection.

A duplicate appears after download

Compare file size and classification. New downloads use exact SHA-256 and PDF content fingerprints. A copy with annotations may be retained intentionally. Exact byte duplicates are reused, while clean and annotated peers can both remain. Keep the intended default before deleting any redundant non-default row.

A corrected DOI still shows old metadata

Press Return in the DOI field and wait for Identifier updated. Then choose Refresh Info. Hover over the button to check whether the exact corrected identifier was found or a service is waiting to retry. Saving an identifier and retrieving its bibliography are separate steps. Do not erase files or create another paper merely to bypass a metadata conflict; see Edit DOI and arXiv Identifiers.

Refresh complete reports partial results

Green Refresh complete means the operation ended. Successful source updates are retained even if another source was unavailable. The hover report and batch task window retain the detailed outcomes and cooldowns. Repeating a broad task immediately is usually unnecessary.

A normal Library item points into Recycle

With an active Library, Space or My Publications placement, app-managed operations keep or return its original to normal storage. A recycled occurrence may instead be a shortcut to that retained original. For a historical discrepancy, inspect the selected Key, file path and surviving locations before taking action. Do not empty Recycle or manually delete the path as a diagnostic shortcut.

Search misses the phrase you expected

Try a title fragment, surname or exact identifier. Library supports spelling tolerance and word variants, but does not automatically translate languages or invent synonyms. It searches saved metadata and names, not a semantic index of PDF content. Clear the search to return to normal folder browsing.

A monitor shows no papers

Read the source status. An empty successful source is not the same as a failed fetch. In Subject Monitor, allow scheduled source-level retries to finish, or use the selected subject's refresh command when a manual retry is needed. In Journal Monitor, confirm the date and filters. If a VPN is involved, test a direct connection without repeatedly refreshing.

Author Monitor shows a red Scholar pause

Check the stated retry time and full status message. A saved access cooldown survives restart and network changes; it is separate from a temporary connection failure or the all-author metadata counter. See Author Monitor status and recovery. Repeated refreshes do not remove a cooldown. A completed refresh that says papers need identity review instead concerns those records’ identifiers or metadata, not the network.

A journal count and the visible cards disagree

This is usually expected when Field Filter is active. Journal counts describe all stored papers for the selected journal and day; field choices narrow the visible cards. Clear or broaden the field selection before diagnosing a missing fetch.

A journal disappeared from the configured list

Open Journal Settings and inspect the disabled history before editing configuration files. Removing a journal disables its subscription but preserves previously collected papers and history. Add it again to restore monitoring. Because the subscription list is SQLite state, replacing source files should not be used as a journal-list repair.

LaTeX remains visible as source text

On a cold launch, allow the math renderer a moment to become ready. The active day should re-render automatically. If raw $...$ text remains, check network availability for the renderer, then reload the same view once; switching calendar dates should not be required.

Folder Loader looks incomplete

Open the live or previous Loader log and the result guide. Confirm the metadata mode, source path, and any stop action. Re-running the same source should reuse existing files rather than overwrite the primary PDF.

A default file cannot be deleted

The Default is kept as the protected main file, including for non-PDFs. Choose another eligible resource with Set as Default before removing the old main file from Paper Files. The old resource remains in Associated Files until you explicitly remove it. To remove the paper itself, use the normal Library reference/Recycle workflow, which preserves shared references. Do not bypass a main-file warning in File Explorer. An Invalid file remains an audit record and is never eligible to become Default.

Change where website links open

Open Settings > Website Links and save System Default Browser to use the browser selected in Windows. The default, Gewu Insight Browser, opens a new built-in webpage tab or reuses its unused first tab. This covers website actions in all five research views, including publisher arrows, DOI/arXiv links, scholarly profiles, citation-source links, and links inside Note. Existing web pages stay open. Local PDF, Preview, File Explorer, download, and file-import actions are unchanged.

Home works offline but a website will not load

Home displays local Favorites without a Google request. Missing site icons fall back to initials; they do not prevent opening Home. Search results and account actions require a connection. Read the load error, check the destination and Clash route, and try Reload once. A website may reject embedded browsers or have its own session policy; an unsupported-browser banner alone does not prove why a sign-in ended. Open in Default Browser is a manual compatibility fallback, with a separate sign-in session.

A publisher stays on security verification

An embedded Browser can still be rejected by a publisher's verification. Reload once; if it repeats, use Open in Default Browser and complete the site's normal access steps yourself. The external browser has a separate session. Do not repeatedly retry or bypass the challenge.

Website sign-in is unavailable

Apple Passwords and the macOS AutoFill trigger are not part of Windows Preview. Complete sign-in yourself in Browser. If a website rejects the embedded browser, use Open in Default Browser; its sign-in session is separate. Do not copy cookies or credentials into the research interface.

Website sign-in differs between interfaces

The Windows App and Zotero use separate website sessions. Sign in normally in the interface you are using. Neither Windows interface needs the Mac Keychain or the project's Mac update-signing private key.

Science displays a PDF but Save shows Article only

Wait for the Science ePDF reader to finish loading, then reopen Save to Gewu > Details and check the title, DOI and PDF status. Choose Use Loaded PDF if offered. A changed document, incomplete transfer or file above 128 MB can prevent the original from being read. Choose a saved local PDF, or save the article alone and attach its PDF later under the same Gewu Key. See Save a Science ePDF; a failed fresh download does not prove that the loaded copy is unusable.

The in-app guide and Print Guide look like different editions

The searchable guide is served by the running Gewu backend; Print Guide opens the fixed-layout PDF packaged in the App. A source-backed backend reads its configured checkout, while a standalone backend uses its packaged source. If one guide is older, the running code and bundled resources are out of sync. Follow Back Up and Upgrade to install a complete matching version. For a source build, regenerate the PDF and package it before reopening the App. Clearing Monitor Cache does not replace a bundled guide.

A long task keeps returning as Continue

That task was paused or interrupted, so its remaining queue is saved. Choose the footer's Details, or open Loader > Refresh All Metadata and select the task. Choose Stop to end it permanently. Completed work remains. Closing the window merely hides it; Pause deliberately keeps it resumable.

Two Paper Files cards seem to be the same file

Two folders showing the same Gewu Key normally share a single Paper Files bundle. Within that bundle, different edited PDFs can have similar names. Use Show in File Explorer and inspect each resource before deleting anything. Exact unchanged reimports are reused, but changing a DOI, restarting, or clearing Monitor Cache is not a historical duplicate-repair command. If two cards reveal the same physical file, report the Gewu Key and the steps that produced it through Help > Contact Us.

Contact support

Help > Contact Us opens info@gewu-insight.com in the Windows default email application. If none is configured, use your preferred mail service. Include the installed version, operation and error; omit passwords and tokens. Review and send the message yourself.

Download reports supplements but no main PDF

This reports two separate outcomes: some supplementary PDFs were saved, but the main article did not arrive as a readable PDF. MP4, ZIP, spreadsheets and other non-PDF supplements are skipped by automatic PDF collection. They do not turn a successful main-PDF download into a failure. Check access to the actual main PDF in Gewu Browser, then retry Download or use Save to Gewu with an already-loaded original. See Choose the right save action.

A journal's unread dot returns after changing fields

This is expected when the newly visible field contains unread papers. A tab counts only its currently visible unread results. Click or use Up/Down on each paper you read; opening the tab or changing fields does not acknowledge the whole list. Read history is not reset by the updated rule.

A correction or retraction is missing

For a saved original, check its DOI and request Refresh Info; inspect the source outcomes and Paper Files. In Journal Monitor, choose the notice's publication date and check the Journal and Field filters before expanding Publication updates. Saved papers do not receive a continuous retraction watch. Missing provider relations, delayed indexing or unavailable sources can leave a notice undiscovered. Verify the publisher record when necessary; do not create a duplicate article simply to store its notice.

A mathematical note shows formula source

Built-in Markdown math renders locally. Check paired formula delimiters and keep formulas outside code blocks. Unsupported or oversized expressions remain readable as source. This does not require refreshing the paper's metadata or downloading its PDF again.

Reference

Storage Reference

The relative paths below are inside your selected Gewu Database, not inside the App or source checkout. Find the active folder through Gewu Insight > Database Location…. The remaining machine locations are listed separately for backup and diagnosis.

  • data/paper_monitor.sqliteAuthoritative database for papers, identities, relationships, settings, operational state, Browser bookmarks, and visit history. May contain saved metadata API keys; treat backups as private.
  • data/LibraryVisible main Library root, canonical main files and secondary Windows .lnk shortcuts.
  • data/SpacesIndependent Space roots.
  • data/My PublicationsManaged local files for My Publications.
  • data/Associated FilesMirrored bundles for versions, supplements, and attachments.
  • data/pdfsLegacy managed PDF location retained for compatibility where needed.
  • reportsGenerated daily reports, exports and legacy analysis artifacts. New AI analyses saved to Paper Files belong to the paper's managed associated bundle.
  • configWorkspace configuration retained with the research data. Saved per-user settings and authoritative journal subscriptions also live in SQLite.
  • backupsPre-schema SQLite snapshots, migration reports and retained recovery material when present. Backups in this folder are on the same disk and do not replace a separate full backup.

Preview page thumbnails use a separate, automatically trimmed temporary cache. It is rebuildable preview data, not part of the Library, Associated Files, or the SQLite record, so it does not belong in a research backup.

App and machine locations

  • %LOCALAPPDATA%/Programs/Gewu Insight: installed program and bundled resources.
  • %USERPROFILE%/.gewu-insight/database-location.ini: selected database folder and identity; not the database itself.
  • %LOCALAPPDATA%/Gewu Insight/Databases/<identity>/Logs: startup and background-service diagnostics.
  • %LOCALAPPDATA%/Gewu Insight/Databases/<identity>/Cache: rebuildable cache; not research originals.
  • %LOCALAPPDATA%/Gewu Insight/Databases/<identity>/Browser: separate website profile.
  • %LOCALAPPDATA%/Gewu Insight/Updates: downloaded program updates and per-computer check preferences.

Associated Files layout

An associated bundle follows the managed scope and path, then a work-specific bundle. Its children separate Versions, Supplements, and Files. The exact physical name can change as the paper moves; the Gewu Key remains stable.

Database and exports

SQLite is the only source of truth. JSON, HTML, Markdown, Word, LaTeX, and PDF outputs are exports, diagnostics, or reading artifacts. Editing one of them does not edit the Library record.

ImportantDo not delete, rebuild, or “clean” the database because a generated JSON file looks stale. Diagnose the selected record and local path first.
